News.title: Woman found dead on major UK motorway after driver ‘spotted body’ on hard shoulder sparking 5-hour closure
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

GRIM END Woman found dead on major UK motorway after driver ‘spotted body’ on hard shoulder sparking 5-hour closure

A WOMAN has tragically been found dead on a major motorway – after drivers reported seeing a body on the hard shoulder.

The M55 was closed for five hours after the grim discovery near Preston, Lancashire, yesterday evening.

Officers were scrambled to the busy stretch following multiple reports from concerned motorists at around 10.20pm.

The tragic discovery was then made between Junction 1, for Broughton Roundabout, and Junction 2, for Becconsall Interchange.





An investigation into the woman’s death has since been launched, Lancashire Police confirmed.

The force said: “We were called at 10.20pm yesterday (Aug 10th) to a report of a concern for welfare of a woman.

“Ten minutes later at 10.30pm we received another call after a motorist driving towards Blackpool on the M55 reported seeing what they believed was a body on the hard shoulder of the motorway.

“Officers attended the scene, between junctions 1 and 2 near to the Broughton interchange, where very sadly we can confirm they found the body of a woman.



“Enquiries are ongoing into the circumstances.

“The motorway was closed for around five hours.”

News.title: ‘National disaster’ in Colombia after 7.4-magnitude earthquake kills more than 160 & topples buildings as LOOTING erupts
News.content:
A NATIONAL disaster has been declared in Colombia after a mega quake killed more than 160 people.

Hundreds of buildings collapsed as the South American country was hit by a huge 7.4-magnitude earthquake on Monday morning – one of its largest in years.



So far, 164 people have been confirmed dead and nearly 500 left injured, officials said.

The death toll is likely to rise, with many feared trapped under collapsed buildings.





By Monday evening, more than 2,700 people had been reported missing as desperate families posted information about missing loved ones online.

Striking at a depth of 64 miles in Chocó province, the quake was felt across a huge area – stretching for hundreds of miles across western Colombia, as far as Venezuela’s capital, Caracas, 750 miles away, and in Ecuador and Panama.

In Chocó – where much of the area is only accessible by boat, through the jungle or by plane – 13 people have died.

Another 66 have been reported dead in Periera – where the mayor broke down in tears as he told reporters that numbers were expected to rise.



Three people died at the Pereira airport terminal, according to the mayor, and pictures showed rescuers helping passengers trapped on the city’s 11,000ft-long gondola lift.

In ​Cali, Colombia’s third biggest city and home to about 2.2 million people, at least 85 people were killed.



At least 20 buildings collapsed in the city or were significantly damaged, including the paediatric wing of the de Valle University Hospital.

Rescue workers were seen helping a woman and a newborn baby from a fourth-floor window after the quake.

Colombia’s president Abelardo de la Espriella said 1,000 members of the security forces have been deployed to Cali following reports of looting.

City mayor Alejandro Eder announced an overnight curfew on Monday to “preserve security in the city”.



In Manizales, the heart of Colombia’s coffee-growing region, at least five people were killed and 20 houses were destroyed.

One of the towers of the city’s 20th-century cathedral collapsed in front of shocked crowds.

In Quibdó, one of the first deaths confirmed was Jairson Leonel Valencia, the six-year-old son of a local mayor, The Times reports.

President de la Espriella said he had mobilised the entire military as well as police to respond to the quake – deploying engineers, rescue workers and search dogs.



The country’s Aviation Authority reported widespread damage at airports in Pereira, Manizales, Quibdo, Armenia, Cartago and Buenaventura – with all flights grounded.

Across the country, around 1,600 buildings were damaged or collapsed.



Soldiers, rescuers and families picked through the rubble, removing large pieces of concrete by hand down lines of volunteers.

US secretary of state Marco Rubio said America “stands ready to support” the country.

The US Department of State described the disaster as “devastating” and pledged £11.5million to help provide emergency shelter and supplies.

The EU is also providing funding and supporting rescue operations, EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said.

One of Columbia’s most famous stars Shakira offered her condolences after the earthquake struck her homeland.



The epicenter of the quake was in San Jose Del Palmar – located some 250 miles west of Bogota, the US Geological Survey reported.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The quake follows two back-to-back 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude earthquakes in Venezuela in late June.

Those earthquakes destroyed hundreds of buildings and killed more than 5,000 people.

News.title: PC Andrew Harper’s killers WILL be kept in prison – as Angela Rayner confirms No10 U-turn after ‘solution identified’
News.content:
PC ANDREW Harper’s killers will be kept in prison, Angela Rayner has confirmed, as No10 make another U-turn after weeks of back and forth.

The government previously claimed it would reportedly face legal challenges if it tried to block the release of Albert Bowers and Jessie Cole halfway through their 13-year jail terms.



But a government spokesperson said last night that the new PM has been pushing to exempt the duo from the early release scheme.

Andy Burnham reportedly asked Justice Secretary Alex Norris to find a way to keep the pair locked up.



He is understood to be opposed to the early release of the thugs himself with a petition launched to stop the duo from being released early now reaching over 900,000 signatures.

Bowers and Cole could be let out in January under Labour plans to release up to 5,000 prisoners over ten months from October if they are not exempted from the scheme.



Andy Burnham urged his Justice Secretary to “work through further options” to stop their release after two previous plans were shot down with the threat of legal challenges.

And, today Angela Rayner said the Justice Secretary would set out the government’s plan to exempt Cole and Bowers from early release when Parliament returns in September.

Speaking to LBC, Ms Rayner said: “The Prime Minister is really clear, the Justice Secretary will come to Parliament in September to lay out our plans on how we keep the most serious criminals in jail.”

Asked if that would include killers of police officers Ms Rayner replied: “Yes.”

Ms Rayner continued: “The Prime Minister is really clear that these people that have created the most abhorrent crimes should not be released early and that he wants to set out in September with the Justice Secretary how we can resolve this issue.”



This morning, a communities minister doubled down on the promise, telling Times Radio a way to stop PC Andrew Harper’s killers being released early from prison had been “identified.”

Sally Jameson said the Prime Minister found a solution to the problem with details of the plan to be announced next month.

She told Times Radio: “He’s looking for solutions, and a solution’s been identified.

“I mean, it is tricky because of how sentencing works and the sentence that was handed down to those particular offenders, and we’ve got to find a way that makes sure we stop those getting out whilst also recognising that in relation to other offenders.”

Alex Norris is now expected to set out the steps the government will take to exempt the duo from the early release scheme when Parliament returns in September.



It remains unclear how the Government will prevent Cole and Bowers’ release, with two proposals already being rejected.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham today said: “I understand the depth of public concern about the potential early release of those involved with the killing of PC Andrew Harper – and I share it.

“I fully appreciate the anguish of Andrew’s family and, more broadly, of all those victims and their families who may see those who caused them such harm not serve their full sentence.



“It is incumbent on me as Prime Minister to do everything within my power to minimise that possibility. And I am determined to do so.

“I have spent recent days considering in depth all of the issues involved and the range of advice I have received. I have been pushing for further progress. I have not accepted that it is impossible to do more.

“As a result, I have asked the Justice Secretary to fast-track the development of a plan for presentation to Parliament early next month to create more headroom within the prison system.”

The PM added that he is “increasingly confident” that work to increase space in the prison system “will allow us to reduce the number of people released early and, in the case of the most serious offenders like those convicted of the killing of Pc (Andrew) Harper, prevent their early release altogether.”

It comes amid increasing pressure from PC Harper’s family and the police not to allow the two thugs to be freed.



PC Harper’s family have previously expressed anger and disappointment at the decision not to exempt Cole and Bowers from early release.

And, the boss of his former force said he was considering joining a potential legal challenge over the Government plans.

This morning PC Harper’s mum appeared on Good Morning Britain to say she had been “turned inside out” by the government’s flip-flopping on the issue.

Debbie Adlam explained that she received a call last night to tell her the Prime Minister was “doing everything he can” to keep Bowers and Cole locked up.

She told the programme, however: “Until it happens, here we sit. We’ve been down this road now for a few weeks.



“This is week three of waiting to see what is happening and I don’t know how to feel really, Andrew’s family are just going through the ringer here.

“We’re not asking for anything more than they were sentenced which wasn’t exactly a tight sentence.

“I’m not asking for more to be added on or a special case for Andrew, but the emergency service workers as a whole need better protection.”

She went on to brand the early release scheme a “lottery” saying it was “ridiculous.”

Debbie continued: “We deserve so much better than this, this is our society and I just feel like we are going to the gutter.”



PC Harper’s furious widow Lissie Harper, 35, previously said it was “disgusting” that her late husband’s killers could get out early.

She said: “What abhorrent message does this send?

“How dare ministers say the killing of a police officer isn’t enough of a ‘sickening crime’ that deserves the stiffest of punishments.

“Andrew’s killers have shown no remorse. To release them early from their already pitiful sentences is an affront to justice.

“The Government and justice system have not just let me down, they have added insult to injury.



“This is an utter betrayal, one I will not be able to forgive or forget.”

Yesterday it was revealed that the government had already had two plans to keep Bowers and Cole behind bars shot down.

Andy Burnham’s government has reportedly already ruled out exempting the killers of emergency workers from early release.

The planned exemption to the scheme that would have kept them locked up is understood to have been described as a “complete non-starter.”

It was decided that the planned change would be subject to a legal challenge.



And, because there is no specific offence of manslaughter of an emergency worker the case would be tough to win for the government.

But is understood that the PM has been holding calls while on holiday over the past week to discuss how to resolve the issue, and is said to be pushing for solutions.

Yesterday, Mr Burnham’s official spokesman said manslaughter of an emergency worker was “not a standalone offence” and it was “not possible to simply exclude one or two offenders” within the wider category of manslaughter.

In another potential route to block the release of PC Harper’s killers, former detective superintendent at Thames Valley police, Stuart Blaik, suggested those more culpable under manslaughter laws be barred from the scheme.

Cases of manslaughter are categorised in three culpability ratings, A, B and C.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

In response to the fury around the potential release of Bowers and Cole, Blaik suggested offenders in the two most severe categories of manslaughter be prevented from an early release.

But officials shot down this plan too, saying judges did not always include culpability ratings in their sentences – making it hard to determine who would be eligible for Labour’s early release scheme.

News.title: Southwest passenger, 22, suddenly becomes unresponsive & dies mid-air on LA flight despite crew attempts to save him
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

FLIGHT TRAGEDY Southwest passenger, 22, suddenly becomes unresponsive & dies mid-air on LA flight despite crew attempts to save him

A SOUTHWEST Airlines passenger has died after “suddenly” becoming unresponsive mid-air while flying to Los Angeles.

Crew and fellow travellers desperately performed multiple rounds of CPR on Rain McMillan Walmsey after he suffered a medical episode aboard.



Flight 958 was travelling from Dallas to Los Angeles when the 22-year-old suddenly stopped responding, according to reports.

Those on board rushed to try to save the young passenger as the aircraft continued towards Southern California.



Emergency crews were waiting on the ground when the Southwest jet touched down at Los Angeles International Airport.

Paramedics immediately attempted to resuscitate Walmsey but were unable to revive him.

Firefighters pronounced him dead at the scene.

But exactly what caused the medical emergency remains a mystery.

His cause of death has been deferred and the case remains open while officials investigate the circumstances surrounding the tragedy.

Authorities have not revealed what symptoms Walmsey experienced before becoming unresponsive.



It is also unclear whether he had any underlying medical conditions before boarding the flight.

Southwest Airlines previously confirmed there had been a “medical incident involving a customer” aboard Flight 958.

The airline did not provide further details about the passenger or what happened on board.

The circumstances surrounding Walmsey’s death remain under investigation.

News.title: Inside rise of Gen Z mafia paying boys £160 to kill in tourist spots… with ‘no rules’ on bloodshed & chilling new tactic
News.content:
FROM gunning down civilians in the street to planting car bombs, a deadly new class of teenage gangsters are terrorising Europe, ripping up the traditional mafia ‘rulebook’ to commit acts of unspeakable violence.

Welcome to Daltons Mafia – a brutal syndicate originating in Turkey and ruled by 29-year-old Berat Can Gökdemir – who are now targeting tourist hotspots, including Spain and France.





Armed with AK47s and explosives, the brazen gangsters revel in murder sprees and traffic heroin and cocaine – all while flaunting their sick exploits across TikTok and Instagram.

Impoverished teen drug mules and hitmen have no fear of the police – and regard prison time as a glorious networking opportunity.

“They don’t use any rules,” mafia investigator Osman Çaklı told The Sun, adding that “their main aim is to destroy everything”.

The Daltons – named after a bumbling gang of comic book villains – began as a collection of child gangs committing petty theft in the suburbs of Istanbul, Turkey, according to reports.

But in the last two years, the Gen Z mafia have exploded in the German capital of Berlin and are infiltrating southern France, Italy and Spain.

Chilling videos posted online show attacks on shop owners or wads of cash from drug deals – with some clips even filmed inside prison cells.

“Thousands of videos [are] filmed from inside cells”, sociologist Marcello Ravveduto told The Sun, adding that inmates dance to music and “show off life behind bars as if it were a reality show”.

Online mafia clips overlap with the manosphere because they “share a dominant masculinity”, explained Ravveduto.





“In both we find the cult of virility, money as the measure of worth, redemption through force, a hierarchy that rewards whoever dominates.”

Germany has rarely been under the boot of mafiosos – unlike their neighbours in Italy and Eastern Europe.

But Berlin is now facing “an unprecedented surge in lawlessness” said a new report from the Global Initiative against Transnational Crime.

Gun crime has spiked – doubling from 2024 to 2025 – and since January there have been nine shootings on people or property.

New Gen Z mobsters are more violent than traditional mafias, according to Turkish journalist and investigator Osman Çaklı.

“Normally underground life has its own rules, the traditional mafia maybe kidnaps the [shop] owner, hits them, maybe shoots them in the foot”, he said.

“But when it comes to them [the Gen Z mafia] they don’t use any rules.

“Let’s say it’s a bar or a pub – they walk in and they can kill everyone in the pub. Their main aim is to destroy everything.”



Where once the mafia used single-shot firearms, the Daltons “use AK47s and explosives”.

More than 5,000 kids dealing drugs for different Gen Z mafias have been locked up in Turkish prisons in the last three to four years, said Osman.

Many are seduced into the mafia online – and transformed into disposable gunmen.

“There is no training”, said Osman, adding: “They just find one person online and put money in his pocket and send them to kill their target.”

Teen mobsters are killing for a pittance – paid just £160 (10,000 Turkish liras) for murder, rising to £1,600 (100,000 Turkish liras) for high profile assassinations.

Chillingly, Osman added that recruits “are learning by doing”.

Describing their crimes, he said: “They go to one store and they say ‘if you want to continue your business you must pay out.’ If shop owners refuse, they start to show unseen violence against them.

“It is something new in Turkish mafia-style”, he added.



Some members are just 15 years old, with many lured in by the promise of wealth and luxury plastered across the digital mafiosphere.

Disturbing videos show violent extortions – or boast luxury cars and designer watches over a backing track of melodic trap music.

Flagrant displays of criminality across TikTok and Instagram have outraged older mafia bosses – who regard the videos as reckless and stupid.

Osman explained that older mafioso committed their crimes “in a very hidden way and nobody used to know what was going on”.

Gen Z mafia on the other hand “intentionally show everything that is going on – they put videos on social media”.

Ravveduto said “the tension is real” between old-school mafia bosses and the younger mafiosos.

He said: “The old guard built its power on the myth of silence.

“A boss who shows himself is a boss who exposes himself, and whoever exposes himself becomes fragile in front of investigators and rivals. From that point of view, the showing-off on TikTok looks like recklessness, almost vulgarity.”



Osman points out that the Daltons Mafia is built up of children who grew up surrounded by poverty and crime – and have no fear of being arrested.

He said: “For normal people like us it is, of course, frightening to be caught by police, but for them its a risk worth taking.

“They go to prison and gain new networks in the prison – the benefit is more than the harms.”

Ravveduto agreed, adding “prison is the university of the underworld” and considered a rite of passage for child delinquents.

Thousands of child criminals have been arrested in Turkey after trafficking Class A drugs and shooting dead shopkeepers who fail to do their bidding.

Police in Germany have also been scrambling to crack down on the rise in shootings, extortion and violence – seen especially in Berlin but also across Stuttgart, Frankfurt, Cologne and Hamburg.

In November 2025, the Berlin police launched a new Iron Taskforce in February this year they added another called “Telum” – meaning weapons – to battle the spike in gun trafficking.

German investigators trying to crack down on the lawless teens have found themselves on disturbing “death lists” with bounties placed on their heads, reported newspaper Bild.



Cops have so far failed to arrest any members of the Daltons Mafia, according to one Berlin-based member who spoke to Osman.

Osman trawled through court documents from June and confirmed that the names of those arrested were not those of the Gen Z mafia.

The Berlin police force declined to comment.

Turkey has spawned three main Gen Z mafia syndicates – of which the biggest are The Daltons.

The other two are the Casper Mafia – also named after a cartoon character – and the Çirkinler which translates to “The Uglies”.

The three gangs engage in bitter turf wars on the streets of Germany with The Uglies and the Caspers both gunning at rivals The Daltons.

But all three are ruthlessly expanding their territory with The Daltons snaking into Marseille, southern France.

The Casper Mafia and the The Uglies meanwhile are establishing a presence in Spain, Italy and Georgia.



But German police are cracking down on the lawlessness.

One suspected thug, 21, who punched a businessman in the face alongside three masked accomplices, was charged in June.

And Berlin’s Iron Taskforce is currently handling 126 cases involving gun trafficking and violent extortion, according to German newspaper Tages Spiegel – though it is unclear whether suspects are members of The Daltons.

News.title: Man ‘sexually assaults’ girl, 16, at train station before passengers confront him and he flees – as cops release CCTV
News.content:
'ASSAULT' PROBE Man ‘sexually assaults’ girl, 16, at train station before passengers confront him and he flees – as cops release CCTV

A 16-YEAR-OLD girl has allegedly been seriously sexually assaulted at a train station, as police release CCTV.

The reported incident happened at around 10.30pm at White Hart Lane station in Tottenham, North London.

A man is alleged to have approached the teen and sexually assaulted her before being confronted by passengers and fleeing onto a train.

Police have now released CCTV of a man they believe may have information that could assist their inquiry.





British Transport Police detectives are asking anyone with any information that may assist them to come forward.

The force said: “Detectives would like to speak to the man pictured, as they believe he may have information that could assist their ongoing investigation.

“Anyone who recognises him is asked to text BTP on 61016 or call 0800 40 50 40, quoting reference 875 of 7 July.

“Information can be given anonymously to Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.”

News.title: Trump ‘smuggled off Air Force One in catering cart to board secret flight’ away from Nato summit amid Iran threat
News.content:
DON A MISSION Trump ‘smuggled off Air Force One in catering cart to board secret flight’ away from Nato summit amid Iran threat

DONALD Trump was reportedly smuggled off Air Force One in a catering truck last month in an elaborate ruse after a threat from Iran.

The US president was secretly swapped onto a different plane as he left a Nato summit in Turkey on July 8, according to the Washington Post.



Journalists and even White House staff were tricked by the plot, believing they were on the same plane as the president as it left Ankara.

Trump had publicly boarded Air Force One – but it was a decoy.



He was then smuggled off the plane into a catering truck by a door on the other side of the plane.

It had reportedly been raised right to the plane door so the president couldn’t be seen at all as he slipped out.

Trump was accompanied by aides as he duped onlookers.

The US president was then driven in the truck and snuck onto a smaller military plane, Air Force C-32A, according to reports.



War Secretary Pete Hegseth shared the secret flight with Trump.

A US official told the Post he boarded from the outside, “to make the flight appear typical”.

Both planes were painted with blue and white, and emblazoned with the presidential seal.



But the public had been told that Trump would fly on the older plane which he boarded in plain view before sneaking off.

The US president had announced he would travel on the “former Air Force One” to leave Turkey, instead of the plane he had arrived on, a newer jumbo jet gifted to him by Qatar.

He had started using the newer Boeing 747-8 just days earlier.

The cunning plot to use Air Force One as a decoy flight – carrying the media and some White House staffers – came after a night of heavy US strikes on Iran.

The “deception operation” was triggered by a credible threat to Trump from Iran, a US official said.



Questions had been raised about the security of the Qatari jet as Iran ramped up threats on the president’s life.

Both flights landed at RAF Mildenhall and Trump appeared before TV cameras and descended the decoy plane’s stairs.

It is not clear how he snuck back onto the former Air Force One.

White House communications director Steven Cheung said: “The new Air Force One is a state-of-the-art aircraft that has been fitted with high-level security protocols that ensure the safety of the President and his staff.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“As the President has said recently, there are many enemies of America who have their sights on him, and we use every tool at our disposal to address those threats.”



The White House did not confirm the secret flight swap.

News.title: Amber heat health alerts in place for almost all of England as next heatwave hits
News.content:
Amber heat health alerts are in force across most of England on Tuesday as temperatures start to climb again at the start of the summer's latest predicted heatwave.

The UK's Health Security Agency (UKHSA) is warning that significant impacts are likely across social and health care, including a rise in deaths.

The amber alerts are in place until Friday evening to cover high and even extreme temperatures expected through this week.

During the peak of the heatwave temperatures across England and Wales will widely be in the low to mid-30s Celsius.

The only region in England without an amber alert is the North East which has been given a less intense yellow alert for the same period.

It comes after drought officials declared 71.3% of England is now in drought.

News.title: Councils to get more powers to stop vape and betting shops, PM announces
News.content:
New vape shops will require planning permission and councils will get more powers to block new betting shops, under government plans aimed at improving high streets.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said town centres had been "hollowed out" by decades of decline and "for many people, the high streets they grew up with have become unrecognisable".

BBC News has exposed organised crime on high streets across the country, revealing shops selling illegal cigarettes and vapes, selling cannabis and cocaine, enabling illegal working and suspected money-laundering.

The Conservatives and Reform said the proposals would lead to "more empty" shops, without tax relief for other small businesses.

Burnham said the measures will give councils more power to control what businesses open in town centres.

The proposals come as the prime minister embarks on a tour of the UK, with Downing Street saying he will be in "listening mode" during his visits as he works on a "10-year plan to bring back hope".

The plans announced by the government include:

Changes to planning law which would mean every new shop selling e-cigarettes, or vapes, would need to apply to their local council for permission to open (England only)

Tightening the definition of a vape shop to prevent businesses avoiding the rules by describing themselves as a general convenience store or retailer (England only)

Scrapping a rule known as "aim to permit", which currently restricts councils' ability to refuse new betting shops and 24-hour slot machine shops (Great Britain-wide)

Requiring planning permission for new adult gaming centres, which offer 24-hour access to gambling machines (England only)

New powers to extend closure orders for mini-marts and vape shops found to be selling illegal tobacco or up to twelve months, something previously proposed by former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer (England and Wales)

The National Crime Agency (NCA) estimates that at least Â£1bn of criminal cash is laundered through high street stores in the UK each year through businesses connected to the sale of fake goods, tax evasion, illegal working and illegal drug supply.

Burnham said "the rise of vape shops, betting shops and rogue operators have replaced the shops, services, and community spaces that people are crying out for".

He added: "That's not on. I said we would improve Britain's high streets, and that's exactly what we are starting to do.

"We're putting communities back in control and giving local people a real say over what opens on their high street."

News.title: Trump says it would be 'terrible mistake' to remove Infantino
News.content:
US President Donald Trump says it would be a "terrible mistake" if under-pressure Fifa president Gianni Infantino was ousted from his position.

Trump's backing followed Uefa, Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) issuing an open letter accusing Infantino of breaking trust "through deception" with his aborted Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal.

FFE would have meant a new company being created to manage commercial and ticketing rights of all Fifa competitions, including World Cups, with 21% sold off to a private investment company.

Trump's comments mark the first time he has come out in defence of Infantino since the FFE plans came to light on 28 July.

"Fifa would be making a terrible mistake if, for any reason, they even considered replacing president Gianni Infantino," Trump wrote on social media.

"He is fantastic, having just presided over the most successful World Cup, by four times, ever presented. If he is gone, it will never be as successful or profitable again."

The 2026 World Cup was co-hosted by the US, Canada and Mexico this summer, with Spain crowned champions after beating Argentina in the final.

When addressing the FFE proposals for the first time on 31 July, Trump said he had not spoken to Infantino about the plans.

Thrive Eternal was expected to lead the proposed investor group for FFE.

Thrive is an American venture capital firm founded by Joshua Kushner - the brother of Trump's son-in-law Jared.

Infantino has a close relationship with Trump and awarded him the inaugural Fifa Peace Prize in December 2025.

News.title: Perseid meteor shower reaches peak: When and where to catch a glimpse
News.content:
The best annual meteor shower has once again returned to our skies, and the Perseids dazzling display is set to peak on Wednesday night.

But skywatchers will be treated to not one, but two, impressive astronomical events within just a few hours of each other.

A deep partial solar eclipse will be also visible in the UK in the early evening before the Sun sets and the stars emerge. While the two events are unrelated, their timing makes for an exceptional night of stargazing.

Astronomer Dr Becky Smethurst said it was "the perfect cosmic coincidence of events".

Here is when to look up and where you will have the best views of the meteor shower.

News.title: Jewish school heads spend more time on security than education, review finds
News.content:
Headteachers of some Jewish schools are spending more of their time dealing with security arrangements than on educational matters, a review into antisemitism in schools and colleges has found.

Sir David Bell, speaking for the first time about his ongoing government-commissioned independent review, told the BBC he had been struck by how many leaders of Jewish faith schools had told him security was their primary concern - and that "sometimes education takes second place to that".

The report, due in the autumn, examines the experiences of Jewish pupils and staff in faith and secular schools and colleges in England.

Sir David said he found that pupils were "subject to regular harassment and abuse".

He said Jewish children and young people "are facing a pressure - and indeed one might say even a crisis - that is not the experience of other communities in this country".

The review is likely to recommend dedicated training for all teachers and improved education about antisemitism for pupils, the BBC has been told.

The BBC has spoken to several headteachers and staff at Jewish schools. All asked not to be named because of concerns over their security and that of their schools.

One headteacher said: "In recent years [security] has become an overwhelming priority and increased a significant amount. There have been weeks where approximately 90% of my time has been spent on security-related matters.

"Security concerns can become one of the many things that headteachers carry with them beyond the school day and, quite literally, can be among the things that keep me awake at night."

News.title: 'I started in my 20s and made £8,000': Why women are often better investors than men
News.content:
It can be "largely attributed to culture", according to Gillian Fleming, co-founder and managing director of UK-based Mint Ventures, a women-led angel investment firm.

"Men historically have been more likely to make family investment decisions, and women have also historically not owned the balance of wealth, but that is changing now," she says.

"Also, money and wealth creation is not a topic that women often discuss, and we would like to change that."

Teleri says she has noticed a shift of late. "Investing is definitely something that women are talking about more, which is always a good thing," she says. "That's the case with my friendship group."

When women do invest in stocks and shares, analysis by Fidelity International found that over three years its female personal investing customers recorded cumulative returns of 50%, compared with 47% for men. The analysis does not identify the reason for the difference, but why may it be the case?

One possible clue to women's slightly higher long-term returns lies in how often they buy and sell their investments, with Barclays data showing that women trade around half as frequently as men.

News.title: England set to eliminate hepatitis C
News.content:
Hepatitis C is spread through contact with blood infected with the virus, such as by sharing needles with someone who has it.

Donor blood is already screened for it.

It is a silent disease, meaning people often have no symptoms until much later.

Untreated, it can cause serious and potentially life-threatening liver damage.

NHS England says that since 2015, more than 100,000 people have been diagnosed and treated for hepatitis C, meaning the country is already meeting that target.

Another goal - a 65% reduction in hepatitis C-related mortality compared with 2015 levels - has yet to be met, but might be before the 2030 target date.

Around 50,200 adults are living with hepatitis C, figures for England in 2024 suggest.

Estimates indicate 84.6% of those living with hepatitis C have been diagnosed - just short of the 90% target.

The Hepatitis C Trust says England is "on the cusp" of one of the most significant public health achievements in our country's history.

Prof Frankie Swords, NHS national medical director, added: "England is now leading the world in the mission to eliminate this disease and on course to beat the WHO's 2030 target, but we are determined to keep up the momentum and finish the job.

"We are committed to finding and treating everyone who needs support and would urge those at greater risk to come forward by ordering a free and confidential home-testing kit online."

Adults born in Ukraine, Romania, Estonia, Latvia, Poland, Albania, Lithuania, Bulgaria, Czechia or Slovakia are particularly urged to test, as some may have been infected through medical or dental procedures before 1991.

People can order a free, confidential NHS home self-testing kit, external without needing to speak to a GP.

News.title: Swimming lessons 'vital' as schools gap revealed
News.content:
Children at English primary schools with more pupils on free school meals are less likely to leave able to swim 25m, BBC research has found.

While 72% of Year 6 children on average left school able to swim 25m in 2024-25, this drops to just 55% for schools with a higher proportion of disadvantaged children.

Ashley Jones, head of water safety and education at the Royal Life Saving Society (RLSS), said it was "absolutely vital" children were equipped with basic swimming and self-rescue skills.

A Department for Education (DfE) spokesperson said it was aware of the gap and it "needs to change".

The national curriculum in England, external states when they leave Year 6, all pupils should be able to:

Swim competently, confidently and proficiently over a distance of at least 25m

Use a range of strokes effectively (for example, front crawl, backstroke and breaststroke)

Perform safe self-rescue in different water-based situations

A BBC Freedom of Information request to the DfE has revealed the proportion of Year 6 pupils at individual state schools, excluding special schools, who are able to meet the targets.

While 70% of 2024-25 Year 6 leavers nationally could on average perform a safe self-rescue, only half of children from schools with the highest level of free meal eligibility could do so.

A safe self-rescue includes being able to tread water for 30 seconds, children being able to float on their back for 60 seconds and swim 15m to exit the water unaided.

Most school groups only get six weeks of 30-minute sessions to learn basic swimming skills â three hours in total.

The findings come after several water-related deaths this summer, including an 18-year-old man who died after getting into difficulty at sea at the weekend in East Sussex.

News.title: GB's Hunt comes of age with European 100m gold
News.content:
Amy Hunt had her coming of age moment as she stormed to 100m glory to claim her first senior international title and deliver Britain's first gold medal of the European Athletics Championships.

Hunt announced herself on the sport's global stage last year with world 200m silver in Tokyo - the first individual international medal of her senior career.

Having backed that up with Commonwealth 100m silver two weeks ago, the 24-year-old would not be denied gold this time in Birmingham.

"I have had such a string of silvers and I was starting to get a bit fed up with it, so I thought it was time for gold," Hunt, who won in 11 seconds flat, told BBC Sport.

"My parents gifted me these gold earrings to finally level up, because I wear all-silver jewellery.

"They said it was time for gold - they left me that note two nights ago - so it made me quite emotional.

"It was definitely time for me to come of age here."

It was Britain's second medal on the opening day of action after the hosts took silver in the mixed 4x400m relay.

Yemi Mary John held off Dutch athlete Myrte van der Schoot on the home straight to bring a British quartet also featuring Ben Jefferies, Charlotte Henrich and Toby Harries home in three minutes 10.47 seconds, behind winners Norway (3:09.62).

News.title: Treasury contributed to woman's death, inquest hears
News.content:
The death of a Treasury worker who took her own life the day after a meeting with her managers was "materially contributed" to by her employers, an inquest has heard.

Chloe Moffat, 26, a personal assistant to a Treasury director, died on 20 May last year, after she was told of allegations she had shared sensitive confidential information about colleagues, which she denied.

Surrey Coroner's Court heard the Treasury did not apply written disciplinary policy which would have made clear that if the allegations were proven, the likely penalty was a written warning, not dismissal.

A spokesperson for the Treasury said it was "considering the findings carefully".

In a statement to the press, Moffat's family said they believed the Treasury failed in its duty of care.

"When she needed support, reassurance and fair treatment, she was left frightened, isolated and convinced her career and reputation had been destroyed," they added.

The inquest, in which a conclusion of suicide was recorded, heard that on 19 May Moffat went to what she thought was a routine one-to-one with her line manager, but a more senior manager was also present.

She was told of allegations she had shared sensitive personal information about colleagues, obtained as part of her job.

Moffat, from London, denied this.

News.title: Cocaine worth £232m found in banana shipment
News.content:
Cocaine with a street value of Â£232m was discovered hidden in a large shipment of bananas from South America.

The 2.9-tonne (2,900kg) haul was smuggled into London Gateway Port in Thurrock, Essex, on Thursday.

The drugs were removed from the container and then delivered to an address near Buntingford, Hertfordshire, where Border Force officers swooped in.

They arrested nine men allegedly connected to the bust, who were later released on bail.

Border Force had been tipped off about the illegal consignment by the National Crime Agency.

News.title: Vandals target playground before it has even opened
News.content:
A play area that cost more than Â£178,000 was vandalised days before it was due to open.

Knowsley Council leader Graham Morgan said he was "absolutely furious" that every piece of play equipment at the Finch Woods play park in Halewood, Knowsley had been spray painted with graffiti over the weekend.

Trees and safety surfacing were also damaged and rubbish was left strewn across the site, with the cost of the damage estimated to run into thousands of pounds.

Morgan condemned the "mindless vandalism", saying "it is the cost to the community that sickens me the most".

News.title: Antiques stolen in 16th Century manor house raid
News.content:
More than 20 antiques were stolen from a National Trust (NT) property during a break-in last month, it has been revealed.

The silver, pewter and brass items were taken from the 16th Century manor house at Baddesley Clinton in Warwickshire, on 30 July.

The most notable piece of the 25 taken was a Georgian silver salver engraved with the coat of arms of the Ferrers, the family who resided at the house for about five centuries, the NT said.

"We very much hope the objects will be returned, so they can be enjoyed by everyone," a spokesperson added.

News.title: Great-grandad with cancer risks his health to help others on 460-mile journey
News.content:
A great-grandfather with bladder and kidney cancer is walking 462 miles (743km) for charity, despite knowing it could impact his own treatment.

John Eryl Parry, 78, from Pontypool, Torfaen, began his coast-to-coast journey at the UK's most easterly point in Lowestoft, Suffolk, on 21 June, and is due to reach St David's Head in Pembrokeshire on 11 August.

He found out he had cancer after he fell off a ladder and was taken to hospital.

John admitted he had not told his oncology team about his challenge, but said he was warned by a doctor that his body would "change" during it, and it could impact his treatment plan.

News.title: MSP apologises for hurt caused by rape 'demonisation' comments
News.content:
A newly-elected MSP has apologised for the hurt caused by comments in which they talked of the "demonisation" of rape.

Scottish Green Party politician Q Manivannan has also faced criticism for suggesting rape is a "spectrum of things" during a podcast recorded before they were elected to the Scottish Parliament.

Earlier, the Scottish Rape Crisis Alliance (SRCA) - which represents four rape crisis centres - said there is "no hierarchy of rape" and warned the MSP not to minimise sexual violence.

In a statement, Manivannan said clips from the podcast had been "selectively edited" but said they were "sorry" for the upset, and insisted they would never seek to diminish a rape survivor's experience.

The comments, which were made during The Subjective Space podcast , externalrecorded last year, sparked fury after they re-emerged online at the weekend.

News.title: No evidence of data breach after Chinese-made component found in Navy drones, MoD says
News.content:
The Ministry of Defence (MoD) said there is no evidence to suggest a systems or data breach after the Royal Navy's new sea drones were found to include a Chinese-made component.

During what the MoD called a "routine cyber vulnerability assessment" of the drones, the cameras were found to have sent a squark â also known as a heartbeat communication â to a Chinese IP address.

A squark can signal when the system is switched on, is functioning properly, but it can also carry location information.

"A thorough investigation found no evidence of MoD data or systems being accessed, compromised or transmitted externally," an MoD spokesperson said.

"Our assurance and testing processes are designed to identify and address potential vulnerabilities early, and we continue to undertake routine security activity across our systems and equipment," the MoD added.

This is embarrassing for the MoD which, like most Nato countries, has banned Chinese components from military equipment - not least over fears of spying.

The K3 Scout sea drones can remotely carry out surveillance, and according to their supplier, "support a wide range of mission profiles including maritime awareness, force protection, logistics and precision strike".

The supplier of the Royal Navy's 20 new K3 sea drones, Kraken, said it was given assurances about security. But a third party supplier of the drone camera still had Chinese-made components.

Kraken has said it is confident no sensitive information has been shared.

The story was first reported by The Telegraph., external

The security lapse has been addressed, but it is a reminder of the heavy dominance on Chinese supply chains.

Even the defence sector â which has taken measures to prevent espionage â still struggles to source materials, and technologies that are China free, or as cheap.

Actor Reggie Bannister, best known for his role in horror series Phantasm, has died aged 80.

The Californian-born actor, was remembered as “my best friend, my confidant, my partner, my soul mate” by his wife Gigi in a statement on Facebook.

She said: “At 3.45am on Sunday, August 9, 2026, I last checked on my beloved Reggie Bannister’s condition.

“He was panting but quiet and asleep. I was exhausted so I went back to sleep.

“At 0600 hours, our kitty, GG (Grey Guy) who has been sleeping on Reggie’s bed at night, came running upstairs and jumped onto the bed meowing. I went down to see what the problem was.

open image in gallery Bannister, pictured in 2006, appeared as the gun-toting ice cream man Reggie in 1979’s Phantasm, then appearing in all four sequels ( Getty )

“Somewhere inside, in my soul, I knew, Reggie was gone.

“He looked so quiet and peaceful, like he was asleep, in his bed, In Our Mountain Home, as his song goes. In the snap of fingers, my best friend, my confidant, my partner, my soul mate was transitioned to another dimension – a higher plane.

“He no longer suffers, he’s no longer in pain, that gives me solace.

“I will see you on the flip side, honey bunny, save me a hug, wait for me.”

Bannister appeared as the gun-toting ice cream man Reggie in 1979’s Phantasm.

He also appeared in its sequels Phantasm II (1988), Phantasm III: Lord Of The Dead (1993) and Phantasm IV: Oblivion (1998), all directed by Don Coscarelli, and Phantasm: Ravager (2016), which was co-written by Coscarelli and directed by David Hartman.

In a tribute on Facebook, Coscarelli said: “In the Phantasm series, only Reggie could turn a simple role as an ice cream vendor sidekick into an unlikely action hero for the ages.

“He channelled himself into that role. All the fans who met him at the horror conventions could attest that in-person, Reg was cool, funny, loyal, and steadfast.

“Reggie the character was Reggie the friend. In real life, he embodied all the qualities of his character in Phantasm and no one questioned that Reg was that guy, the one willing to lay his body down on the fires of hell for his friends.”

He added: “Reggie Bannister was a gifted creative collaborator, a dear friend and he will be sincerely missed. Yes, Reg, to me and your legion of fans, you’ll always be ‘Hot As Love’.”

Bannister’s other film roles included in Survival Quest (1989), comedy horror film Bubba Ho-Tep (2002), both directed by Coscarelli, and Bugs (1990).

Born in 1945, Bannister was also a US army veteran who served in the Vietnam War before becoming an actor.

He was reportedly diagnosed with Lewy body dementia and Parkinson’s disease in 2016.

Media regulator Ofcom has launched an investigation into GB News after a broadcast guest linked Pride parades to bestiality and paedophilia.

The watchdog announced the inquiry on Monday after receiving more than 12,000 complaints about the programme, which aired on 5 July, shortly after London Pride.

The remarks were delivered by Catholic media commentator Caroline Farrow during an appearance on the Alex Armstrong Tonight show.

Farrow told the host that Pride was "not about gay rights" and claimed it had "become about celebrating every single sexuality that isn’t heterosexuality".

She added: “Including some very bizarre and unhealthy kinks and quirks, you know, like furries and bestiality, and even minor-attracted – they call themselves minor-attracted. You know, paedophiles.”

RuPaul’s Drag Race UK star Bimini and Green Party leader Zack Polanski were among those to speak out and signed an open letter calling for Ofcom to hold the channel to account.

Alex Armstrong on GB News interjected during the live segment and challenged the comments ( GB News )

Armstrong interjected during the live segment and challenged the comments. He addressed the comments again in a later broadcast, describing them as an “age-old gay trope”.

He told viewers: “We welcome robust and difficult debates on this channel, and particularly on this show. It is not, and never will be, an echo chamber for anybody. That’s why we always have a dissenting voice on all of my shows, want you to hear all aspects of every debate.

“That’s made it even more important, when guests come on my show and make statements that are considered homophobic or deeply offensive, that they are challenged and balanced by me and my guests if they do that. But sometimes I feel it’s necessary to go a bit further, and I’m going to do that tonight.

“Comments made by guests last weekend conflated gay pride with the celebration of paedophilia. This is an age-old gay trope that’s been used over a number of years to demonise and slander gay people. And as I said to the guest during that segment, it is a statement I fundamentally reject and have not witnessed when attending Pride myself.

“The debate we were meant to be having was around whether or not Pride was suitable for children. Those comments by guests had no place in that discussion, and in my opinion, were lazy and offensive arguments that don’t reflect my views or the views of this channel, where many LGBT people also work.”

The videos have since been removed from GB News’s YouTube channel.

A GB News spokesperson said: “These investigations have been the subject of an orchestrated campaign against GB News. As a regulated broadcaster, GB News takes its regulatory obligations seriously and complies fully with the Ofcom Broadcasting Code.

“GB News is Britain’s number one news channel and has proudly occupied this position for the last 12 months. We intend to robustly defend these investigations.”

Firefighters have warned they need more funding as they face increasing pressure from “an unprecedented summer of dangerous and volatile wildfires.”

As three quarters of England was plunged into drought on Monday, the Fire Brigades Union (FBU) has said crews across the country would need access to the best equipment as the consequences of climate change become a “national priority”.

"Firefighters are having extra demands put on them as a result of an unprecedented summer of dangerous and volatile wildfires,” said Steve Wright FBU general secretary. "Our country is facing unpredictable environmental challenges, and it must be a national priority to ensure we have enough properly equipped firefighters ready to face these threats."

Major wildfires have hit areas such as the Pennines, the Cairngorms in Scotland, Llanwonno in the Rhondda Valleys in South Wales, and Dunwich Heath in Suffolk as the UK experiences tinderbox conditions.

open image in gallery Firefighters stood down a major incident in Dunwich Heath this week, weeks after 150 hectares of the nature reserve caught fire (Jacob King/PA) ( PA Wire )

More than 120 firefighters were working on Monday to contain the latest blaze, which is affecting a square kilometre of heathland in the New Forest, Hampshire and has closed the A31, following a vehicle fire.

The Met Office warned last month that the extreme conditions this summer, which have seen numerous temperature records broken, would become the new normal due to climate change.

Climate information scientist Mike Kendon said: “What we used to think of as extreme, we increasingly consider as normal.”

The union also warned that while fire brigades didn’t have a statutory duty to attend floods, they often tackled them out of moral obligation and would need the correct equipment to do so as flooding becomes more common.

open image in gallery Firefighters have been tackling a blaze in the New Forest near Ringwood in Hampshire ( PA Wire )

"Flooding is also a major issue which our members do not have a statutory duty to attend but they often to do out of a sense of moral obligation,” said Mr Wright.

"Rather than leaving it to individual firefighters and brigades making these decisions, we believe it should be a statutory duty for firefighters to attend floods. However, with those extra responsibilities must come increased funding, improved access to the best equipment and better national resilience.”

The Environment Agency (EA) said on Monday that 71.3 per cent of England is experiencing “flash drought”, as a dry start to August followed the country’s driest July on record.

Flash droughts develop very quickly because of a combination of very low rainfall and high temperatures. In Monday’s announcement, the agency said the East Midlands, Lincolnshire and Northamptonshire, Kent and East Sussex, and Solent and the South Downs have become the latest areas to move into drought.

It comes after two record-breaking heatwaves in May and June that led to the deaths of more than 2,800 people, followed by further heatwaves in July. A fifth heatwave will hit parts of the UK this week as temperatures could reach 36C in parts of the south and east of England on Thursday.

Amber heat health alerts have been issued for most of England including the Midlands, South East, North West and South West, while a yellow alert will be in force for the North East.

The UK is set to witness its fullest solar eclipse for the next 54 years this Wednesday, with the Met Office pinpointing Devon and Cornwall as prime locations for viewing the celestial event.

Between 6.17pm and 8.06pm on August 12, over 90 per cent of the sun will be obscured by the moon.

It will be the most extensive blockage of the sun over British skies since the total eclipse of 1999.

The south-west of England, specifically Devon and Cornwall, and the westernmost parts of Pembrokeshire in Wales, are forecast to experience the fullest extent of the eclipse, with 94 to 96 per cent of the sun expected to be covered.

Plymouth, for instance, is predicted to see 94.66 per cent obscuration at 7.16pm.

Elsewhere, regions including the rest of Wales, Northern Ireland, parts of the West Midlands and the wider South West, and western Scotland, can anticipate between 92 and 94 per cent solar coverage.

open image in gallery The Met Office has released a map showing the best places to watch the 2026 solar eclipse ( Met Office )

Cardiff is expected to see 93.24 per cent of the sun obscured at 7.13pm, while Belfast will experience 93.09 per cent coverage at 7.08pm.

Skygazers in the rest of the UK will likely see the moon obscure 90 per cent to 92 per cent of the sun – with 91.79 per cent expected in Birmingham at 7.12pm, 91.41 per cent in London at 7.13pm, 90.74 per cent in Inverness at 7.03pm, 90.71 per cent in Edinburgh at 7.06pm and 90.22 per cent in Newcastle at 7.07pm.

Those keen to catch a sight of the fullest possible solar eclipse should avoid the easternmost parts of the UK, where only 88 per cent to 90 per cent of solar coverage is expected.

These include the coasts of Norfolk, Yorkshire and Aberdeenshire, as well as the Orkney and Shetland Islands.

open image in gallery Planetarium Astronomer Dr Carys Herbert demonstrates wearing Celestron solar eclipse glasses to safely view the celestial event ( PA )

Do I need glasses to view the solar eclipse?

The Royal Greenwich Observatory warned the public that regular sunglasses are not a safe enough method to view the cosmic phenomenon.

Imo Bell, a planetarium astronomer at the observatory, previously said: “It’s not a total eclipse, but over 90 per cent is really exciting. We’re not going to get one this good for a really long time.

“So, it’s important not to miss it, and to be prepared. You can’t just go out and expect to have a look because it’s really dangerous for your eyes.

“So, you can use solar eclipse glasses, which are very, very different from sunglasses – they block out so much light that you can’t see anything through them except the sun, because that’s how much light they need to block for the damaging light of the sun to be safe to view.

“Ideally a solar telescope is an amazing way to witness it, and if you don’t have one of them then you can look into whether your local astronomy society is doing any events.

“And if all else fails, you can project the image of the eclipse using a household item like a colander which has lots of holes in – point the colander towards the Sun with your back facing it, and in the shadow of the colander you’ll be able to see the eclipse in the holes, which is really cool.”

The next time the moon obscures as much of the sun will be in 2081 and the next total solar eclipse in the UK will be in 2090.

Ms Bell advised getting to a vantage point facing west, with minimal buildings around, as the best way to view the eclipse.

“We might notice the sky getting a little bit dark, so if you’re looking safely, it’ll look a bit like the moon is taking a bite out of the sun, you’ll see something that looks a bit like a crescent sun.”

The media company behind US President Donald Trump’s Truth Social platform has slumped to a 238 million US dollar (£176 million) quarterly loss and announced plans to move back to its social media roots.

Trump Media & Technology’s losses in the three months to June were more than 10 times those a year earlier, as it counted the cost of branching out into businesses outside media, such as crypto, online betting, finance and even nuclear energy.

It said, on announcing second quarter figures, that it would largely ditch many of the new ventures and refocus efforts on its social media mission and acting as a forum for users to post their views.

The firm’s new chief executive, Kevin McGurn, said: “We made the disciplined choice to pivot in order to invest more time and resources in our most important initiatives.

“We will say no to things or change course as warranted.”

Key to the firm’s plans is its controversial new Truth API service, which will charge for special high speed access to Truth Social posts, including those made by Mr Trump.

Wall Street financial traders can access posts from top users ahead of others – such as major policy announcements made by Mr Trump on the platform – allowing them to profit from subsequent moves in shares, bonds and interest rates.

Trump Media has already attracted criticism from those claiming it is a vehicle for Mr Trump to profit from his presidency.

Mr McGurn brushed aside these concerns, saying: “Providing licensed real-time public data through commercial APIs (application programming interface) is a well-established business practice across the technology, financial information and media industries.

“This is no different.”

But he confirmed Trump Media’s nuclear fusion business would continue under the new strategy, with aims to complete a previously-announced merger with energy company TAE Technologies by the end of 2026.

Its second-quarter figures showed much of the hit to the result was because of paper losses on the value of the firm’s crypto holdings.

With those paper losses excluded, Trump Media suffered a 164 million dollar (£121 million) loss from a 44 million dollar loss (£33 million) a year earlier.

In the second quarter, Trump Media posted revenues of 1.7 million dollars (£1.3 million), more than double from a year ago.

News.content:

The Inbetweeners star James Buckley has revealed that he’s been forced to give up alcohol and make major lifestyle changes after being diagnosed with a genetic disease.

The actor, 38, opened up about his health on the latest episode of his podcast with co-host and wife Clair, telling listeners that doctors told him that he had a high level of Lipoprotein(a) in his blood – and was therefore at a “high risk” of a cardiovascular incident.

Lipoprotein(a) is a cholesterol-carrying lipoprotein found in blood, the level of which is mostly inherited. High levels of it can increase the chances of heart disease, heart attacks and stroke.

Speaking on At Home With The Buckleys on Sunday (9 August), Buckley – who is best known for playing vulgar teenager Jay on The Inbetweeners, said that he’s been dealing with “health problems” after receiving blood test results.

open image in gallery James Buckley reveals he has a genetic disease ( At Home With the Buckleys )

“I’ve got a genetic disease, mate,” he said. “It’s something to do with my Lipoprotein(a), something to do with that.

“There's nothing you can do about it, by the way. And the doctor's just been like, ’You need to change.’ I'm at a high risk now for a cardiovascular incident. My heart, my arteries. It’s not my fault.”

Buckley added that since receiving the diagnosis, he has given up alcohol and stopped ordering takeaways – with his wife joining him in solidarity.

“I'm not a religious man, but sometimes I feel like there is a God that sort of goes, ‘That’ll teach you,’” he added. “I feel like I've been on this podcast slagging people off that don't drink, and now I’ve been told to try not drinking.

“But I'm going to have a beer soon. I’m just trying to do a little reset, especially after the tour.”

open image in gallery Buckley with his wife Clair ( Getty )

He also admitted that he fears for his kids when they’re older, as he may have passed down the high levels of lipoprotein(a). “Also, another little worry is that because it’s genetic, my children might have it,” he said.

Buckley married former glamour model Clair Meek in 2012, with the couple now parents to sons Harrison, 14, and Jude, 12, who were named after The Beatles’ George Harrison and the song “Hey Jude”.

While Buckley has appeared in comedies White Gold, Zapped and Popstar: Never Stop Never Stopping since finding fame on The Inbetweeners, he’s set to return to the Channel 4 show for a rebooted version on Netflix.

He’ll reportedly be reuniting with co-stars Simon Bird, Joe Thomas and Blake Harrison for the project, helmed by original creators Damon Beesley and Iain Morris.

News.content:
