The inexperienced Matt Lawlor is set for a challenging first full season in charge of Fleetwood, who are boosted by the signing of Andy Cannon from Wrexham. Steve Cotterill revitalised Cheltenham almost a year ago, but five of their first six summer signings were relegated in May, which does not inspire confidence. After finishing comfortably in midtable, Accrington Stanley may not fear the drop and Cole Stockton is a clever signing but there is a nagging doubt about the club’s efficacy.

View image in fullscreen Managerial inexperience may prove challenging for Matt Lawlor (left) who has much to prove in his first full season at Fleetwood Town. Photograph: Phil Oldham/Shutterstock

Ones to watch

Maldini Kacurri, Grimsby, 20 After starting last season on loan at doomed National League side Morecambe, the Albania international may have wondered if life outside Arsenal was really for him. The defender shone when he stepped up to League Two with Grimsby, guided by David Artell, proving himself capable of coping with the physicality in the lower tiers.

Patrick Mlynarski, Crewe, 18 A Wales youth international, the recently-turned 18-year-old is now in his first year as a professional. The winger made his debut in the EFL Trophy last season, but is yet to feature in the league. Previously part of Everton’s academy, Mylnarski is skilful and powerful, playing on the left, possessing the ability to cut in or beat defenders on the outside.

Will Gray, Shrewsbury, 17 The midfielder made four starts last season and signed his first professional contract in the summer. His manager, Gavin Cowan, has praised his mentality and ability to keep things simple in the centre of the park.

Sports.title: Liverpool owners close to £1.35bn sale of 30% stake to consortium including Jeff Bezos
Sports.content:
A consortium including the Amazon founder, Jeff Bezos, is close to completing a deal for a 30% stake in Liverpool after months of talks with Fenway Sports Group. The investors are led by Amit Bhatia, the son-in-law of the Indian billionaire Lakshmi Mittal and who previously was a shareholder and director at Queens Park Rangers.

The Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin is another member of the group who will pay in the region of £1.35bn. The deal is effectively agreed, but may take up to a month to complete.

Bezos has a personal fortune of around $257bn (£190bn), according to Forbes, making him the fourth-richest person in the world, while Saverin is reportedly worth $32bn. This will be Bezos’s first investment in football, but he has previously looked into bidding for NFL franchises. The 62-year-old will receive equity as part of the deal, which Deloitte has advised on.

Bezos is the executive chair of Amazon having relinquished day-to-day control when he stepped down as chief executive five years ago. Under his leadership, the online retailer has diversified into being an entertainment provider and has bought numerous sports rights for its streaming service.

Amazon had live UK rights for 20 Premier League games each season for six seasons until the end of last year and broadcasts the Champions League in several European countries, as well as some NFL games in the US.

FSG bought Liverpool in 2010 and have overseen two Premier League titles. FSG sold 3% of the club to the US private equity firm Dynasty Equity in 2023.

It has been a summer of change at Anfield, with Andoni Iraola replacing Arne Slot as head coach, Mohamed Salah left on a free transfer and has joined Trabzonspor and Michael Edwards departed his role as chief executive officer at FSG.

Sports.title: Nottingham Forest owner Marinakis sues Crystal Palace over fan banner
Sports.content:
The Nottingham Forest owner, Evangelos Marinakis, is suing Crystal Palace for defamation after supporters of the south London club displayed a banner depicting him holding a gun to the head of the England midfielder Morgan Gibbs-White.

Almost 12 months since the banner appeared midway through the first half of Palace’s 1-1 draw with Forest at Selhurst Park, lawyers for Marinakis lodged the claim for defamation against CPFC Ltd and “persons unknown” at the high court on Monday.

The banner showed the Greek shipping magnate pointing the gun at Gibbs-White, who had been set to join Tottenham last summer before Forest pulled out of the deal, and also featured the message: “Mr Marinakis is not involved in blackmail, match‑fixing, drug trafficking or corruption.” Marinakis has previously rejected all those allegations. Lawyers for Marinakis were approached for comment. A spokesperson for Palace did not comment.

Palace were fined £50,000 by the Football Association in February after being found guilty of failing “to ensure its spectators and/or supporters (and anyone purporting to be supporters or followers) didn’t behave in an improper, offensive, abusive, insulting and/or provocative way at this match”. The FA added in its statement: “The fact that Crystal Palace had a policy to prevent banners being smuggled into the stadium demonstrates that it was aware of the risk.”

Last summer, Palace and Forest were at loggerheads after Forest wrote to Uefa to voice their concerns that Palace could be in breach of multiclub ownership rules. The FA Cup winners ended up being demoted to the Conference League, with Forest – who had finished seventh in the Premier League and originally qualified for the Conference League – promoted in their place. Palace went on to win that competition under Oliver Glasner, while Forest reached the Europa League semi-finals.

Glasner has since joined Forest after leaving Palace at the end of his contract in a move that has surprised both sets of supporters. The Austrian said this week that Marinakis had persuaded him to change his mind over dinner in Athens after previously rejecting Forest because they were not in Europe next season.

“Then I had a more detailed look and there are two reasons why I changed my mind and I told him,” Glasner said. “No 1 is I think there is more potential in the squad than they have shown. And No 2 is you, it’s your ambition, because I am very ambitious.”

Sports.title: Manchester City closing in on £85m Bouaddi to soften blow of Rodri’s expected exit
Sports.content:
Manchester City are closing in on signing Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille, with the midfielder’s expected arrival clearing the path for Rodri to join Barcelona. The 18-year-old has agreed personal terms with City, but the club are still finalising the deal with Lille who value Bouaddi at €100m (£85m).

City’s new manager, Enzo Maresca, wants to integrate the Morocco international into his first-team squad immediately. City meet Arsenal in the Community Shield on Sunday and start their Premier League campaign against Bournemouth on 23 August.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Barcelona are confident of signing Rodri from City, but they will have to return with an improved offer after an initial €45m bid was rejected last week. The sale of Ferran Torres, who is of interest to Paris Saint‑Germain, would finance Rodri’s purchase. City are all but resigned to the sale of the 30‑year‑old, who has a year left on his contract.

If the Bouaddi deal can be completed, he would join Elliot Anderson, who arrived last month from Nottingham Forest for £116m, in a new-look midfield, which has lost the experience of Bernardo Silva.

Manchester United, meanwhile, are interested in the Leicester player Louis Page. United, who face competition from Arsenal, are hopeful of securing a deal for the 18-year-old midfielder, with Page believed to favour a transfer to Old Trafford.

Marcus Rashford has joined United at their County Kildare training camp following the England forward’s post‑World Cup break. The 28-year-old has spent the past season and a half on loan at Barcelona and Aston Villa respectively, in the aftermath of a breakdown in his relationship with the club executive and the former United head coach Ruben Amorim. Relations have now eased and Rashford is focused on working under the United manager, Michael Carrick, although he could still leave before the end of the transfer window.

Sports.title: Are Manchester United returning to relevance under Michael Carrick? | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
Manchester United finally seem to have something that resembles stability in the dressing room under Michael Carrick. I feel with quality signings in defence and midfield, they could mount a decent challenge for the Premier League next season. How do you feel they will fare? – Sterling.

There’s an odd sense that Michael Carrick’s level of achievement last season was at precisely the most awkward level for the board. United didn’t produce indisputably brilliant football under him but equally 12 wins and three draws in 17 games was good enough that they pretty much had to give him the job. But it’s one thing to turn out those kinds of results when the pressure’s off, you’re already out of both cup competitions and you don’t have any European football; it’s quite another to do it in the heat of a full season. United don’t have to have an especially amazing season to play 15 more games this season than they did in 2025-26.

That’s not to say that Carrick won’t be successful. There was much that he did last season that was very impressive. Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans bolster an area of the squad that desperately needed to improve. A left-back seems almost certain to arrive before the end of the month and there’s probably the need for one more high-class experienced central defender. It’s not clear what Marcus Rashford’s future is after his return from loan at Barcelona, but he has two years left on his contract and could add dynamism and finishing to the left side of the attack. It’s probably not a title-winning squad, but it’s certainly one that should qualify for the Champions League.

Two questions remain that will only be answered as the season goes on. First, Carrick himself: can he cope with the churn of two games a week, and operating with a squad that is at least as fatigued as their opponents? And second, where is the club psychologically? Part of the problem for United, a familiar trait of big clubs who have fallen from grace, is that they have got into a routine of failure, that no success can ever quite be trusted, and every setback is seen as a further example of the terminal decline (although just as damaging would be suddenly believing everything is fine if United were to win, say, their first three games of the season). Retaining clarity of thought and making realistic assessments are perhaps the greatest challenges for a club that has known greatness but is struggling to return to those heights.

What do you see the broader impact of the VAR changes that Fifa made this year being? Do you think that other soccer leagues will see the increasingly automated, faster but less human approach taken by Fifa this summer and choose to adopt it? (I am aware that the Premier League has already chosen to reject much of it) – Dennis.

The most notable changes implemented before the World Cup allowed VAR to review and overturn incorrectly awarded corner kicks, certain attacking fouls and clear mistakes relating to red cards given from a second yellow. The only one of these adopted by the Premier League is to allow VAR to overturn a second yellow leading to a red (VAR cannot recommend that a referee should award a second yellow that would lead to a red). If we have to have VAR, that seems reasonable enough; nobody wants to see a team incorrectly reduced to 10 men.

At the World Cup, the corner issue only rarely came up, but it always seemed slightly odd that incorrectly awarded goal kicks could not be turned into corners. Personally, I would scrap VAR, or at least this form of it, but if incorrect decisions can be corrected quickly and unobtrusively then they probably should be. I understand, though, why the Premier League, aiming for a “light touch” – good luck with that – would be resistant.

Greater use of VAR, though, seemed to be the direction of travel. I suspect relatively soon offsides will be almost fully automated, which probably makes sense so long as it’s almost instantaneous. Whatever doubts there may be about margins of error and frame rates, it’s still going to be more accurate than a 40-year-old running the line 30 yards away, peering through a thicket of players.

More significant is probably the Premier League’s adoption of regulations against timewasting: speeded-up substitutions, players who receive treatment having to remain off the field for 60 rather than 30 seconds, an outfield player having to be withdrawn for 60 seconds after a goalkeeper receives treatment, and a five-second clock on throw-ins and goal kicks. All should speed up the game and improve the spectacle. It’ll be interesting as well to see the level of tolerance for grappling in the box, particularly by attacking players, which was an area in which the Premier League seemed out of step with the rest of Europe last season.

Which of the Premier League’s promoted sides have the best chance of staying up, and why? – Nicholas.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Twice weekly Sign up to Soccer Desk Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer. Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The achievements of Sunderland and Leeds last season, finishing seventh and 14th, will have heartened the promoted sides, but the truth is it will be extremely difficult for all three. Both those sides invested heavily in a way that is impossible for Coventry, Ipswich or Hull. It’s very hard to see how Hull, who were promoted unexpectedly, can survive. Coventry, perhaps, with the euphoria of their Premier League return and the Frank Lampard factor can give it a go, but their summer spending has been modest. Ipswich, with recent Premier League experience, have a chance and have made some intriguing signings in Daizen Maeda, Abdul Fatawu, Issa Diop and Chuba Akpom, but they’ve lost the manager who got them up, with Kieran McKenna opting for a break rather than another Premier League campaign. Gary O’Neil perhaps feels he has unfinished business, but if any of the promoted sides are to survive, they need another club to have a dreadful campaign.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace and Everton agree Brennan Johnson-Dwight McNeil swap deal
Sports.content:
Crystal Palace and Everton have agreed a straight swap for Brennan Johnson and Dwight McNeil – six months after McNeil’s partner accused Palace of messing with his mental health after pulling out of a deal.

McNeil and Johnson, who became Palace’s record signing when he joined in January from Tottenham for £35m, only to be surpassed by the arrival of Jørgen Strand Larsen from Wolves for an initial £43m a few weeks later, are understood to have agreed four-year contracts with the option of a further 12 months. They are expected to have medicals on Monday.

McNeil, who has entered the final year of his Everton contract, appeared to be moving to Selhurst Park in February after Palace agreed a £20m fee on transfer deadline day. But the collapse of Jean-Philippe Mateta’s £30m move to Milan, after the France striker failed a medical, prompted Palace to change their offer to an initial loan with an obligation to buy at the end of the season.

They submitted a deal sheet to the Premier League, but then pulled out. McNeil’s partner, Megan Sharpley, wrote an emotional post on Instagram saying there had been “radio silence” from Palace and that the player’s mental health had been affected.

“Tonight, and the last 48 hours, have broken my heart to see how the football world you love so much can be so cruel to you,” she wrote at the time. “We live in a world where everyone is aware of how big a problem mental health is. So, in football, why do we find it acceptable because these young men are on a lot of money and that’s OK to mess and toy with their mental health and that it’s just part of the job?”

Johnson has been disappointing since moving to Palace, failing to score in 18 Premier League appearances. Given he signed a four-and-a-half-year contract in January that is believed to be worth more than £100,000 a week, Palace will take a significant hit on the fee they paid, but remove one of their highest earners from the wage bill.

Palace are also finalising a deal to sign Anan Khalaili from Union Saint-Gilloise for £21m. The Israel right-back had his medical on Sunday and is expected to sign a five-year contract. The 21-year-old’s move to Internazionale broke down last month after he failed a medical.

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho's Netflix documentary gives fans the chance to see a version of the Special One they have never seen before. It's a must-watch with added stardust from Sir Alex Ferguson, Zlatan Ibrahimovic and Co: TV REVIEW
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho's Netflix documentary gives fans the chance to see a version of the Special One they have never seen before. It's a must-watch with added stardust from Sir Alex Ferguson, Zlatan Ibrahimovic and Co: TV REVIEW

'You don’t want to make me cry, because I don’t want.’ Then there is a long pause as an uncomfortable Jose Mourinho looks around, taps the table, and attempts to suppress his emotions.

This is Mourinho as we have never seen him before.

The 63-year-old had just been asked about how he processed the death of his father while he was manager of Manchester United in 2017. He fights back the tears for as long as he can, battling to keep his enigmatic personal persona intact.

This is something that Mourinho tries to do throughout his new hit three-part docu-series on Netflix. The legendary manager wants to give football fans an insight into his outrageously successful career on the touchline, which has seen him win 26 major trophies across England, Spain, Portugal and Italy, rather than delve into his private life.

Speaking in the latter stages of the documentary, Mourinho says: ‘People think they know me, but they don’t know me. And I’m happy they don’t. It’s a privilege for the people that know me.

‘You want to do a documentary because of my career. You don’t do a documentary with a guy that wins nothing in football.’

Jose Mourinho shows vulnerability like never before in his new Netflix docu-series

The documentary goes through the highs and lows of Mourinho's life and career

Mourinho is right; there is no world in which he would be sat on a sofa in his luxurious mansion, with the sunshine beating down on his swimming pool in the background (a Netflix cameraman’s dream setting) and be speaking to director Joe Pearlman if he had not achieved what he has done in his trophy-laden 30-year coaching career. That said, that doesn’t mean we don’t want to know what makes him tick.

Pearlman, who has directed documentaries about pop stars Robbie Williams and Lewis Capaldi, and BECKHAM producer John Battsek do an exemplary job of respecting Mourinho’s wishes to maintain his privacy while also providing a window into Jose the man and what he has been through.

From how his children ‘enjoy life more without me’ to how his father shaped the person he is, the docu-series showed us a more vulnerable Mourinho than he has ever allowed us to see previously.

Now, these small snippets are only really delved into towards the end of the final episode. The majority of the show takes us through the box office rollercoaster of a career Mourinho has had in the beautiful game. And boy, does it do a great job.

To make a sporting documentary enjoyable, it needs heaps of insight from those closest to the subject, untold anecdotes and exclusive information we haven't heard before. MOURINHO ticks all three of these boxes, and some.

It has bucket loads of insight from the likes of Frank Lampard, John Terry, Sir Alex Ferguson, Iker Casillas, Zlatan Ibrahimovic, and that’s just to name a few. These household names show just what a mammoth impact Mourinho has had on the game. I mean, they aren’t exactly nobodies, are they?

Not all of them drop in to shower the manager with compliments and praise. Former Real Madrid captain Casillas spoke of the ‘very cold’ relationship he had with Mourinho and how it was ‘taken to a limit’ during his first tenure.

This is Mourinho, after all; he has created a whole host of enemies throughout his time on the touchline. The programme doesn’t hold back from showing that; it takes us on a journey through the good and the bad, the highs and the lows. It doesn't shy away from anything.

There is plenty of insight into Mourinho from big names such as Sir Alex Ferguson

Zlatan Ibrahimovic also spoke of how Mourinho impacted his career when at Inter Milan

This is a man adored by Chelsea fans for his successes in England and by Inter Milan supporters for putting them back on their pedestal with a magical Champions League triumph.

But he is also the same man who had an acrimonious exit from Madrid, after forming what Sami Khedira calls a ‘nightmare’ and poisonous dressing room, and who was forced to agree a settlement with former Chelsea club doctor Eva Carneiro over claims that the manager discriminated against her.

There are also some incredible revelations, such as Mourinho discussing how he had meetings about returning to Barcelona in 2008 as manager, almost a decade after working tirelessly as an assistant and how, to this day, he doesn't like to be described as, 'the translator'.

But by far the biggest revelation of them all was Mourinho admitting, for the very first time, that he had verbally agreed to become Sir Alex Ferguson's replacement at Manchester United in 2013. However, the desire to feel 'loved' again changed his mind, so he made a dramatic U-turn and rejoined Chelsea.

'The objective of the work that we are doing is to tell the truth,' Mourinho eloquently said when revealing his big United bombshell. And well, that's what he is in this documentary: honest. He is, as always, unapologetically Mourinho.

Sports.title: Former Chelsea doctor Eva Carneiro aims thinly-veiled dig at Jose Mourinho on social media after his refusal to apologise over infamous touchline row in Netflix documentary
Sports.content:
Former Chelsea team doctor Dr Eva Carneiro has made a tongue-in-cheek jibe at Jose Mourinho in light of his comments about their infamous touchline row in a new documentary.

Mourinho avoided apologising to Carneiro when opening up about their infamous touchline row for the first time in over a decade in his new three-part Netflix docu-series titled MOURINHO, which is released on Tuesday.

The former Blues boss claimed he sees 'a lady doctor is the same as a man’s doctor' when addressing the incident which led to him agreeing a settlement with Carneiro after she took them to a tribunal in 2016 over claims that she was discriminated against by the manager.

And on the same day that Mourinho's quotes hit the headlines, Carneiro took to social media to make a light-hearted joke toward her former boss when announcing an exciting new chapter in her career.

Taking to X, Carneiro wrote that her announcement, which will be revealed in Autumn, was a 'Special One' before adding a winky face emoji.

'Bom Dia,' her post started. 'I have an announcement to make. A truly Special One.'

Bom Dia 😁⚽️!!!!!



I have an announcement to make.



A truly Special One 😉



A project close to my heart which I have been working on for years and is almost ready for launch.



Not an old set piece!



Watch this space. This autumn!!!! pic.twitter.com/kVXyNqJ3DD — Dr Eva Carneiro (@evacarneiro) August 10, 2026

Dr Eva Carneiro (left, pictured in 2015) has aimed a tongue-in-cheek dig at Joe Mourinho on social media

'A project close to my heart which I have been working on for years and is almost ready for launch. Not an old set piece! Watch this space. This autumn!!!!'

During a Premier League clash with Swansea City at the start of the 2015-16 season, Mourinho hit the roof when Carneiro and physio Jon Fearn went onto the pitch to treat Eden Hazard, who had gone down seemingly injured.

Dr Carneiro claimed that Mourinho sexually discriminated against her during his tirade and called her the 'daughter of a wh***' in his native Portuguese.

Back in 2015, Mourinho called her 'impulsive and naive' in his first public reaction to her decision to treat Hazard. She was then dropped from first-team duties and left the club just a month later.

Mourinho and Chelsea eventually agreed a settlement after Carneiro took them to a tribunal over claims that she was discriminated against by the manager, and constructively dismissed by the club.

But 11 years on, Mourinho believes he treated Carneiro in the same manner that he would treat any other doctor who made what he deemed as a mistake.

‘For me, a lady doctor is the same as a man’s doctor,' Mourinho said in the docu-series. 'So, as always, I use my vocabulary when I’m not happy.

'There are words in moments where the tension is very, very high. Normally, people with football culture, with football DNA, with football background, they go over it in one second. In that case, it was different.’

The 63-year-old has spoken up about the incident for the first time in over a decade in Netflix's new three-part docu-series MOURINHO

Hazard, who played under the now-63-year-old for two years, claimed 'it was nothing special' in the documentary, which is set to air on Tuesday, but 'with Jose everything is bigger'.

Footage shows that the Portuguese coach, who is now Real Madrid manager, shouted a whole host of expletives toward Carneiro and Fearn as they treated Hazard. He screamed phrases such as 'f*** off, man' and 'f*** you, man'.

'I’m not a doctor, but my eyes know when a player is injured, and they know when a player is not injured,' Mourinho said in the docu-series.

'I knew that he was not injured, but the doctors went to the pitch, and in that moment we were left with nine players.’

Hazard was forced to come off the pitch for a brief period, as is the rule when a player receives medical treatment, leaving Chelsea with nine men after Thibaut Courtois had been sent off.

Chelsea gave Dr Carneiro an unreserved apology, but Mourinho refused to say sorry and grinned as he left the tribunal.

A deal was done in a back corridor of the court and Chelsea then issued a statement saying it 'regretted the circumstances' which led to the former club doctor leaving and 'apologises unreservedly to her and her family for the distress caused'.

The terms of the settlement remain secret, but during the tribunal it was revealed that Chelsea had previously offered £1.2million to silence Carneiro.

Mourinho did not apologise after the incident or at the tribunal and there were no signs of an apology in the docu-series either.

Sports.title: How Enzo Maresca is quickly making Man City his own: The lowdown Pep Guardiola gave him on which players sulk when dropped, his obsession with beating man-to-man football - and why Erling Haaland WON'T be captain
Sports.content:
How Enzo Maresca is quickly making Man City his own: The lowdown Pep Guardiola gave him on which players sulk when dropped, his obsession with beating man-to-man football - and why Erling Haaland WON'T be captain

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The manager’s office is no more. Converted into a meeting room these days, one still filled by an aura of the guy who bid a teary farewell three months ago. Those walls can talk and Enzo Maresca would rather do his just down the corridor instead.

Maresca, the new Manchester City boss, has taken up permanent residence in the office previously held by a Pep of the Lijnders vintage rather than Guardiola.

The decision, one of his first in the chair, represents a literal embodiment of the reset that Maresca has been preaching to his players during pre-season in Asia. There will be ghosts in that office for some of the squad; there will be fond memories for others. He doesn’t want either emotion stirred from the past to surface as they pass the threshold into his space.

This call is likely to have been spawned from a lengthy meal with Guardiola in Barcelona the day before Maresca moved to the north west. The handover over a bottle or two of Sassicaia, Guardiola giving a rundown of the characteristics of these players, how they react to certain situations – largely not being picked. He’s morose, he fights, that one sulks. The conversation leaned towards personalities over tactics.

‘Useful for me,’ Maresca says. ‘I like to go in empty sometimes, to see things for myself, but he was here for so long and he has his opinions. He will be there (available) but he has to enjoy his holiday. He has to relax, so the idea is not to be calling him all the time. You have to decide which moments are the right time to pick up the phone and talk to him.’

The dynamic will be fascinating. The pair are close, Maresca an assistant during the Treble season before flying the nest for Leicester City and latterly Chelsea, both jobs ultimately successes. Yet Guardiola’s wise enough to keep his distance and has told his successor to speak unfettered publicly. The appointment came with his blessing, Txiki Begiristain’s blessing, but the old guard now have to sit back and watch.

This is a new City. Maresca’s City.

Guardiola gave Maresca the lowdown on all of the Man City players over dinner in Barcelona, largely noting how each star reacted to not being picked

Maresca, the new Manchester City boss, has taken up permanent residence in the office previously held by Pep Lijnders rather than Guardiola

On the seventh floor of Seoul’s Four Seasons, Maresca’s iPhone is pinging with government safety alerts about the ridiculously hot weather, which officially 'felt like' 45C during a win over the K-League All Stars. He only got to sleep at 4am and two espressos down – a third is on the way – is holding court, cracking wise and giving an insight into the man who will soon be patrolling the Etihad’s touchline as the club embarks on an intriguing era.

He’s beaming, flashes of the personality his players talk glowingly about but rarely seen in front of the cameras. Temperatures began to ease slightly through the week in South Korea and training has been progressively more encouraging and sharper, the concepts he wants on show during a 3-1 win over Atletico Madrid in the hours before they jetted home. With the big names – Jeremy Doku, Erling Haaland, Rayan Cherki – rejoining the group in Manchester this week, the real business is starting, Arsenal waiting in the Community Shield on Sunday. Rodri’s due back on Friday but Barcelona could have finalised a deal by then.

Haaland was one of the first to contact Maresca when the worst kept secret in football was finally confirmed in the summer. They had kept in touch since 2023 anyway and the Norwegian is going to prove a crucial lieutenant, a link between new and old, forming a quarter of the leadership group. He will not be first-choice captain though. Maresca has his grounds for this: the striker scores way too many goals. Haaland’s relentlessness has done him out of the armband.

‘At Leicester and Chelsea, I had a rule that when we scored, the captain had to come to the bench for instructions,’ Maresca smirks. ‘If Erling is the captain, f****** hell, we have a problem. Can you imagine?

‘If you saw in the game here, Ruben (Dias) came over to the bench. I think even if it is two or three minutes in, there is always something to adjust.’

That little sweary anecdote sets Maresca off. That or the third shot of coffee. He is regaling the initiation songs at dinner a few nights earlier. All of the staff, except himself, performed.

‘They were all s***,’ Maresca roars.

It’s suggested to him that coach Denis Silva’s was not too bad. He vehemently disagrees.

‘Javi (Molina), our analyst… it was a disaster. He was singing My Way, Frank Sinatra! You are already bad, go for an easy one. Ah actually, the best one was Michele (De Bernardin), our goalkeeping coach – he was very good.’

Haaland will not be Maresca's first-choice captain on the basis that the Norwegian striker scores too many goals

High standards, even with the microphone. The idea behind bringing in the Englishman on his staff, Danny Walker, is raised. Walker was an academy coach at City before Maresca was appointed as the Elite Development Squad’s boss during Covid. The pair were thrown together when Begiristain said the Italian couldn’t bring in his own assistant – even though the man in question, Marcos Alvarez (now on Maresca’s staff), was Catalan. Walker and Maresca have been inseparable ever since.

‘F****** hell, Danny Walker!’ Maresca laughs. ‘We go for breakfast and it is beans on toast, we go for dinner and it is a beer!’

But there is a reason why he is here beyond having worked with the likes of Nico O’Reilly and Rico Lewis when they were kids.

‘Danny is good on extra work at the end when we keep players doing something extra. I have six, seven people with me and not one of them is there because I feel they are just a friend. It is demanding. If we don't win games, we are all going home. That is good. I have Willy (Caballero) from Argentina, two Italian guys, one English, three Spanish. So we can speak all the languages. I speak French so we have it covered.’

In training sessions, Walker is the energetic sidekick to Maresca, who himself is fully immersed in the middle of drills, directing traffic and demanding exactly how City should build the play and move the ball.

This has been an obsession across the opening weeks of his tenure: finding ways of navigating opposition who go man-to-man, a tactic that has consumed the game at the highest level over the past two seasons. Maresca studied various plans over the six months between resigning in acrimony at Chelsea and taking over from Guardiola.

‘I was focused on not watching many games but I watched teams against man-to-man - it was more focused than watching general football,’ he explains.

‘Everyone goes man-to-man. I’m not sure it’s going to continue like that. For instance, if you see last season when Newcastle played Barcelona and it was 6-1. Atalanta and Bayern Munich was 6-1. Chelsea tried to go man-to-man with PSG (in March) and they destroyed them.

‘The games from last season, when (underdogs) tried to do it against big teams, they concede many goals.’

PSG are the ideal reference point: a side built on adaptability and runners carrying the ball, which is why Antoine Semenyo should thrive under similar instructions

PSG are the ideal, although that is obvious given the consecutive Champions League titles and a general fearlessness to their play. An adaptability with runners on the ball, which is why Antoine Semenyo ought to flourish under similar instructions. He certainly has in Seoul over the past week.

It is therefore no surprise that Ettore Messina, the renowned Italian basketball coach who was once at the San Antonio Spurs, knocked around some ideas with Maresca a few months back. Those will have strayed into tactical, given the two sports are beginning to collide.

Maresca’s primary focus is on these tweaks to the system and messaging. While improving their set-piece record is on the agenda, it is not a priority. ‘Probably Arsenal rely on set pieces a lot,’ Maresca says. ‘They use different strategies to win games (to City). Set pieces is the big change in the Premier League.

‘I tried to enjoy a little bit more time with the family and then I did two AI masterclasses because it’s like now everyone goes man to man, everyone is talking about AI. I wanted to understand how it works and have more knowledge.’

One class came in general use of AI – and in turn, communicating with a younger generation - and the other more specific on how it can be implemented into the technical side of football. Even after all that, Maresca laughs that he is unable to explain the basics of the technology.

He wants to move with the times and certainly times have changed in Manchester since his departure in 2023. His favourite Italian, Salvi’s, has shut. Vero Moderno is the new haunt, often frequented by Gianluigi Donnarumma and there have been bonding meals with staff already.

Maresca would prefer to live in the city centre, like Guardiola, but moving out towards Cheshire is more sensible with a family consisting of four kids under 13 whose accents are all English. A seven o’clock dinner at home with them is considered sacrosanct.

He will need that sanctity. This is an unknown, uncharted territory. They are only too aware of what happened across town but there is a calm, a certainty, to the way Maresca wants to do this and negotiate his way through what cannot be an easy task.

‘I know people will be comparing it to Pep after 10 games,’ he says, doing well not to reference that Guardiola won all 10 of those. ‘It doesn’t put pressure on me. I’ve said many times that he’s the best manager in the world over the last 20 years.

‘Someone asked me if it’s the impossible job to follow him. Maybe, but at the same time it’s a privilege.’

Sports.title: Evangelos Marinakis SUES Crystal Palace: Nottingham Forest owner brings defamation case against Premier League rival after fans held Morgan Gibbs-White 'blackmail' banner during feisty clash
Sports.content:
Evangelos Marinakis SUES Crystal Palace: Nottingham Forest owner brings defamation case against Premier League rival after fans held Morgan Gibbs-White 'blackmail' banner during feisty clash

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Evangelos Marinakis is suing Crystal Palace at the High Court following a controversial banner displayed at Selhurst Park last season.

The Nottingham Forest owner on Monday lodged a claim for defamation against his club’s Premier League rivals that dates back to the 1-1 draw between the clubs last August.

The banner depicting Marinakis holding a gun to the head of Forest player Morgan Gibbs-White and carried the words ‘Mr Marinakis is not involved in blackmail, match-fixing, drug trafficking or corruption.’ Marinakis has consistently denied any wrongdoing in relation to such allegations.

Palace were charged by the Football Association last November and while the banner was not specified as the reason for the charge, there are strict rules regarding messaging containing defamatory, political and offensive slogans.

There has been bad blood between Forest and Palace since Palace were demoted from the Europa League to the Europa Conference League a year ago, due to UEFA’s rules regarding multi-club ownership. Forest benefited from that decision and were promoted into the Europa League.

Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis is pursuing a defamation case against Crystal Palace

There has been bad blood between Forest and Palace since Palace were demoted from the Europa League to the Europa Conference League a year ago

The Gibbs-White/Marinakis banner appeared while that row was still fresh in the clubs’ minds.

Then Oliver Glasner, who led Palace to three trophies before departing at the end of last season, was promptly hired by Forest on a three-year deal. Palace host Forest in the Premier League on October 10.

‘This claim has been issued at Court shortly before the expiry of the one-year limitation period in defamation which could indicate that prior efforts to resolve the dispute have been unsuccessful,’ said Jamie Hurworth, a defamation specialist for law firm Payne Hicks Beach.

‘One of the first steps will be for the Court to determine how a reasonable reader would have interpreted the allegations on the banner which included an image of a gun being held to a player’s head, and whether that allegation is defamatory.

‘There will also be a potentially novel legal issue to address given the banner was held up by Crystal Palace fans, rather than perhaps any allegations being made by or on behalf of the club itself.’

Crystal Palace have declined to comment.

Sports.title: Man United's lack of transfer business risks undermining all their good work under Ineos. It's time to back up talk of grand plans with action - or fans' patience will run out, writes NATHAN SALT
Sports.content:
Heading into the summer transfer window, the expectation outside of Manchester United was that this was a club ready to splash the cash. A third-place finish - and crucially a return to Champions League football - was to be supplemented by a record-breaking access fee for Amazon’s All or Nothing documentary, a record training kit sponsorship with Betway, upticks in sponsorship deals with existing partners and huge salaries for the likes of Casemiro and Jadon Sancho now officially off the books. All signs pointed to a £200million midfield rebuild, with players of the quality of Elliot Anderson, Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes, Mateus Fernandes and Aurelien Tchouameni on the shortlist, to help transform United back into one of England and Europe’s elite. After the club's newlook recruitment team hit the mark with four summer signings a year ago, transforming the club’s fortunes in attack and in goal, excitement was through the roof. But now, as United’s players and staff enjoy a five-day training and team-bonding retreat in Ireland, fingers are again being pointed at the powers-that-be by supporters. Just how serious are you about competing with the very best? Man United's decision-makers (from left to right) Sir Jim Ratcliffe, Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox are starting to come under pressure from fans over a lack of transfer activity Actions speak louder than words There are a handful of things that Ineos and the decision-makers at Manchester United love. They love to tell supporters about the ‘clear plan’ to take them back to contending for Premier League titles. They love self-imposed frugality and how that shift in approach no longer leaves United open to being a pawn in the game of chess that is the transfer window. And they love project players in the mould of Chido Obi, Ayden Heaven, Sekou Kone, Enzo Kana-Biyik, Diego Leon, Cristian Orozco and Tynan Thompson. ‘We have a clear plan,’ director of football Jason Wilcox said back in October. ‘I am sure there are going to be bumps in the road but we have just got to make sure we stay calm irrespective of the noise outside.’ Only this summer, that same phrase was repeated by chief executive Omar Berrada through the club’s internal podcast arm Inside Carrington. ‘We have a clear plan,’ Berrada said. ‘[Director of football] Jason Wilcox and his team are well set up to execute that plan. ‘What we saw last season is a good way forward for us. We want a mix of experience and youth. A mix of players who have demonstrated they can perform in the Premier League and players that are doing very well outside the Premier League. ‘Whatever decisions we take will not just be for the short term but the long term.’ The issue Manchester United are facing is that talking about a plan doesn't represent fun for supporters.

Your browser does not support iframes.

Restraint isn’t fun. Projects tend to be a slow process that take years to pay off, with the likes of Leon, Orozco and Kana-Biyik some way off first team football. Fans of any club crave the dopamine rush a new transfer provides. The transfer window has become an addictive loop of rumour and reward, and the absence of business quickly causes inquests online. And there is some legitimacy to the frustrations of many United fans. They didn’t get Anderson, their undisputed No 1 target. He ended up at Manchester City in a £116million record-breaking deal for an English midfielder. An obvious ‘bump in the road’, as Wilcox put it. They didn’t get Mateus Fernandes, a player that felt much more attainable internally before the finances involved exploded and Ineos’ frugality kicked in. He ended up at Tottenham Hotspur for £85million. United were frustrated that the player didn’t push more to end up at Old Trafford. Bruno Guimaraes and Sandro Tonali have both long been admired but figures close to both parties have explained to Daily Mail Sport how any hope United would get close to the financials to land one of Newcastle's star men was quickly extinguished under their new, more austere regime. They ended up at Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur for a combined £175million. ‘We have to be really disciplined. We have a plan, we know what we can invest and we need to stick to it,’ Berrada added back in June. ‘In some cases, we may decide to make an investment knowing it is the right thing, not for the next two or three years but the next ten. ‘We need to stay very focused on what we are trying to achieve. It's very important you don't let the market or the agents dictate what we should be doing.’ The final line is the kicker. In a market where the base price for a good-to-great Premier League midfielder is around £75-80million, United are determined not to fall into the traps of the previous regime, where big-money signings would lead to years of expensive repayments, all for little-to-no on-pitch success. United pivoted to Aston Villa's Youri Tielemans, triggering his release clause. It was a smart signing As was the addition of Andrey Santos from Chelsea. But United need more numbers in midfield So, United pivoted. First to Andrey Santos, a player United first brought up to Chelsea when the terms of Alejandro Garnacho’s move were discussed a year ago, before finally getting him for £50million earlier this summer. Then it was Youri Tielemans, triggering his £35million release clause. Having landed the Premier League's official ‘Signing of the Season’ in Senne Lammens last term, internally there is a belief that his fellow Belgian Tielemans can make it two-for-two in 2026-27. Both are smart signings with huge upside. Adding to Bryan Mbeumo, Matheus Cunha, Benjamin Sesko and Lammens, Ineos can point to a track record of their way being a successful one. Internally, too, there has been a real eagerness to no longer be seen as a club that can be ripped off, a club that agents can manipulate or bully. This was one of the main reasons they didn’t cave on their valuation of Jorge Mendes client Fernandes when Tottenham upped the ante. The desire to limit leaks is stronger than ever, too. Wilcox and Berrada have placed immense emphasis on acting in the shadows and out of the court of public opinion. The Tielemans signing appeared to outsiders to come from nowhere, much to the delight of bosses. They have been decisive in moving on from Rasmus Hojlund, in getting all the wages covered in the loans for Andre Onana (Trabzonspor) and Altay Bayindir (Celta Vigo), and insiders believe United are close to escaping the dreaded cycle of being seen as a poor recruiter, blinded by star power. But with three weeks left to go in this transfer window, Ineos and United’s decision makers are at a crossroads. It’s an expensive market and Michael Carrick needs more. With Champions League football on the horizon, and the first seven games coming in a 29-day stretch, Carrick needs help. United proved against Paris Saint-Germain in Gothenburg that they are ready to be aggressive on the pitch, with their exciting style of play. The question now is, can Ineos be aggressive off it? With his team set to play seven games in the first 29 days of the new season, Michael Carrick needs more quality players to call upon So, where do they need to strengthen? Signing a left back is absolutely essential. Two enquiries to Newcastle United for Lewis Hall – both strongly rebuffed – show that United know that, too. For as much credit as Luke Shaw deserves for starting every single Premier League game last season, asking him to replicate it amid the added strain of European football feels like wishful thinking. The options in front of United are to make a big play for Hall, a player that could be United’s and England’s left back for the next decade. Newcastle will want record money for a full back. That won’t change. Or there is the youth route, promoting Harry Amass, who has looked bright during pre-season. Yet he has been told his best chance for regular game-time is elsewhere. United are understood to be open to both loan and permanent deals. And then there is the cheap option of keeping faith with Shaw and leaning on Noussair Mazraoui, who plays left back for Morocco, in case of injury. Luke Shaw deserves credit for starting every Premier League game last season. But to expect him to do the same in 2026-27 feels like wishful thinking Lewis Hall would be an ambitious and exciting signing at left back. But United's efforts so far haven't extended beyond an enquiry Only one of those three options would signal that United are heading towards the very top, and it’s not options two or three. Patrick Dorgu, despite being listed as a defender in every squad list, is only seen as an option further forward on the wing. Then there is the conundrum of the midfield, and whether United do or don’t need a third recruit in that area (they do). Mason Mount, who has been a huge success across pre-season, came off in Gothenburg after 20 minutes and that highlighted the fragility of United’s side just a fortnight out from the season. Mount is popular with every manager he plays under but his reliability is an issue. He has started just 25 league games since joining United for £55million three years ago. Tielemans, as exciting a signing as he is, missed over 20 games with injury last season. Manuel Ugarte is a long-term absentee and the plan was to move him on. Casemiro has gone. Santos is a smart addition and Kobbie Mainoo will rightly be an important figure. But United need another body. Shifting too much onus, too soon onto the likes of Tyler Fletcher, who is expected to be the young midfielder United place the most effort into developing for the first team this season, is unfair. ‘For us to get in the top four and consistently challenge for Champions League places, win the Champions League, win the Premier League, we have got to invest in the squad,’ Wilcox said back in that October sit-down. ‘We have got to buy the right players.’ And so far they’ve done that. Of the 13 first-team signings to this point under Ineos, only Ugarte has proven a major disappointment. In bringing in (from left) Bryan Mbeumo, Benjamin Sesko and Matheus Cunha last summer, Ineos worked wonders in the transfer market. But they need to be more active this time around But if Project 150 – the stated aim of winning the Premier League title by 2028 in United’s 150th anniversary year – is legitimate and not just a piece of catchy PR, United face a defining three weeks to set the tone for where they are going. Ineos deserve trust and patience to navigate ‘bumps in the road’ after their success in moving on the deadwood, bringing down the wage bill, transforming the team’s fortunes with hits in the transfer market, and committing to plans for a new stadium. But patience doesn’t last for ever and if, in three weeks' time, United are still light in midfield, relying on Shaw as a sole left back option, and there is no back-up to Sesko, don’t be surprised if many fans' patience has run out.

Sports.title: Newcastle suffer ANOTHER transfer market setback as talks with Pierre Emile Hojbjerg break down - with French club Marseille left furious at ex-Tottenham man's change of heart
Sports.content:
Newcastle are exploring other options after their move for Marseille midfielder Pierre Emile Hojbjerg broke down on Monday.

The Denmark international had been identified as the experienced organiser that suited the plans of new boss Matthias Jaissle and talks had initially gone well but the 31-year-old changed his mind over the deal.

Daily Mail Sport understands Marseille's owners have been left furious by this change of heart. The French club, keen to raise funds for their own summer spending, provisionally agreed to selling the Dane to the Toon.

Newcastle had also considered Bayern Munich's Joao Palhinha as a potential back-up but after putting in effort on Hojbjerg, that has left the door open for Aston Villa to step up their negotiations with the Portuguese.

Hojbjerg is considering his options with AC Milan also understood to be interested if he decides against staying with Marseille.

Palhinha, also 31, has also become a target for Villa after Amadou Onana suffered an anterior cruciate ligament injury at the World Cup.

Villa director of football Damian Vidagany told German outlet Bild: 'Joao Palhinha is a very good player who would fit our plans. We are in talks, but there is currently no agreement. If something were to happen, it would always be based on the great respect we have for Bayern.'

Talks had initially gone well but the 31-year-old changed his mind over the Newcastle deal

They have also missed out on top targets including Spain winger Victor Munoz, who opted to join Liverpool

Villa lost 2-1 to Bayern in a pre-season friendly in Hong Kong over the weekend and Palhinha came on as a substitute.

It is proving to be a summer of unrest for Newcastle, who have sold club captain Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal, star forward Anthony Gordon to Barcelona, and midfielder Sandro Tonali to Tottenham.

Eddie Howe, the manager who saved them from relegation before transforming them into a Champions League club and their 56-year major trophy drought, then stepped down on July 31.

They have also missed out on top targets such as Spain winger Victor Munoz and Switzerland midfielder Johan Manzambi, who opted to join Liverpool and Aston Villa respectively.

Howe has since been replaced by a Jaissle, who joins from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli. The 38-year-old's previous coaching experiences include a two-year spell at RB Salzburg preceded by a short-term stint at Austrian side Liefering.

They have recouped north of £250million following the sales of Gordon, Tonali and Guimaraes and have made five signings this summer - goalkeepers Lukas Hornicek and Ewen Jaouen, midfielders Aladji Bamba and Sean Steur and forward Bazoumana Toure.

Sporting director Ross Wilson is prioritising a midfield addition and a new full-back, with signings beyond that dependent on Jaissle’s assessment of what his squad then needs.

It is proving to be a summer of unrest for Newcastle, who have sold club captain Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal and have also lost key players in Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon too

Midfielder Joe Willock will join Besiktas if they meet Newcastle’s asking price, and sources believe there will likely be progress on that front. Goalkeeper Nick Pope has also been told he can leave and, while no offer has yet arrived, both Ipswich and Celtic are said to be monitoring his situation.

Meanwhile, Newcastle expect midfielder Lewis Miley to be fit for the season opener against Liverpool after recovering from a broken leg, but the game will come too soon for Tino Livramento.

The England defender is currently in the United States as he continues his rehabilitation from the calf injury that ruled him out of the World Cup. He could return on the second weekend of the campaign at Tottenham.

Sports.title: Donald Trump warns FIFA it would be a 'terrible mistake' to oust Gianni Infantino as he throws his support behind 'fantastic' under pressure president amid deception allegations
Sports.content:
Donald Trump is backing FIFA president Gianni Infantino's highly controversial re-election bid by predicting financial doom for the organization if it fails to return his friend and supporter to office for another four-year term.

'FIFA would be making a terrible mistake if, for any reason, they even considered replacing President Gianni Infantino,' the US President wrote on Truth Social. 'He is fantastic, having just presided over the most successful World Cup, by four times, ever presented. If he is gone, it will never be as successful or profitable again! Thank you for your attention to this matter. President DJT.'

The 'four times' mention appears to be a reference to the 2026 World Cup viewership, which more than doubled the television audiences for the 2022 event in Qatar.

But not even Trump's support may be enough to save Infantino, who was accused of deception in a joint statement Monday from UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) and CONCACAF, which governs the sport in the Caribbean as well as North and Central America.

The governing bodies claimed Infantino broke trust 'through deception' with the now-abandoned proposal to sell stakes in the World Cup to private equity investors including Joshua Kusher, the brother of Trump's son-in-law, Jared.

Furthermore, Infantino 'placed himself above the collective,' according to the three confederations, which called for a fully independent review of his conduct.

President Donald Trump is backing Gianni Infantino's re-election bid by predicting financial doom for FIFA if it fails return his friend and supporter to office for another four-year term

Trump has been repeatedly congratulating Infantino in the success of the 2026 World Cup

Joshua Kushner was said to be among the potential investors in World Cup stakes

'Football's strength has always been its unity,' the statement concluded. 'We call for that unity to be honored now, for leadership that serves football, not seeks to command it.'

FIFA released a statement on Saturday criticizing a 'concerted and ongoing effort' to 'undermine' both the organisation and Infantino.

UEFA announced on Thursday that they will continue to boycott FIFA competitions if Infantino remains at the top of world football after his scandalous plans to sell $4.2 billion (£3.1billion) in World Cup stakes to private investors collapsed. Meanwhile, Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) president Lise Klaveness called for him to resign on Friday.

Mexico's football federation broke ranks with CONCACAF to come out in support of Infantino, with Argentina, Qatar, Paraguay, Morocco and Egypt among those in favour of him remaining as FIFA president.

Infantino has also faced allegations this week that UEFA made a 'departure payment' to a female employee with whom he is alleged to have been in a relationship while general secretary of European football's governing body.

UEFA confirmed a payment was made, but FIFA labeled the allegation as 'categorically untrue.'

The next FIFA presidential elections take place next March.

Infantino talks to Trump's son-in-law, Jared Kushner, whose brother Joshua was a potential investor in FIFA's now-abandoned plan to sell World Cup stakes to private equity groups

Prior to Trump’s Truth Social post, Infantino was said to be in talks with the White House on the best way to save his job, the New York Post reported.

As an insider told the Post: 'He wanted to get online with [Secretary of State Marco Rubio] and talk about how soccer can be a form of soft power for America. But we all know that it is about job protection. It is not about anything else at this point.'

A second source described Infantino as feeling 'isolated' by the 'avalanche' of negativity surrounding his now-doomed plans. 'He is looking for allies of note to publicly support him,' they said.

The Daily Mail reached out to FIFA and the White House for comment but did not receive a response. Meanwhile on X, the Assistant Secretary of State for Global Public Affairs, Dylan Johnson, denied that a call would take place.

He posted: 'There are no plans for [Marco Rubio] to speak with Infantino and there is no call this morning. [The New York Post] should check their sources or they could have just asked us.'

Infantino was reportedly seeking support from Secretary of State Marco Rubio (center)

Join the discussion Should FIFA¿s future be shaped by controversial leaders or bold moves for unity and transparency?

On Tuesday, a FIFA spokesperson told the Daily Mail: 'The FIFA President has not made any call to the US President, or any members of his administration, in recent days. It is pure fiction.'

Infantino's alleged last-ditch attempt to save his presidency came after Trump brutally denied all knowledge of Infantino's bold sell-off plan.

When asked 'did Mr Infantino speak to you about his proposal to sell a stake in the World Cup?' Trump brutally first replied: 'Who?'

After the question was repeated, the president then added: 'No, I didn't speak to him.'

Trump's reaction to Infantino in that Oval Office media session was a far cry from previous comments before and during the World Cup, in which he often gave a glowing review of the FIFA boss.

The Post also reported that Infantino repeatedly tried to call Trump amid the controversy, only to be met with a wall of silence from the president, who received FIFA's inaugural peace prize last year.

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury ultimatum issued - 'There will be no fight'
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury ultimatum issued - 'There will be no fight'

Joshua and Fury are contracted to meet in the UK later this year but Netflix, and the fight's Saudi backers, want to host it at Madison Square Garden on November 20

View Image Tyson Fury is due to fight Anthony Joshua (Image: Tyson Fury/Instagram)

Eddie Hearn insists he will pull the plug on Anthony Joshua's fight with Tyson Fury if New York is announced as the venue without a change of contract.

‌



Joshua and Fury are contracted to meet in the UK later this year but Netflix, and the fight's Saudi backers, want to host it at Madison Square Garden on November 20. But Hearn insists he and Joshua want the fight to be held at Wembley and is refusing to back down in the row.

‌



"Everybody wants to do the fight in New York, apart from Anthony Joshua and me," he told The Punch Podcast. "We're under a huge amount of pressure, and we're being told by Turki Alshikh and those guys - Netflix particularly - 'Look, we really want to do the fight in the US.' It's almost not a 'please Eddie,' but like, 'We're partners. We're paying a lot of money. Come on, you have to understand that we need to put the fight where we feel is commercially the best place.'

‌



Anthony Joshua sets out demands to move Tyson Fury fight to New York READ MORE :

Tyson Fury's stance on Anthony Joshua fight venue becomes clear READ MORE :

"I don't agree with their arguments, but I'm not the one paying the money. However, we wouldn't have signed the contract if the fight was in America, so we have to have a discussion around that. Then you've got Nick Khan phoning me up from TKO and Zuffa, saying, "Come on, can we be involved?" And I'm like, "What? Why? Why would I let you be involved?" "Well, we think we can make the fight bigger," and blah, blah, blah.

"Okay, if you tell me some reasons why I should let you be involved... Are you going to let me be involved in the next Conor McGregor fight in the UFC? No, of course not. So what? But I'm also not stubborn enough to just say no; I'll listen. The other day, though, they wrote to us and said, 'Just to let you know, we'd like to announce the fight for New York.' I said, 'No. You can't.'

Article continues below

"By the way, there might even be a situation where they go ahead and announce it anyway, and you'll probably see me come out quite quickly and say, 'No fight.' Because I promise you, if they announce that fight without an agreement in place to change the venue, there will be no fight, and we ain't bluffing.

"We feel really strongly that this fight should be in the UK. I've also said many times that I want it to work for everybody. Turki is spending a lot of money on this fight, if you really feel that commercially you're going to be so much better off doing it in America."

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Bradley Barcola 'gives transfer green light' and star joins up with squad
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Bradley Barcola 'gives transfer green light' and star joins up with squad

Liverpool are gearing up for the return of the Premier League with some pre-season fixtures at Anfield

View 3 Images Bradley Barcola has reportedly said 'yes' to Liverpool (Image: FRANCK FIFE / AFP via Getty Images)

Liverpool have one more hurdle to overcome in their pursuit of Bradley Barcola as Andoni Iraola looks to seal a much-needed attacking signing. A winger is high up on the Reds' priority list as the new manager confirms it is an "obvious situation" the club needs to address.

‌



The new manager discussed the need to sign attacking stars in July, admitting that the Reds will need to be flexible in the transfer market. He said: "No, I think it’s difficult to say a number when the market is open, and you have to be always open to new options to improve the squad. There are obvious situations that we know where we need to sign players. A winger, for example – we definitely need to sign a winger.

‌



"But there are other situations that we will have to analyse what the market gives you, what’s the cost, how we also see the players we have. We have some tricky positions where we have injured players that we trust but is still not the ideal situation. So, it will depend on a lot of things."

‌



While transfers are very much on the agenda over the next few weeks, Iraola has also welcomed back an important member of the Liverpool squad from an extended summer break. Here, Mirror Football has the latest coming out of Anfield.

Bradley Barcola green-lights transfer

View 3 Images Bradley Barcola is keen on a move to Anfield (Image: Aurelien Meunier - PSG/PSG via Getty Images)

Bradley Barcola has reportedly green-lit a move to Liverpool after agreeing personal terms. Fabrizio Romano reports the two clubs are in "direct, official conversation" and the Ligue 1 side's £145million valuation remains unchanged.

Speaking on his YouTube channel, he reports that the two clubs are in 'daily talks' and while they are yet to strike an agreement on financial terms, PSG's potential move for Barcelona forward Ferran Torres could faciliatate Barcola's switch to Liverpool.

Sports.title: Arsenal mocked for eyeing up Vinicius Jnr transfer - 'You're not one of the big boys'
Sports.content:
Arsenal mocked for eyeing up Vinicius Jnr transfer - 'You're not one of the big boys'

Arsenal eyed up a blockbuster move for Vinicius Junior this summer but the Real Madrid star ultimately decided to stay put - and the Premier League side have since been mocked

View 2 Images Jon Obi Mikel has poked fun at Arsenal's standing as they looked to prise Vinicius Jnr from Real Madrid (Image: The Obi One Podcast)

Arsenal have been told they're not "one of the big boys" by John Obi Mikel, who has mocked them for believing they could ever sign Vinicius Junior.

‌



The Gunners were heavily linked with the Brazilian earlier this summer in what would've been a club-record move. Vinicius' contract was winding down and the Premier League champions were looking to seize on the uncertainty.

‌



It would've been a blockbuster transfer had Arsenal pulled it off, but the player ultimately decided to extend his stay at the Bernabeu, leaving the north Londoners to look elsewhere in a bid to bolster their forward line.

‌



But Mikel has laughed off the idea that Vinicius was ever going to move to Arsenal, insisting the club have got above their station after winning a first league title in two decades whilst still awaiting their first ever Champions League triumph.

Arsenal get significant Julian Alvarez transfer update after Atletico Madrid meeting READ MORE :

The former Chelsea midfielder said on The Obi One Podcast: "I don’t know what the Arsenal fans were expecting. You win the league after 22 years and then you all of a sudden think: that’s it, you’ve arrived, you’re one of the big boys again. No, you’re not.

"They’ve just been humbled because I said it: there’s no way Vinicius Junior is leaving Real Madrid to go to Arsenal, a club that’s won one title in 22 years. This guy wins titles, he’s won lots of titles at Real Madrid. He wants to win titles season after season, the Champions League, La Liga, competing year after year and winning those titles.

‌



"He’s tasted what it feels like winning the Champions League, Arsenal have never won the Champions League. Zero. You expect a player who has won the Champions League with Real Madrid to leave that."

View 2 Images Vinicius Jnr has chosen to remain with Real Madrid (Image: Antonio Villalba/Real Madrid via Getty Images)

Mikel believes that Real Madrid, who have Jose Mourinho at the helm once again, are assembling a team that can challenge for Europe's highest honour once again. They've already signed the likes of Ibrahima Konate, Marc Cucurella, Bernardo Silva and Yan Diomande.

Article continues below

Arsenal meanwhile have looked to build on their champion year and added Bruno Guimaraes at the weekend. The former Newcastle midfielder is their biggest capture of the summer so far, at £75m, and they're still in the market for a major frontline signing.

Sports.title: What's happening with Marcus Rashford? Man Utd return, transfer stance, telling gesture
Sports.content:
What's happening with Marcus Rashford? Man Utd return, transfer stance, telling gesture

Marcus Rashford's future remains the topic of plenty of speculation as he returns to Manchester United after spending last season out on loan

View 3 Images Marcus Rashford has rejoined his Manchester United team-mates after a spell out on loan (Image: Richard Sellers/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images)

A few months ago, the idea of Marcus Rashford returning to the fold at Manchester United looked far-fetched. Strange things can happen in football, though, and the England international's Old Trafford comeback is right up there

‌



Rashford spent last season on loan at Barcelona and looked poised for a permanent move to Spotify Camp Nou. However, the Catalan club let their £26m option expire.

‌



For as long as Ruben Amorim was in the United dugout, a return for the forward looked impossible. However, the arrival of Michael Carrick - a former team-mate of Rashford - has altered the picture.

‌



England's run to the World Cup semi-finals meant a later return for the 28-year-old than for some of his colleagues. Now, though, Rashford's future is very much at the forefront of discussions.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd given Benjamin Sesko reality check after Bayern Munich transfer links READ MORE :

Man Utd return

Following United's 1-1 draw with PSG on Saturday, Carrick confirmed that Rashford has returned as part of his first team group, alongside Kobbie Mainoo.

‌



“We have got a full squad this week in Dublin. We fly straight there and have a few days where we have the whole group back together," United's manager said. “Marcus is part of that, and Kobbie and Lisandro [Martinez]. We look forward to seeing them.”

View 3 Images Rashford has joined the United camp in Dublin (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Get Man United's new 2026/27 home kit This article contains affiliate links, we will receive a commission on any sales we generate from it. Learn more £85 Fanatics Buy Now on Fanatics Product Description Manchester United have launched their new home kit for the 2026/27 season, i nspired by the club's heritage and featuring a classic polo collar with iconic adidas details.

‌



As reported by the MEN, the England pair joined Benjamin Sesko, Senne Lammens, Matheus Cunha, Matthijs de Ligt, Karl Darlow, JJ Gabriel and Tynan Thompson on a private jet to Dublin. Some of those players could play a part in United's midweek friendly with Leeds, with Martinez also expected in Dublin.

Transfer stance

Rashford is not interested in moving to Turkey or Saudi Arabia, thereby limiting his options. He would only join a European side who can offer him Champions League football. There are only so many clubs capable of meeting the forward's demands and one of them, Barcelona, are already out of the running barring a big U-turn.

The fee might not be a huge obstacle, with the MEN suggesting £25m - a little less than the provisional sum agreed with Barca - potentially enough to do it. However, those close to Rashford are said to have suggested United are no longer desperate to sell.

‌



Rashford will be with the rest of the squad for United's final two pre-season friendlies, against Leeds on Wednesday and AC Milan on Saturday, and is expected to be around for the Premier League opener away at Hull on August 22.

View 3 Images Barcelona allowed their £26m transfer option to expire (Image: Aitor Alcalde Colomer/Getty Images)

Telling gesture

While some fans are prepared to wait and see when it comes to Rashford's future, others have been looking for clues wherever they can find them. One such clue comes on the squad number front, where the forward is set to wear No. 14 next term.

Article continues below

United have already given Matheus Cunha the No. 10 previously worn by the England international and there are no indications it will revert back to its previous owner. Rashford wore No. 14 at Barcelona, though, and the choice can be read as an indication that the club and Carrick consider him part of their plans.

The No. 14 shirt was vacant for United last season. The number was not reused when Christian Eriksen left the club, while previous holders include Jesse Lingard and Javier Hernandez.
