The report identified widespread weaknesses in STAR-P’s asset management system.

Among the deficiencies were incomplete fixed asset registers, failure to update newly acquired assets, lack of periodic physical verification, and absence of asset coding.

The audit cited assets valued at US$46,719, including laptops, printers, projectors, office furniture and computers, that were either improperly recorded or omitted from the register.

Although management submitted an updated asset register after the audit, the Auditor General said it still lacked critical information required under public financial management regulations.

Missing and Unverified Beneficiary Assets

Field verification exercises also uncovered concerns regarding assets purchased for beneficiaries under the Liberia Agriculture Commercialization Fund (LACF).

The audit reported that assets worth US$33,500, including cold storage facilities, solar systems, greenhouses and motorcycles, could not be physically verified.

Another US$1,680 solar system procured for a beneficiary had not been put into use, while assets worth US$68,000 supplied to a beneficiary in Grand Bassa County—including trucks, motor tricycles, processing equipment and palm oil machinery—had not been coded for identification.

The GAC concluded that management failed to adequately account for the missing assets or explain why some equipment remained unused.

Management attributed the challenges to decentralized project implementation, incomplete records and logistical difficulties, and said it has begun reconciling assets, strengthening asset tracking and revising its fixed asset management policies.

The Auditor General maintained the findings and called for a joint physical verification exercise with the GAC within one month after submission of the report to the Legislature.

Construction Projects Behind Schedule

The audit further found that US$57,960 had been paid for construction projects that remained incomplete well beyond approved timelines.

The affected projects include a warehouse in Lofa County and a palm oil factory in Grand Bassa County, both of which were still unfinished during GAC’s field verification in May 2026.

Management blamed contractor capacity limitations, adverse weather, rising construction costs and logistical challenges, and said stronger contract monitoring and milestone-based payment systems have since been introduced.

Digital Lending Platform Still Missing

One of the audit’s most significant findings involved an online digital lending platform intended to support farmers through CitiTrust Savings and Loans.

According to the report, US$36,768—representing full payment under the service agreement—was disbursed for the design and implementation of the platform.

However, during physical verification in May 2026, auditors found no evidence that the integrated digital lending system had been deployed or was operational, despite contractual deadlines indicating it should have gone live by May 2025.

Management acknowledged implementation delays, citing software customization requirements, connectivity problems and technical capacity constraints. Officials said the software would be fully integrated before the service agreement expires.

Dashboard and Project Assets Not Handed Over

The GAC also found that the Liberia Agriculture Commercialization Fund’s reporting dashboard and other digital assets were never formally transferred to the Ministry following the expiration of the Fund Manager’s contract.

Auditors warned that the missing dashboard could undermine institutional memory, beneficiary tracking and project reporting.

Management said discussions are underway with the former Fund Manager to complete the handover of databases, user credentials and reporting tools, while committing to strengthen future contractual handover requirements.

Auditor General Maintains Key Findings

While STAR-P management accepted most of the recommendations and outlined corrective measures, the Auditor General maintained several key findings, particularly regarding missing beneficiary assets and incomplete documentation.

The GAC said it will conduct follow-up reviews during subsequent audits to determine whether the Ministry of Agriculture has implemented the recommended reforms aimed at strengthening governance, procurement, financial accountability and project oversight.

World.title: Liberia: EU-Funded Seeds4Liberia Project Hands Over Agricultural Inputs to Boost Local Certified Seed Production
World.content:
Speaking at the event , the project’s National Coordinator /AfricaRice Country Representative to Liberia Moustapha Gaye described the event as more than the distribution of agricultural inputs, saying it reflects the strong partnership between the Government of Liberia, the European Union and the consortium of AfricaRice, the International Institute of Tropical Agriculture (IITA) and WorldFish

MONROVIA –The European Union-funded Seeds4Liberia Project and partners recently handed over improved seeds, seedlings, fish fingerlings and agricultural machinery to local seed enterprises.

Items handed over included power tillers, lowland and upland rice seeders, rice reapers, hermetic cocoons with ECOWAS monitoring systems, hermetic bags, catfish fry, tilapia fry, mixer machines for fish feed production, a feed pellet mill, hapa net, sechi disks, a scale, foundation seeds, and cuttings.

The hand over ceremongy took place last week at the Central Agricultural Research Institute (CARI), with stakeholders calling on farmers to use the inputs responsibly to strengthen Liberia’s food security and agricultural productivity.

Speaking at the event , the project’s National Coordinator /AfricaRice Country Representative to Liberia Moustapha Gaye described the event as more than the distribution of agricultural inputs, saying it reflects the strong partnership between the Government of Liberia, the European Union and the consortium of AfricaRice, the International Institute of Tropical Agriculture (IITA) and WorldFish.

“Today’s event represents much more than the distribution of agricultural inputs,” Gaye said. “It reflects the strong partnership between the Government of Liberia, the European Union and the consortium of AfricaRice, IITA and WorldFish, working together to strengthen Liberia’s agricultural sector and improve the livelihoods of farmers across the country.”

He thanked the European Union for financing the Seeds4Liberia Project, saying the investment is helping strengthen Liberia’s seed systems, improve farmers’ access to quality planting materials, promote sustainable agricultural technologies and create opportunities for increased productivity and food security.

Gaye also acknowledged national partners including, the Ministry of Agriculture, CARI, the Seed Development and Certification Agency (SDCA), the Liberia Agricultural Commodity Regulatory Authority (LACRA), the National Fisheries and Aquaculture Authority (NAFAA), county authorities and other development partners, for supporting the project’s implementation

Gaye also acknowledged national partners including, the Ministry of Agriculture, CARI, the Seed Development and Certification Agency (SDCA), the Liberia Agricultural Commodity Regulatory Authority (LACRA), the National Fisheries and Aquaculture Authority (NAFAA), county authorities and other development partners, for supporting the project’s implementation.

He urged beneficiaries to maximize the use of the agricultural inputs distributed under the project.

“The seeds, seedlings, and equipment being handed over today are not an end in themselves. They are tools that will enable farmers, seed enterprises and producer organizations to increase production, improve quality, create businesses and generate income,” Gaye said.

He emphasized that the project’s long-term success will depend on continued collaboration among research institutions, government agencies, the private sector, extension services and farmers to ensure that improved technologies remain sustainable beyond the life of the project.

Also speaking, the European Union Programme Officer for Agriculture Antonio Di Clemente said the Seeds4Liberia Project is intended to build resilient seed systems for rice, cassava, soybean, coffee and fish value chains to strengthen food security and promote economic diversification.

According to Di Clemente, the project seeks to strengthen institutional capacity to produce and regulate high-quality breeder seeds, seedlings and fish while empowering private-sector and community-based enterprises to produce, store and market certified seeds and quality fish fingerlings

He said the initiative has also operationalized the Seed Development and Certification Agency to improve national quality assurance systems, promote high-yielding and climate-resilient crop varieties, provide practical training for farmers and students, and strengthen market linkages through partnerships between seed producers, buyers and financial institutions.

Additionally, the Assistant Minister for Planning and Development at the Ministry of Agriculture, Francis Mulbah, described the ceremony as another demonstration of the Liberian government’s commitment to revitalizing the country’s agricultural sector.

Mulbah reaffirmed the ministry’s commitment to working with development partners to improve agricultural production through the distribution of quality seeds and planting materials.

The EU-funded Seeds4Liberia Project is jointly implemented by Africa Rice Center (AfricaRice), the International Institute of Tropical Agriculture (IITA), and WorldFish in collaboration with the Ministry of Agriculture (MoA), the Central Agricultural Research Institute (CARI), the National Fisheries and Aquaculture Authority (NaFAA), the Seed Development and Certification Agency (SDCA), and the Liberia Agricultural Commodity Regulatory Authority (LACRA)

Also speaking, Farmers Union of Liberia Director Josephine Francis urged farmers’ cooperatives and federations to take ownership of agricultural projects to ensure their long-term sustainability.

“I always tell our farmers and their families to take ownership,” Francis said. “When you take ownership of projects that come to your cooperatives and federations, that is what makes them successful.”

She encouraged farmers to use the improved planting materials responsibly and highlighted the growing economic potential of soybean production, noting that Liberia has an existing market that imports thousands of tons annually.

Francis also praised the introduction of seven improved cassava varieties under the project and urged farmers to learn the characteristics of each variety to maximize yields.

Project organizers commended CARI, under the leadership of Director General Dr. Arthur Bob Karnuah, for hosting the ceremony and serving as a key technical partner in strengthening Liberia’s national seed systems and promoting improved agricultural technologies.

They also recognized the contributions of SDCA, LACRA, NAFAA, IITA, WorldFish and other implementing partners for supporting the initiative.

Beneficiaries, in turn, thanked the Ministry of Agriculture, the European Union and project partners for providing the agricultural inputs and equipment, pledging to use them to improve production and strengthen their livelihoods.

The EU-funded Seeds4Liberia Project is jointly implemented by Africa Rice Center (AfricaRice), the International Institute of Tropical Agriculture (IITA), and WorldFish in collaboration with the Ministry of Agriculture (MoA), the Central Agricultural Research Institute (CARI), the National Fisheries and Aquaculture Authority (NaFAA), the Seed Development and Certification Agency (SDCA), and the Liberia Agricultural Commodity Regulatory Authority (LACRA).

The initiative aims to strengthen food production, improve rural livelihoods and reduce Liberia’s dependence on imported agricultural commodities through improved seed systems, climate-resilient technologies and stronger public-private partnerships.

World.title: Liberia: Rep. Fahnbulleh Reaffirms Support for China Union Workers in Bong Mines Engagement
World.content:
The lawmaker said his engagement with the workers and residents was also aimed at strengthening cooperation between his office and the people of the district. He maintained that meaningful representation goes beyond legislative duties and requires regular consultation with constituents, particularly workers and communities whose livelihoods are directly connected to economic activities taking place within the district

BONG MINES, Bong County — Representative Foday Fahnbulleh of District Seven in Bong County has reaffirmed his commitment to protecting the interests of residents and Liberian workers in his district, following an engagement Saturday with members of a local cooperative and workers of the China Union Concession Company in Bong Mines, Fuamah District.

By Selma Lomax, [email protected]

Rep. Fahnbulleh, who represents Fuamah and Sanoyea Districts, the two administrative districts that constitute electoral District Seven, held the engagement as part of his continued interaction with constituents to hear directly from them about the challenges confronting them and to discuss possible ways of addressing issues affecting their livelihoods and welfare.

During the meeting, Rep. Fahnbulleh said the engagement was intended to provide an opportunity for residents and workers to speak openly about their concerns while giving him a better understanding of the challenges they face. He said as an elected representative, he considers it his responsibility to remain accessible to the people and to ensure that their concerns are not ignored after they have brought them to his attention.

“As your representative, my responsibility is to listen to you, understand the challenges you are facing and stand with you as we work toward finding fair and lasting solutions. I want you to know that you have my fullest support, particularly when it comes to protecting your rights and interests,” Rep. Fahnbulleh told the gathering.

The lawmaker said his engagement with the workers and residents was also aimed at strengthening cooperation between his office and the people of the district. He maintained that meaningful representation goes beyond legislative duties and requires regular consultation with constituents, particularly workers and communities whose livelihoods are directly connected to economic activities taking place within the district.

Rep. Fahnbulleh said he would continue to engage relevant stakeholders whenever issues affecting workers and residents arise, stressing that accountability and fairness must remain central to efforts to address concerns in the community. He said he would work alongside the people to seek practical solutions rather than simply listen to their complaints without follow-up.

“We cannot claim to represent our people effectively if we are not prepared to stand with them when they raise legitimate concerns. I am committed to engaging the appropriate stakeholders, advocating for fairness and ensuring that the voices of our people are heard,” he said.

The Bong County lawmaker further assured the workers that his support for them would not be limited to a single meeting, emphasizing that he intends to maintain an open channel of communication with workers and residents.

According to him, sustained engagement is necessary to identify problems early, encourage accountability and prevent issues affecting workers and communities from being left unresolved.

He said the people of Fuamah and Sanoyea deserve representation that is responsive to their concerns and focused on advancing their collective interests. Rep. Fahnbulleh also encouraged residents and workers to continue communicating their challenges to his office, noting that constructive engagement provides an avenue for issues to be addressed through dialogue and appropriate institutional channels.

“My commitment is to work with you, not above you. I want our people to feel that their representative is available to them, that their concerns matter and that there is someone willing to carry their issues to the appropriate level whenever necessary,” Rep. Fahnbulleh said.

The lawmaker also called for unity among residents and workers, stressing that the collective interests of the district should remain at the center of discussions involving employment, workers’ welfare, community development and other issues affecting the people. He said disagreements and challenges should be addressed through constructive dialogue and a shared commitment to finding solutions that are fair to all sides.

“Our collective interest must guide us. Where there are challenges, we should sit together, identify the issues, demand accountability where necessary and work toward solutions that protect the dignity and interests of our people,” Rep. Fahnbulleh added.

The engagement was welcomed by Liberian workers who described the lawmaker’s willingness to meet with them and listen to their concerns as an important part of effective representation. The workers said Rep. Fahnbulleh’s presence demonstrated a willingness to maintain direct contact with constituents and to understand the realities they face in their workplaces and communities.

One of the workers said Rep. Fahnbulleh’s engagement was encouraging because it gave them an opportunity to communicate their concerns directly to their elected representative rather than relying solely on intermediaries.

“We appreciate Representative Fahnbulleh for coming to meet with us and giving us the opportunity to speak about the issues that concern us. It is important for workers to know that their representative is willing to listen,” the worker said.

Another worker praised Rep. Fahnbulleh for what the worker described as his continued willingness to stand with Liberian workers and residents of the district. The worker said the engagement demonstrated that the lawmaker was interested in understanding the challenges facing ordinary people and advocating for their interests.

“We are encouraged by the fact that our lawmaker is engaging us directly. We want him to continue standing with the workers and carrying our concerns to the appropriate authorities whenever necessary,” the worker said.

A third worker said the meeting had strengthened their confidence that their concerns could receive attention through sustained engagement and advocacy. The worker stressed that workers need representatives who are prepared to listen and follow up on issues affecting their welfare.

“What we need is someone who will listen to us and help ensure that our concerns are properly addressed. We thank Representative Fahnbulleh for coming to us, listening to us and reassuring us of his support,” he said.

World.title: International Rights Groups Raise Alarm Over Freedom of Religion and Expression in South Korea
World.content:
SEOUL, South Korea — Human Rights Without Frontiers (HRWF), together with CAP Liberté de Conscience (CAP LC), which has accredited ECOSOC status at the United Nations, FOREF, CESNUR and Bitter Winter, held a press conference today at the Seoul Foreign Correspondents’ Club on Freedom of Religion or Belief and Freedom of Expression in South Korea.

The issues addressed included concerns about the treatment of elderly religious leaders in pretrial detention, including questions of proportionality, humanitarian considerations, and due process.

The organizations called on South Korean authorities to review the detention of 95-year-old Shincheonji Chairman Lee Man-hee and to ensure that the legal and administrative response to religious minorities remains neutral, proportionate, and consistent with South Korea’s international human-rights obligations, including with respect to 83-year-old Mrs. Hak-ja Han Moon of the Family Federation.

The issues discussed form part of a broader pattern of Freedom of Religion or Belief concerns in South Korea. Concerns have also persisted regarding Segero Church in Busan, which has reportedly continued to face harassment and official scrutiny even after Pastor Son Hyun-bo was released from detention.

Reporting has also raised questions about conscientious objection, public hostility toward a mosque project in Daegu, and religious accommodation in educational settings.

Over the past decades, HRWF has documented the imprisonment of hundreds of Jehovah’s Witnesses in South Korea as conscientious objectors, and although alternative civilian service was later introduced, critics maintain that it has been implemented in a punitive manner rather than as a genuine rights-respecting alternative, notably because it requires 36 months of service in correctional facilities, twice the length of regular military service. Recent court decisions have also upheld key features of that system against constitutional challenge.

Opening the conference, Hans Noot, Associate Director of HRWF, said the issues at stake “lie at the heart of democratic society,” warning that when religious communities are stigmatized, peaceful gatherings are restricted, and dissent is treated as a problem to be contained, the consequences “extend far beyond any single group or case.”

He said the conference was not about defending any one theology or movement, but about “defending a principle: that fundamental rights apply equally to all.”

Thierry Valle, President of CAP Liberté de Conscience, addressed the legality of Chairman Lee’s detention under international law. Referring to South Korea’s ratification of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights in 1990 and the Convention against Torture in 1995, he questioned whether placing a 95-year-old in pretrial detention is consistent with those obligations. He stressed that the presumption of innocence must prevail over any presumption of guilt.

There are alternative more proportionate and more humane measures respecting the presumption of innocence and human dignity in democratic countries. And he cited precedents including Cardinal Joseph Zen’s 2022 release on bail in Hong Kong and Vietnam’s decision to place Buddhist Patriarch Thich Quang Do under house arrest rather than in prison.

Michael Langhans, Executive Director of FOREF Germany, presented a legal analysis questioning whether pretrial detention for Chairman Lee of the Shincheonji Church was necessary given evidence already sufficient for an indictment, and whether that evidence was gathered neutrally rather than through a narrative framing the defendant’s community as a “sect” or “cult.” He argued that the case raises a broader question for lawmakers: whether measures meant to protect fair elections can be applied without nullifying the constitutionally and internationally guaranteed right to freedom of religion.

Márk Nemes, Deputy Director of CESNUR, shared his thoughts on the effects of ongoing persecution and its possible ramifications for minority faiths.

He noted three recent scholarly investigations conducted in selected Shincheonji congregations in Europe, Argentina, and Australia, each finding worrisome increase in hostility toward the otherwise peaceful and cooperative religious movement. He stressed that Shincheonji is not simply a South Korean minority church but a global religious movement with congregations worldwide.

The disproportionate persecution in South Korea affects the lives of those congregants abroad, whose freedoms for expressing and practicing faith, enshrined in ICCPR Articles 18 and 19, are inalienable rights and must be considered during this current process.

Massimo Introvigne, Managing Director of CESNUR and Editor-in-Chief of Bitter Winter, said South Korea “has crossed a worrying line” by arresting Chairman Lee, arguing that international standards such as the Mandela Rules would call for house arrest rather than imprisonment for a 95-year-old accused of a non-violent offence.

He said the charges, tied to ordinary political participation by members of a religious minority, “appear legally and conceptually overstretched,” and warned that the case fits a broader pattern of pressure against minority faiths in the country.

The organizations called on South Korean authorities, the media, and the international community to examine these developments with close attention to due process, proportionality, and the equal protection of fundamental rights, and made further documentation available to support continued reporting.

At the conclusion of the press conference, the scholars in attendance signed an official letter calling on the Government of the Republic of Korea to immediately release Chairman Lee from custody.

World.title: Liberia: Opportunity Network Liberia CEO Survives Serious Road Accident in Margibi
World.content:
Monrovia — The Chief Executive Officer of Opportunity Network Liberia, formerly known as Change Agent Network (CAN), Eric Wowoh, has survived a serious motor accident while traveling to Gbarnga, Bong County to attend a major signing ceremony.

By J.H. Webster Clayeh — [email protected]

The accident occurred Friday, August 7 in Centa Town, Margibi County, when the spring of the vehicle’s left rear tire reportedly broke, causing the vehicle to lose control and overturn into a nearby valley.

Wowoh, who was reportedly driving alone at the time of the incident, was rescued from the wreckage.

Despite the accident, he proceeded to Gbarnga, where he participated in the signing of a 15-year Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) between Opportunity Network Liberia and LICOSESS College of Education.

According to a press release posted on the LICOSESS Facebook page, the agreement provides for the transfer of management and academic leadership of the CAN Leadership Academy School System to LICOSESS College of Education.

The partnership is intended to expand access to quality education while strengthening teacher preparation and educational delivery in Montserrado, Bong and Nimba Counties.

Under the agreement, LICOSESS College of Education will assume responsibility for the academic, administrative, institutional, and quality assurance management of the CAN Leadership Academy school system.

Opportunity Network Liberia, meanwhile, will continue to provide strategic oversight as the founding institution.

The signing ceremony followed a series of transition and turnover meetings conducted on July 30 and 31 at CAN Leadership Academy campuses in Jacob Town, Montserrado County; Gbarnga, Bong County; and Neigbein, Nimba County.

World.title: Hichilema closes 127-rally campaign as 50,000 students march to State House in show of support
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema has completed a nationwide campaign tour covering all 116 districts of Zambia, addressing 127 public rallies since launching his re-election bid on 28 June, as thousands of students marched to State House pledging to deliver him millions of votes ahead of Thursday’s general election.

State House said the tour began with a rally outside the National Heroes Stadium in Lusaka and progressed through all ten provinces, with the President addressing rallies in Central, Copperbelt, Eastern, Muchinga, Northern, Luapula, Lusaka, Southern, Western and North-Western provinces before concluding his final leg in Luapula on 9 August.

More than 50,000 students from over 50 universities and colleges marched to State House grounds on Monday to rally behind the President, drawn from institutions including the University of Zambia, Levy Mwanawasa Medical University, Chalimbana University and the National Institute of Public Administration.

Clad in red and white, the students carried banners praising Hichilema’s record on free education and chanted messages of solidarity as they gathered at the golf course, where the President addressed them amid music and dancing.

“We have an election this week on Thursday, in order to continue expanding education, including support, including private schools, Bally needs to return to this house. You are welcome to State House, your State House, this is the people’s State House,” Hichilema told the students.

He said his administration had already achieved much in its first term but that more work remained. “We started a journey in 2021, restructured the economy, restructured the debt, restructured the mining sector, the energy sector, restructured the education sector, restructuring agriculture, we have done a lot but we still have a lot more to do,” he said.

Hichilema pledged to introduce structured internships for students in their second and third years of study, saying government would attach them to companies so they would have employment secured before graduation. He recalled his own experience of being hired directly out of an internship without waiting for exam results.

The President also said his administration planned to extend student loans to private colleges and universities and confirmed that meal allowances, already restored, would remain in place. He said government intended to expand bursaries, hostel space and sanitation facilities to help students remain healthy while they study.

University of Zambia Students’ Union president Mwanto Kabaso thanked the President for a sanitation overhaul at the institution and for the accommodation allowance increase from K3,900 to K5,850, saying the university’s highest office now felt like “a paradise on earth.”

UNZASU vice-president Jemimah Mwaba, representing the Zambia National Students Union, said the President’s leadership had touched every generation of students, from bursaries and meal allowances to sanitation and support for the elderly through social cash transfers.

National Council of Students’ Unions secretary-general Vincent Sakala said students had resolved to deliver Hichilema at least 5.8 million votes on Thursday, describing the figure as a reflection of the goodwill built up over the President’s five years in office.

Levy Mwanawasa Medical University student union president Brian Malambo said students believed Zambia’s economic future was secure under Hichilema’s plans for youth empowerment, and the university’s students conferred an honorary degree on the President in what they termed “Kwenyunology,” in recognition of his support for student loan extensions to the institution.

State House said the President’s tour had also included stops at the University of Zambia campus on 1 August, where he addressed thousands of students on the grounds ahead of the broader march that followed days later.

With campaigning due to close on Wednesday, the twin events, a completed nationwide rally circuit and a mass student demonstration of support, mark the final push of Hichilema’s re-election bid before Zambians go to the polls on Thursday

World.title: Binwell Mpundu apologises over “ready to kill” remarks as UPND and Church condemn video
World.content:
Tonse Alliance Presidential Affairs Chairman Binwell Mpundu has apologised after a video circulated showing him saying he was “ready to die” and “ready to kill” over the outcome of Thursday’s general election, following days of condemnation from the ruling party, the Church and civil society.

Mpundu made the remarks in a video posted to his Facebook page on Sunday, before deleting it hours later and issuing a follow-up statement claiming his social media account had been hacked and the footage was artificial intelligence.

By Monday, he had shifted his explanation again, telling reporters at a media briefing that the statement was genuine but had been taken out of context. He said the words were meant as an expression of personal conviction rather than a threat against anyone.

“The truth is this is the statement I made. Believe me, to err is human and sometimes you put words in a place that should not be. But this statement is as simple as it should have ever been from where I come from,” Mpundu said.

He compared the remarks to a parent declaring willingness to die for their children, arguing that such language reflects devotion rather than intent to harm. “I made a statement in which I said I am ready to die from my country, I am ready to die for these elections. The statement I am ready to kill is more of a self-defence statement,” he said.

Mpundu likened his position to that of soldiers who accept mortal risk in service of a cause. “Soldiers for example sign up to die. What we’ve not been told is they also sign up to kill. So ready to die, ready to kill is more of a self-defence statement,” he said.

He further apologised, saying he was human and a leader, and insisted the remarks were never meant to suggest wrongdoing. “That statement doesn’t in anyway suggest I am willing to or I am committing a crime. It’s the literal statement that means I am ready to die for what I hold dear and I am ready to push away that which threatens what I hold dear,” he said.

The apology followed sharp criticism from across the political and religious spectrum. UPND Secretary-General Batuke Imenda said no political position was worth the life of a single Zambian, describing elections as a celebration of democracy rather than a contest to be settled through fear.

“Elections are not war or a death sentence for anyone. Elections are a celebration of democracy,” Imenda said, urging Mpundu to retract the statement and calling on political cadres across the divide to uphold peace during the campaign’s closing days.

Information and Media Permanent Secretary Thabo Kawana also condemned the remarks, saying they were careless and risked alarming citizens into believing violence was an acceptable response to an electoral outcome.

“We call on law-enforcement agencies to ensure such people are brought before the law and they are taken care of as prescribed by the law. This is just an election,” Kawana said.

Catholic bishops, in separate homilies delivered in Eastern, Southern and Copperbelt provinces on Sunday, warned that no political office or electoral grievance could ever justify aggression, intimidation or bloodshed, and urged political leaders to condemn violence among their own supporters rather than excuse it.

The UPND also raised concern over an earlier claim attributed to Mpundu, in which he was said to have suggested that NRPUP presidential candidate Brian Mundubile had taken mercenaries outside the country for military training. Imenda described the confession as troubling evidence of interference in the electoral process.

Mpundu, in his own defence, said the backlash had exceeded what he intended and that he took full responsibility for the confusion the video had caused, regardless of how it originated. He said he now understood the seriousness with which such statements are received so close to polling day.

Zambia Police have not issued a public statement on whether the matter will be investigated as a criminal offence. The video’s circulation comes two days before the country goes to the polls in an election already marked by heightened concern over political rhetoric and campaign conduct.

World.title: ECZ insists ballot papers valid without a cross, cites law amid rising dispute
World.content:
The Electoral Commission of Zambia has restated that a ballot paper will not be rejected simply because a voter failed to mark it with a cross, provided the voter’s intention is clear, as a dispute over the timing of that clarification intensifies three days before the national vote.

ECZ Chief Electoral Officer Brown Kasaro said the Commission had noted with concern misleading statements from some stakeholders, including political party leaders, regarding the marking and validity of ballot papers ahead of Thursday’s poll.

Mr Kasaro said Section 60(6)(b) of the Electoral Process Act No. 35 of 2016 requires a voter to mark the ballot paper in a way that indicates the candidate the voter wishes to vote for. “The law does not prescribe a cross as the only mark that may be used,” he stated.

He noted that Regulation 33(d) of the Electoral Process (General) Regulations, 2016 instructs voters to use a cross when marking their ballot, but said this must be read together with Regulation 46(2)(b), which he said provides that a ballot marked otherwise than by a cross shall not, for that reason alone, be invalid, provided the voter’s intention clearly appears on it and the marking does not itself identify the voter.

“Voters are instructed to use a cross, but the absence of a cross does not, by itself, make a ballot invalid,” Mr Kasaro said. “What matters is whether the voter’s intention is clear and the ballot meets the requirements for validity.”

He added that this has been ECZ’s practice since 2006, and is therefore neither a new position nor a new interpretation of the law.

The Commission’s clarification is consistent with the wider structure of the Act. Section 68(2)(d), which governs the rejection of ballots during counting, provides for a ballot to be rejected where it is marked in a manner that makes it impossible to determine the voter’s choice, rather than requiring an “X” as the sole valid mark.

NRPUP presidential candidate Brian Mundubile has not disputed that reading of the law. His party’s concern is one of timing rather than substance, centred on the effect of raising the point so close to a vote after voters have been taught for years, since long before this election, to use the cross as the standard mark.

That concern is that introducing the wider marking allowance this late risks unsettling an electorate accustomed to a single method, and could feed suspicion that the Commission has a hidden motive for doing so now rather than earlier in the campaign.

Lawyers acting for NRPUP, Aongola & Co. Legal Practitioners together with Makebi Zulu Advocates, wrote to ECZ this week citing Regulation 33(d) and giving the Commission a three-hour deadline to clarify whether both a cross and a tick would be accepted at polling stations. The firms said ambiguity over the acceptable marking method could create uncertainty during counting and verification.

Historian Dr Sishuwa Sishuwa has taken a firmer position than the NRPUP leadership, maintaining that a cross remains the only lawful mark and that a tick or any other mark results in a spoilt ballot.

DPP president Antonio Mwanza has backed the Commission’s position, arguing that Section 60 of the Act does not say a voter must use an “X” or that every other mark is automatically invalid. Mr Mwanza said the provision has existed since the 2016 elections and is not a new requirement introduced by ECZ.

Mr Kasaro, addressing a separate stakeholder meeting in Lusaka, said any single, clear mark confined within a candidate’s designated area on the ballot would be treated as valid. “As long as that marking does not cross over to any other candidate, it’s restricted within the particular area for that candidate, it is a valid mark,” he said.

Mr Kasaro urged all stakeholders to provide accurate information to the public and to avoid statements that could unnecessarily confuse voters or undermine confidence in the electoral process during this period.

Polling stations open on Thursday, with the cross remaining ECZ’s recommended standard in ongoing voter education even as the Commission maintains that other clear markings will not automatically void a ballot.

World.title: ECZ engages political party agents, monitors in Masaiti
World.content:
The Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) in Masaiti District has held meetings with political party agents, monitors and polling agents in Kafulafuta, Kalulalango and Masaiti Constituencies.

Speaking during the closing of the meetings, Masaiti Constituency Presiding Officer Lubombela Mulala urged polling agents and monitors to adhere to the Electoral Code of Conduct during and after polling day.

Mr Mulala said all stakeholders have a duty to contribute towards the attainment of free, fair and credible elections.

He said the meetings were aimed at acquainting polling agents and monitors with their roles and responsibilities, as well as encouraging them to remain vigilant and ensure peace is maintained through factual reporting.

Mr Mulala reminded the gathering that ECZ has not changed anything but is merely applying constitutional provisions governing the holding of General Elections.

He further reminded all aspiring candidates that they are required to provide two polling agents at every polling station, although only one agent is allowed inside the polling station at a time.

Mr Mulala also advised all participants in the elections to adhere to the lawful requirement to remove campaign posters and other campaign materials from walls, trees and other places within fourteen days after polling day.

He said it was important for polling agents and monitors to understand their roles and those of other stakeholders who will be visiting and operating from polling stations on polling day.

And one of the polling agents, Mr Zulu, commended ECZ for equipping them with knowledge on the roles and responsibilities of polling agents and monitors.

Mr Zulu said the information had come at an opportune time and would help polling agents conduct themselves professionally and foster peaceful elections.

World.title: Low Stakeholder Accreditation Worries ECZ In Vubwi
World.content:
The Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) has raised concern over the low turnout of stakeholders seeking accreditation to monitor and observe the August 13 general elections in Vubwi district.

Vubwi District Electoral Officer, Moses Mutyoka, said the number of political parties, Independent Candidates and other stakeholders obtaining accreditation remained low as of Saturday, August 8, with most participating political players having accredited only two members of staff.

The accreditation exercise is scheduled to close on Tuesday, August 11, 2026.

Professor Mutyoka urged political parties and other stakeholders to take the accreditation exercise seriously, warning that failure to obtain the necessary accreditation will result in polling agents being denied access to monitor the electoral process on polling day.

“Political parties are supposed to be at the forefront of acquiring accreditation. If you do not do so, your polling agents will not be allowed to monitor the elections. Make sure you do the needful,” he said.

He assured stakeholders that the ECZ was working throughout the accreditation period to ensure that all eligible persons were accredited, but encouraged them not to wait until the last minute.

Professor Mutyoka warned that late applications could result in unnecessary panic and congestion, potentially leaving some stakeholders unable to obtain the required accreditation documents before the deadline.

He further cautioned stakeholders that those who failed to take advantage of the opportunity to comply with the electoral procedures would have themselves to blame, as the Commission had provided adequate information on the requirements and procedures governing the elections.

The District Electoral Officer said the Commission remained committed to ensuring that the electoral process is transparent and credible, stressing that political parties have an important role to play in monitoring the polls.

He described the participation of political parties and other accredited stakeholders in monitoring the electoral process as an important component of a democratic election.

Professor Mutyoka also urged voters to safeguard their National Registration Cards (NRCs) and voters’ cards, which are required for them to cast their ballots.

He cautioned voters against surrendering their documents to other people, saying voters should remain in possession of their NRCs and voters’ cards at all times.

“The election day is fast approaching. Let us all protect and secure our votes by safeguarding and remaining in possession of our NRCs and voters’ cards. Do not allow anyone to mislead you or take possession of your documents. You cannot vote without these two important documents,” he advised.

Vubwi District, a rural district bordering Malawi and Mozambique, has 33,230 registered voters and 43 polling stations spread across all nine wards.

The district has so far recorded no cases of electoral violence, a development that is contributing to expectations of a peaceful, free and fair election.

World.title: Zalomius cautions against unverified information
World.content:
The Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) has cautioned civil society organisations, faith-based organisations, the media and, local and international election observers against sharing unverified information on social media, ahead of the August 13, 2026 general elections.

ECZ Chairperson Mwangala Zaloumis says stakeholders have an important role to play in promoting responsible access to information and maintaining public confidence in the electoral process.

ZANIS reports that Ms Zaloumis says stakeholders should rely on verified and authoritative information and seek clarification from the Commission through appropriate channels whenever concerns arise.

The ECZ Chairperson was speaking in Lusaka today when she updated and addressed local and international election observers and other stakeholders on the preparedness of the Commission to handle the polls.

She added that information gathered during election monitoring should be handled responsibly, accurately and within the appropriate context.

Ms Zaloumis has also urged stakeholders to distinguish between verified observations, allegations and speculation, and ensure that their reports and assessments are evidence-based, objective and fair.

The Chairperson stressed that the ECZ remains committed to conducting elections that are free, fair, transparent and credible, guided by the principles of impartiality, professionalism, accountability, transparency and inclusiveness.

Ms Zalomius said with only a few days remaining until polling day, all stakeholders have a responsibility to contribute to a peaceful, transparent and credible electoral process.

She has since urged stakeholders to ensure that Zambians are able to exercise their democratic right to vote peacefully and confidently on August 13, 2026.

Meanwhile, ECZ Voter Education Manager Emmah Mwiinga disclosed that 8,786,300 voters are registered on its register, urging them to effectively participate in this year’s polls.

In her presentation, the Voter Education Manager further said the Commission will dispatch 81,000 poll staff in the 13, 539 polling stations dotted across the country.

On the delimitation exercise, Ms Mwiinga said the Commission increased the number of constituencies from 156 to 226 following constitutional reforms necessitated by the Constitution Amendment Act Number 13 of 2025, which led to the delimitation of constituencies.

World.title: CROP commends govt on pension reforms, urges peaceful elections
World.content:
The Consortium for the Rights and Welfare of Older Persons (CROP) has called for a peaceful political environment ahead of the August 13 general elections.

Speaking during an interview with the media today, CROP Team Leader Geoffrey Chiesu says that with only a few days before the polls, political players should ensure peace is maintained.

Mr Chiyesu explained that older persons, just like children are vulnerable people in violent contexts, therefore calling on political players to exercise restraint and promote a culture of peace that safeguards the dignity and security of all Zambians

And Mr Chiyesu noted that the consortium was happy with the United Party for National Development (UPND) government for upholding democratic governance and maintaining a generally peaceful political environment.

He said the Consortium commends the government for transformative pension reforms and improved social protection for senior citizens.

Mr Chiyesu therefore encouraged senior citizens to exercise their democratic rights responsibly.

“We urge older persons to make informed choices that safeguard the progress already achieved in social protection and pension reforms by the UPND government, so that we protect the gains that have so far been achieved,” he said.

Mr Chiyesu also expressed appreciation for amendments to the three pension acts covering the National Pension Scheme Authority (NAPSA), the Public Service Pension Fund (PSF), and the Local Authorities Superannuation Fund (LASF)

He said the measures represent a transformative step forward expected to significantly improve income security for retirees, prospective retirees and senior citizens across Zambia.

Mr Chiyesu however, recommended that government, if given another mandate, should prioritise strengthening the Social Cash Transfer programme to ensure its sustainability, particularly by meeting the minimum threshold of $2 per day.

He also called for the clearing of all outstanding retirement benefits owed to employees, including leave days and other accruals that benefit people in retirement.

“The future of these reforms and the security they provide depend on continued commitment to policies that prioritise the welfare of Zambia’s ageing population.

“Under the UPND government led by President Hakainde Hichilema, we believe that social protection and pension reforms are assured and guaranteed,” Mr Chiyesu added.

CROP comprises six like minded organisations namely the Retirees Welfare Bureau of Zambia, Community Support for the Needy, Support to Older People in Zambia (TOP Zambia), Development for Aged People in Zambia, and the Social Welfare Association of Zambia.

World.title: Lusaka District accredits 4,285 election observers and monitors
World.content:
Lusaka District has so far accredited about 4,285 election observers and monitors ahead of Thursday’s general elections.

Lusaka District Assistant Electoral Officer Victor Kagoli said the figure was recorded by Saturday and represented observers and monitors issued with accreditation cards across the district’s 10 constituencies.

Speaking in an interview with the media, Mr Kagoli said Lusaka has 1,246 polling stations, with at least three observers and monitors expected to cover each polling station.

Mr Kagoli said the number of people seeking accreditation has continued to rise as the accreditation exercise approaches its conclusion.

He noted that the district initially started the accreditation exercise with 10 kits but has since received additional 10 kits from the Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) to respond to the increasing demand.

Mr Kagoli added that the district was currently operating with 16 kits and expected to have all the kits in use as the number of applicants continued to increase.

“Stakeholder engagement in the electoral process has also been quite high, with political parties showing keen interest in the preparations for the elections,” he said.

Mr Kagoli further revealed that the district had already conducted a briefing for poll agents representing all political parties, while police officers are scheduled to be briefed tomorrow.

He said the high level of stakeholder participation was a positive indication of citizens’ interest in ensuring a transparent electoral process.

Meanwhile, Mr Kagoli noted that 40 pallets of ballot papers had already been delivered to the facility and would tomorrow be inspected by stakeholders before being distributed to the respective constituencies.

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - August 11, 2026
World.content:
Zambia Election Set for Closely Fought Opposition Battle

Zambia's 13 August election has become a closely contested battle between the ruling United Party for National Development and the Tonse-Pamodzi opposition alliance, led by newcomer Brian Mundubile and backed by former Patriotic Front structures. The election is expected to test the opposition's strength and serve as a referendum on President Hakainde Hichilema's record. The government has made progress on debt restructuring, economic growth and inflation. But the high cost of living remains a big concern for voters. The poll is also taking place amid concerns over alleged state interference, restrictions on opposition activity and controversial legislative changes, making it a key test for Zambia's democracy.

WHO Warns DR Congo Ebola Response Falling Behind

More than 1,900 people have died in the Democratic Republic of Congo's Ebola outbreak. 60-70% of deaths occur in communities before patients reach treatment centres. The WHO said that the concentration of healthcare services in Bunia, Ituri province, is forcing patients to travel long distances and seek care too late. Poor transport systems may also increase transmission. The agency plans to expand treatment facilities closer to communities, add 400 Ebola beds and strengthen public awareness and early referrals. WHO is also looking to the town of Aru, where no new cases have been reported for two weeks after authorities expanded surveillance and response beyond individual patients to surrounding communities.



Nigeria Lassa Fever Cases Reach 1,000 in 2026

Nigeria has reported 1,000 confirmed cases of Lassa fever and 237 deaths in 2026, with cases reported in 23 states and 116 local government areas. Five states, Ondo, Bauchi, Taraba, Edo and Benue, account for 86% of confirmed cases. At least 53 healthcare workers have also been infected, prompting the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention to introduce a 30-day protection plan for frontline staff. The agency has said that late presentation, high treatment costs, poor sanitation and limited awareness are contributing to the outbreak and high fatality rate. Lassa fever is a viral haemorrhagic disease transmitted primarily through contact with food or household items contaminated by the urine or faeces of infected rodents.

Malawi Land Audit Flags Irregular Plot Allocations

Malawi's Ministry of Lands is set to release findings from a pilot land ownership audit in Lilongwe that reportedly uncovered irregularities in the allocation of plots in the affluent Area 3 and Area 10. The audit was launched in February 2026 to improve transparency and accountability in land administration. It is said to have identified politically exposed individuals, including current and former ministers, judges and MPs, among those allegedly linked to irregular land acquisitions. The findings could trigger political controversy, with questions remaining over whether those implicated will be publicly named or face legal or disciplinary action.

UN Somalia Auction Raises Security Concerns

The UN Support Office in Somalia (UNSOS) has opened a tender to auction vehicles, generators, IT equipment, medical supplies, construction machinery and other assets. This comes as Washington moves to end funding for the mission's logistical support by the end of 2026. UNSOS provides critical transport, fuel, food and other supplies to about 12,000 African troops and police serving under AUSSOM in the fight against al-Shabab. The auction has raised concerns among civil society groups over transparency and oversight. Regional leaders have warned that any premature reduction in international support could create a security vacuum as al-Shabab continues to operate in parts of Somalia.

Close 

Climate Change Shifts Africa's Malaria Risk

Climate change is reshaping malaria risk across Africa, with rising temperatures making parts of southern Africa and high-elevation areas of East Africa increasingly suitable for transmission, according to a new Nature study. Some parts of West and Central Africa may have become too hot for optimal malaria transmission. The region still bears about 95% of the global malaria burden. But experts warn that climate change is only part of the equation, with funding gaps, drug and insecticide resistance, and weak health systems still major threats. They are urging countries in emerging risk areas to step up malaria prevention and surveillance while maintaining elimination efforts in high-burden areas.

World.title: South Africa: Gauteng Gets 500,000 Grade 1 and 8 Applications - South African News Briefs - August 11, 2026
World.content:
Gauteng Records Nearly 500,000 Grade 1 and 8 Applications

Almost half a million applications have been submitted for Grade 1 and Grade 8 places in Gauteng for the 2027 academic year since the online application system opened, reports EWN. The Gauteng Department of Education has said that improvements have been made to streamline the process. Education MEC Lebogang Maile has urged parents to apply early. The department also says learners awaiting specialised placement should receive interim support rather than remain on waiting lists, with officials focusing on successful placements and resolving outstanding cases.

Strong Winds Damage Homes in Free State

The South African Red Cross Society is assessing damage caused by strong winds and heavy rainfall in Koppies and other parts of the Free State, reports SABC News. Several homes have reportedly been damaged, including roofs blown off, as severe weather persists. Red Cross volunteers are working with disaster management authorities and municipalities. Assessments continue, with humanitarian assistance being provided to affected households.

Fadiel Adams Unlikely to Testify at Madlanga Commission

National Coloured Congress leader Fadiel Adams is unlikely to testify before the Madlanga Commission, reports EWN. This comes after the commission received his affidavit and supporting documents late. Adams was expected to testify about his involvement in an Investigating Directorate Against Corruption probe into alleged corruption within Crime Intelligence. In 2024, he asked IDAC to investigate claims that the Political Killings Task Team had misused secret service funds for luxury accommodation and vehicles.
