World.title: One year after Putin-Trump summit, ‘spirit of Anchorage’ dissipated
World.content:
Moscow – In the year since Donald Trump hosted Vladimir Putin on US soil for a summit designed to broker an end to Russia’s offensive on Ukraine, the diplomatic initiative has fizzled out and the conflict has escalated.

For months, Russian officials talked up the “spirit of Anchorage” — a supposed climate of detente, renewed dialogue with Washington and a framework for finding a way out of the deadliest European conflict since World War II.

Now there are few traces of that atmosphere. US mediation efforts are at a standstill, both Russia and Ukraine are ramping up attacks and more civilians are being killed than at any point since the first months of the war.

– ‘Ending the war’-

On August 15, 2025, Trump broke with the West’s policy of isolating Putin, rolling out the red carpet as the Kremlin chief stepped off his plane at the Elmendorf-Richardson air base in Alaska.

It remains unclear what was decided or discussed behind closed doors.

Russia has always maintained some kind of understanding on a peace deal was struck — “a compromise proposal”, as Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov called it.

Washington has rebuffed any talk of a deal being reached.

“There was a proposal in Alaska, but there was no agreement. If there had been an agreement, we would have had an end of the war,” Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in June.

Moscow had hoped the summit would lay the foundations for a “lasting peace” by addressing what it calls the “root causes” of the conflict, said political analyst Sergei Markov — designated a “foreign agent” but still close to the Russian authorities.

For years — including right before launching its offensive in February 2022 — Russia has called for a new overarching security deal with the United States over Europe, NATO and arms control.

The “compromise” Russia tabled in Alaska, Markov told AFP, was to limit its territorial claims on Ukraine to the eastern Donbas region in exchange for recognition of Russia’s new borders by Washington and the lifting of sanctions.

– Disenchantment –

Those Russian demands were included in a 28-point document drafted by the United States — later cut down to 19 — after separate negotiations with Kyiv and Moscow.

The document was never published officially and never came to fruition.

US-brokered direct talks between Russia and Ukraine in early 2026 broke down, chiefly over the issue of territory.

Ukraine refuses to cede land it still controls and wants an immediate ceasefire along the current front line, with territorial status to be decided during fuller peace talks.

And since late February, Washington’s attention has been consumed by the war on Iran.

Trump has since issued fresh sanctions on Russia and the last remaining nuclear arms control agreement — New Start — has been allowed to lapse.

Having once sensed a window of opportunity to press its demands and been at pains to praise Trump’s efforts, Russia has lately allowed itself to publicly question Washington’s commitment to diplomacy.

“I don’t even want to imagine that Alaska … was conceived to gain time in order to strengthen Ukraine militarily,” Lavrov said in June.

A meeting between Lavrov and Rubio in Manila in July — their first since September 2025 — lasted only around 30 minutes.

“We’ll have to find new suggestions and new ideas” that both “Russia and Ukraine can agree to,” Rubio said after that meeting.

“That’s going to require a lot of work,” he added.

– Escalation –

The two sides’ conditions for peace are irreconcilable.

Russia demands territory alongside political and military concessions that Ukraine rejects as capitulation.

At the same time, both are convinced force can improve their negotiating position.

“The Russian armed forces will continue their mission to liberate the Donbas and Novorossiya in line with the approved plan,” Russia’s army chief Valery Gerasimov told Putin in a televised meeting in early July — referring to land stretching across eastern and southern Ukraine.

Buoyed by European support, Kyiv is banking on its long-range strike campaign to tip Russia’s economy and society over the edge.

Its attacks triggered a nationwide fuel crisis over the summer, and have forced Moscow-installed authorities to put the annexed Crimean peninsula under a local “state of emergency”.

Russia has upped its missile attacks on Kyiv, killing dozens there in recent weeks.

It has also brought Ukrainian exports through the Black Sea to a standstill through a campaign of port and ship strikes.

“The spirit of Anchorage has dissipated,” said Russian political analyst Fyodor Lukyanov — close to the ruling elite — in August.

The result? “Brutal escalation.”

World.title: AI’s hunger for power sparks US private gas plant boom
World.content:
Washington – As US tech companies race to build the data centers fueling the AI boom, they are increasingly putting up their own power plants — off the grid and running on gas — to get online faster.

Analysis by the research firm Cleanview, shared with AFP, identified around 60 data centers planned for the coming years with a combined 97 gigawatts of “behind-the-meter” generation into the early 2030s — around the total installed capacity of Mexico.

The climate implications could be enormous.

The precise figure depends on how many are built, how efficient the turbines are and how often they run, but even with very conservative assumptions, the plants would easily top 200 million tons of carbon dioxide emissions a year.

That’s equal to annual emissions of more than 46 million gasoline-powered cars.

The latest addition to the tally — a 7.5 GW plant in Texas powering Amazon data centers — shows how analysts often have to piece together clues to link projects to hyperscalers.

The plant got air pollution permits in January, Amazon received construction permits last week, and satellite imagery confirmed clearing had begun at the site named in the plant’s air permit records. Cleanview then confirmed the link with Amazon directly.

– Poor efficiency –

Alongside greenhouse gases, gas plants emit fine particulate matter, linked to a range of heart and lung problems; nitrogen oxides, which aggravate respiratory disease; and hazardous air pollutants including mercury, formaldehyde and benzene.

“Powering data centers with behind-the-meter generation that relies heavily on dirty gas or diesel turbines is a surefire way to needlessly pump a variety of hazardous pollutants into local communities’ air while worsening climate change,” John Rogers, associate director of energy analytics at the Union of Concerned Scientists, told AFP.

“These dirty plants, which are also subject to less public accountability, are unacceptable when record heat and fires are showing us that we need to change course,” said Yuqi Zhu, a senior policy analyst at Natural Resources Defense Council.

The practice began as an oddity, exemplified by Elon Musk’s decision to truck in mobile gas turbines to an xAI data center in Memphis in 2024. xAI still accounts for most of the two gigawatts online today.

But Cleanview’s analysis finds nearly every hyperscaler is pursuing such projects, including Meta, Microsoft and Oracle. AI labs including OpenAI and Anthropic have signed leases for more than 10 gigawatts of behind-the-meter power.

Instead of the equipment utilities normally buy, they have turned to more exotic and more polluting options, including trailer-mounted generators, turbines originally designed for aircraft and warships, piston engines of the kind commonly found in vehicles, and refurbished turbines from industrial operations.

– Test case –

Development tilts toward Republican-leaning states, with Texas far in the lead at more than 40 gigawatts announced.

The NAACP civil rights group has filed suit against xAI, accusing it of unlawfully operating turbines in Mississippi to power its Memphis data center.

“We are concerned that if this case is decided against us, data centers across the country will be emboldened to go forward,” Laura Thoms, enforcement director at Earthjustice, which is co-representing the NAACP, told AFP.

President Donald Trump’s administration has created a voluntary “Ratepayer Protection Pledge,” under which signatories promise not to pass data center costs on to residential consumers, something Thoms fears will only accelerate the problem.

Gas was already enjoying a renaissance before Trump returned to office, according to data compiled by Atlas Public Policy.

After years of decline, new announced fossil fuel capacity for the grid hit a low in 2022, rebounding the following year as the AI boom took hold.

“In the first half of 2026 alone, we’re already seeing that the announced new (fossil) capacity is higher than it’s been in the last 10 years, so that’s a pretty significant sign,” said Rachel Reolfi, a senior policy analyst at the group.

World.title: Iraq unveils dual pipeline plan to Faysh Khabur and Baniyas via Chevron
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The Iraqi Ministry of Oil announced on Monday, August 10, 2026, plans to construct a major new pipeline network featuring two strategic export routes toward Faysh Khabur and the Syrian port of Baniyas. The infrastructure push aims to diversify Iraq’s crude oil export outlets beyond its primary southern Gulf terminals.

Deputy Oil Minister for Extraction Affairs, Nseer Aziz, chaired an executive planning meeting to establish implementation frameworks for the multi-billion-dollar project. Discussions centered on finalizing investment mechanics under a Build-Own-Operate-Transfer (BOOT) model with a consortium of global energy firms including UCC, TI Capital, and Chevron.

Key Infrastructure & Project Details

Dual Export Corridors: Route 1:Basra – Haditha – Faysh Khabur (connecting southern oilfields to northern export infrastructure near the Turkish border). Route 2:Haditha – Baniyas (reactivating the strategic Mediterranean export route across Syria).

Investment Model: To be executed under a BOOT (Build-Own-Operate-Transfer) framework in partnership with international consortium partners Chevron, UCC, and TI Capital.

Inter-Agency Coordination: Attended by leadership from Basra Oil Company (BOC), North Oil Company (NOC), Missan Oil Company (MOC), state oil marketer SOMO, and the Ministry’s Studies and Planning Directorate.

Syrian Transit Agreement: Follows a U.S.-sponsored Memorandum of Understanding signed between Iraq and Syria on July 17, 2026, to reactivate the historic Kirkuk–Baniyas pipeline corridor.

The dual-pipeline initiative marks a decisive effort by Baghdad to reduce its reliance on southern Gulf ports following severe disruptions caused by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

By linking Basra’s southern production hubs directly to northern transit corridors at Faysh Khabur and Mediterranean terminals at Baniyas, Iraq aims to secure uninterrupted crude flows to global markets, lower war-risk freight costs, and enhance long-term energy marketing flexibility.

World.title: Iraq Stock Exchange trades surge 55% in July as ISX60 Index gains 2.1%
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The Iraq Stock Exchange (ISX) recorded a sharp acceleration in trading volume during July 2026, with total shares traded jumping 54.9% month-on-month despite broader regional economic headwinds.

Official exchange data shows that 166.66 billion shares changed hands across 21 trading sessions, generating an aggregate turnover of 120.03 billion Iraqi Dinars ($91.6 million)—a 1.2% increase compared to June figures.

Key market performance metrics

Trading Volume: 166.66 billion shares traded, marking a 54.9% surge from June.

Trading Value: 120.03 billion IQD (~$91.6M), up 1.2% month-on-month.

Transaction Count: 24,342 executed deals, declining 8.3% month-on-month.

Corporate Participation: 85 out of 125 listed joint-stock companies actively traded during the month.

Index Movements: ISX60 Main Index: Closed at 1,041.07 points, gaining 2.1% from June’s close of 1,019.39 points. ISX15 Benchmark: Closed at 1,267.67 points, edging down 0.48% from 1,273.79 points.



The ISX operates under the oversight of the Iraq Securities Commission (ISC), facilitating electronic trading for 125 listed companies through 38 licensed brokerage firms.

Banking and financial institution equities continued to dominate overall trading volume and liquidity during July, offsetting softer performance across industrial and hospitality counters as retail and institutional investors repositioned portfolios heading into the second half of the year.

World.title: Iraqi Airways resumes direct Basra to Delhi flights
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Airways announced on Monday, August 10, 2026, that it will resume direct commercial flights between Basra International Airport and Indira Gandhi International Airport in New Delhi starting August 18. The route will operate once weekly on Tuesdays.

The direct service had been suspended since early March due to regional security escalations. According to an official statement from the state-owned carrier, flight operations are being reactivated following regional de-escalation and rising passenger travel demand between Iraq and India.

Key Operational Details

Route: Basra (BSR) to New Delhi (DEL) direct service.

Flight Frequency: Weekly service operating every Tuesday, beginning August 18, 2026.

Background: Suspended in early March 2026 due to regional airspace and security disruptions.

Network Expansion: Iraqi Airways has launched or resumed more than 10 regional and international flight routes over the past two months.

The resumption of the Basra–Delhi line reflects a broader push by Iraqi Airways to expand its international flight network and restore routes linking major Iraqi cities with key international destinations.

India remains a major destination for Iraqi travelers seeking medical care, commercial partnerships, and higher education, making the direct link between Iraq’s southern economic hub and Delhi a key commercial route for the national carrier.

World.title: 'Speak impeccable Tamil' vs 'I have my own style': Grammar jibes set off row in Tamil Nadu assembly
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A row over Tamil Nadu finance ministerâs language and pronunciation skills during his budget speech triggered a political row in the state assembly on Monday, with the opposition members criticising his use of English and "grammatical errors".

The controversy began when MDMK MLA T M Rajendran, who won from Kadayanallur assembly constituency on the DMKâs Rising Sun symbol, pointed out "gramatical errors" in TVK minister N Marie Wilsonâs August 5 budget speech.

'Several grammatical errors'

Rajendran said Wilson had skipped several Tamil sentences and used English extensively during the speech. âAs a Tamil enthusiast, I observed in his (Marie Wilsonâs) speech that he had skipped many of the Tamil sentences.

There were several grammatical errors too,ââ Rajendran said.

âAtleast in the future, when he gets the opportunity the finance minister should speak in impeccable Tamil,â he added.

Rajendran also asked school education minister A Rajmohan to help Wilson improve his Tamil. Rajmohan, however defended the finance minister, saying there was nothing wrong with his speech. He also pointed out that leader of opposition

spoke in a plain and simple language.





'I would speak in my own style'

The remarks drew an angry response from Wilson, who defended his communication style and said his focus was on governance and the stateâs development rather than linguistic formalities.

âThe government under chief minister C Joseph Vijay has made significant achievements in the past 60-75 days, successfully bringing Rs 15,000 crores into the treasury through various reforms,â Wilson said, without elaborating.

Wilson said he had worked in the education sector for 25 to 30 years and had primarily communicated in English during his professional career.

âEarlier they were body shaming other and were insulting others based on caste and gender. Now they are insulting us over language,â Marie Wilson said.

The minister said he felt that members were targeting his communication style and background instead of focusing on his work.

He said he could not change the way he spoke simply to satisfy others.

Citing the Bible, Wilson said that while he might not be well-versed in Tamil, Christianity had taught him several languages, including the âlove language, peace language and the language of kindnessâ.

He added that he could not change his pronunciation for others and said âI would speak in my own style and that I could not change it to suit others.â

Speaker J C D Prabhakar intervened and advised Wilson to sit down and avoid getting angry.

'Tamil and English both allowed'

DMK senior leader and former minister E V Velu sought to defuse the issue, pointing out that Tamil has several dialects across the state, including differences between north and south Chennai.

Velu also stressed that Tamil Nadu followed a dual-language policy of Tamil and English.

The Speaker also noted that Rajendran himself had used the English word âbudgetâ in his speech instead of its Tamil equivalent.

Prabhakar urged members to treat the matter lightly and avoid turning language into a source of conflict in the House. He said the Assembly was a forum where multiple languages were permitted under its rules and members should focus on policy discussions rather than personal remarks.

The Speaker cited an earlier instance when then chief minister J Jayalalithaa allowed a Congress member to speak in Telugu in the Assembly.

He also pointed out that former finance minister P Thiaga Rajan had used English during earlier budget sessions.

Prabhakar said Assembly Rule 86 allows members to conduct proceedings in Tamil or English, or in both languages. He stressed that the focus should be on the intent and substance of what is being said rather than the language used.

World.title: 'Life begins at conception': Tamil Nadu Speaker sparks row over anti-abortion remarks
World.content:
Tamil Nadu Assembly Speaker JCD Prabhakar attended the 5th National March for Life as the chief guest on August 8 and 9.

During the gathering, which protested abortion rights and advocated for the protection of unborn life, he reportedly said that âlife begins at conception," as cited by PTI.

The event, hosted by the Archdiocese of Madras-Mylapore at Stella Maris College, drew more than 5,000 participants. The gathering also explicitly criticised the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act.

Prabhakarâs remarks echoed global anti-abortion sentiments expressed at the event, which focused on opposing abortion rights and advocating for the protection of unborn life.

The remarks prompted state Health Minister K G Arunraj to clarify on Monday that abortions can be a medical necessity and are strictly regulated under national law.

Responding to reporters during a press conference to announce the MBBS/BDS rank list for 2026-27, the Health Minister sought to address the controversy, saying he was unaware of the context in which the Speaker made the remarks and urging the public not to misinterpret them.

World.title: Jharkhand protest: BJP bandh, ED probe, arrests deepen recruitment exam row - top developments
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Normal life was affected in parts of Jharkhand on Tuesday as the

enforced a statewide bandh over police action against job aspirants during their march to the state assembly, while an Enforcement Directorate probe and the arrest of a former JPSC chairperson added a new dimension to the recruitment exam controversy.

Most schools and business establishments remained closed, while vehicular movement was thin in Ranchi and several other cities. The bandh, announced from 8 am to midnight, was called by the BJP to protest the use of water cannons, tear gas and batons against students during Monday's assembly march. Essential services were kept outside its purview.

BJP calls bandh over police action

BJP state president Aditya Sahu described the police action as "atrocities" against students and accused the JMM-led government of using force instead of addressing their grievances.

The party has backed demands for an independent probe into alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations conducted by the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC).

The Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad has also condemned the alleged police action and announced a 'Vidhan Sabha March' from the old assembly building to the new assembly premises.

The bandh followed a tense day in Ranchi when thousands of aspirants breached multiple barricades while marching towards the assembly, where the monsoon session was underway.





Police used water cannons and tear gas near Jagannathpur Temple before resorting to a lathi-charge after protesters crossed the final barricade and reached Gate No 1.

Students allege brutal crackdown

Student leaders alleged that the protest was peaceful until police action began in the evening. Ravinder Pasawan said students from all 24 districts had gathered and waited until 5 pm for the government to respond to their demands.

"But suddenly, force was used. Some of our companions were injured.

The administration did its job; before that, they were quite cooperative, but in the evening, they lost their cool. Many of our colleagues, including women students, were injured. It was also seen that media personnel were pushed and shoved. We remain firm on our demands. We appeal to the Honourable Chief Minister that we are all students; please accept our demands, as they are all logical.

Our indefinite protest will continue until the Jharkhand government accepts them," Pasawan said.

Another student leader, Piyush, claimed nearly 50,000 aspirants had participated in what he described as a "historic" march. He said the students remained independent of political parties and would continue their indefinite protest.

Police, however, said 14 personnel were injured during the protests and that CCTV footage would be examined to identify those involved in stone pelting and disruption.

ED launches money laundering probe

The controversy escalated further on Monday after the Enforcement Directorate launched a money laundering investigation into alleged irregularities in multiple recruitment examinations, particularly the JSSC-CGL examination.

The Jharkhand CID also arrested former JPSC chairperson L Khiangte in connection with the alleged irregularities. His arrest took the number of people apprehended in the case to 20.

Khiangte, a 1988-batch IAS officer and former Jharkhand chief secretary, was appointed JPSC chairperson in February last year and resigned on July 22. The CID had earlier searched 18 locations across Ranchi, Palamu, Hazaribagh, Bokaro and Dhanbad.

The state government has agreed to cancel the 14th JPSC examination and backlog examinations conducted in 2023 and 2025. Higher and Technical Education Minister Sudivya Kumar said the government had also agreed to the ED probe after evidence of financial irregularities emerged.

Students demand CBI investigation

The protesters have been agitating since July 25, demanding cancellation of the JSSC-CGL examination, a CBI probe into alleged irregularities and comprehensive reforms in the JPSC and JSSC.

They have also sought cancellation of several recruitment examinations, including the 14th Jharkhand PSC Civil Services Examination, and an independent investigation either by the CBI or a panel of retired high court judges from outside Jharkhand.

On the JSSC-CGL examination, Kumar said the state government could not order its cancellation because it was conducted under court monitoring. The government has proposed a committee headed by a retired high court judge to oversee the CID investigation, but protesters have rejected the proposal.

The government has also proposed reforms to the standard operating procedures of the JPSC and JSSC, with inputs from IIT-ISM Dhanbad, IIM-Ranchi and XLRI Jamshedpur.

Hunger strike leader's health worsens

JLKM leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who has been on hunger strike for nine days over the issue, was admitted to Ranchi Sadar Hospital after his blood sugar level dropped "drastically". Doctors described his condition as critical.

Mahto joined Monday's march in an ambulance and later addressed protesters while lying on a stretcher.

His supporters alleged that he was injured during the police action.

Earlier, Mahto had said, "Attempts were made to stop us. Barricades of barbed wire were erected. Water cannons were used. Tear gas was deployed. Lathi charges were carried out, leaving people injured. Yet, we did not raise a single slogan against the government. We did not engage in any political rhetoric or utter a single obscene word. The only flag present was the Tricolour."

He also questioned the credibility of any investigation, saying, "Exams are conducted with candidates sitting in places like Nepal. What faith can one have in the investigation?"

Soren seeks dialogue amid political row

Chief minister Hemant Soren urged students to resolve their grievances through "dialogue and trust", while saying their demands would be examined with "utmost seriousness and sensitivity".

Soren also accused opposition leaders of attempting to mislead students for political gains and said the government wanted to make the examination system more transparent, technology-enabled, secure and accountable.

Congress leader Rahul Gandhi condemned the police action, saying peaceful protests should not be met with violence.

"Students have a right to peaceful protest, and only dialogue can yield solutions," the Congress leader said, urging the Jharkhand government to resolve their grievances at the earliest.

His remarks drew a response from the BJP, which accused Gandhi of double standards because the Congress is part of the JMM-led ruling coalition in Jharkhand.

World.title: 'Images disturb me deeply': Congress's Sam Pitroda questions 'use of force' against Jharkhand students

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Sam Pitroda on Monday backed protesting students in Jharkhand as an agitation over alleged irregularities in JPSC and JSSC recruitment examinations intensified in Ranchi. Criticising the governmentâs use of lathis, tear gas and water cannons, Pitroda called for âreform, accountability and compassionâ as the protests entered their 18th day.The development comes as the Jharkhand studentsâ 'Vidhan Sabha gherao' march in Ranchi on Monday saw police use lathis and water cannons to disperse protesters. The march was organised over alleged irregularities in examinations conducted by the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC).The protesters are demanding, among other measures, the cancellation of the JSSC-Combined Graduate Level (CGL) examination, a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into alleged irregularities and reforms in the recruitment process.In a series of posts on X, the Indian Overseas Congress (IOC) global chairman said the grievances of young people should be addressed through dialogue."The images from Ranchi disturb me deeplyâ, he wrote.Pitroda said students should not be met with force, calling them India's future and expressing solidarity with Jharkhand's youth.In another post, Pitroda said, "Democracy requires governments to create space for peaceful dissent, dialogue and resolution."Pitroda's remarks came after Congress leader Rahul Gandhi also condemned the police action and called for dialogue with the protesting students, urging the Jharkhand government to address their grievances. The Hemant Soren-led Jharkhand government is run by a JMM-led coalition in which the Congress is a partner.Pitroda also said the protesting youth deserved to be heard respectfully and urged authorities to address their concerns over fair examinations, transparent recruitment, employment opportunities and their prospects for the future."These are not unreasonable demands. India owes its youth a system they can trustâ, he added in the postHe further said the concerns of students needed to be viewed in the context of the sacrifices made by their families."Behind every protesting student is a family that has sacrificed - often for years for education and the hope of a job.Pitroda criticised the JMM-led Jharkhand government over the handling of recruitment and examination-related grievances, saying delays in recruitment and failures in examinations risk eroding young people's trust in the system. He called for "reform, accountability and compassion" in addressing their concerns.Calling India's youth its "greatest assets", Pitroda said the country's demographic dividend could turn into frustration if education does not translate into opportunities and examinations fail to inspire confidence."We must redesign education, assessment and employment systems for this generation â not punish them for demanding change," he said.On Monday, police and protesters clashed during the march outside the Jharkhand Assembly. Police resorted to at least three rounds of lathicharge, while tear gas shells and water cannons were also used to disperse demonstrators.Injured protester alleged that police began the lathicharge without warning.The police have, however, given a different account of the events. Ranchi deputy commissioner Manjunath Bhajantri said a stone was thrown at a police jawan and alleged that some "anti-social elements" attempted to provoke police and officials during the protest.Addressing a press conference, Bhajantri said the police had exercised restraint throughout the demonstration and used "mild force" only after a situation arose in which a jawan's life was allegedly at risk.Ranchi City SP Paras Rana said most students were peaceful but alleged that a section of protesters damaged barricades and pelted stones.The protest also affected Jharkhand Loktantrik Krantikari Morcha (JLKM) leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who was admitted to Sadar Hospital in Ranchi after taking part in the march.Mahto had been on hunger strike for nine days at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium before joining the 'Vidhan Sabha Gherao' march despite his deteriorating health. He was later admitted to hospital.The police action drew criticism from political leaders across party lines. On Monday, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi also condemned the police action and called for dialogue with the protesting students."The use of force against students protesting in Jharkhand is wrong. Students have a right to peaceful protest, and only dialogue can yield solutions," Rahul Gandhi said in a post on X, on Monday.He further urged the Jharkhand government to address the students' grievances."The Jharkhand government must continue to hear these students out and resolve their issues immediately," he added.The JPSC and JSSC examinations have been at the centre of protests by aspirants over alleged irregularities. Separately, the Enforcement Directorate (ED) has registered an Enforcement Case Information Report under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act in connection with alleged irregularities in JPSC examinations.

World.title: 'New Parliament,  PM house, why not new govt schools in villages?' CJP's Dipke announces nationwide campaign
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke has announced a nationwide campaign to improve government schools in villages, seeking to address the "neglect of rural educational infrastructure".

The campaign will be launched on August 15, with the CJP calling on citizens, parents and village leaders to work together to improve basic facilities in government schools.

Dipke said he would launch the initiative from his village in Hingoli, Maharashtra, by approaching the village head and requesting him to take steps to improve government schools there.

âThe coming 15th August is our 80th Independence Day. But, if anything has been neglected or ignored the most in the last 80 years, it is the government schools in our villages,â Dipke said on Monday.

âWe have made a new Parliament, a new PM house. Why have we not been able to build new schools in our villages? Do we not consider the children of farmers and labourers the future of our country?â he asked.

Dipke said children in villages continue to face difficulties in accessing schools and basic facilities such as drinking water and toilets.

âEven today, village children have to walk a long distance to go to school. After going there, they donât find water or toilet facilities,â he said, highlighting the difficulties faced by girls in particular.





âI feel that on this 15th August, if we should pay attention to anything, if we should make a new start, we should start by improving our government schools,â he said.

The âSarpanch Challengeâ

As part of the campaign, the CJP has appealed to sarpanches across the country to take up the task of improving government schools in their respective villages.

Dipke said he would personally approach the village head in Hingoli and urged other sarpanches to do the same in their villages.

The organisation has termed the initiative the âSarpanch Challengeâ, under which it plans to publicly recognise village heads who improve their schools by sharing before-and-after photographs on its social media platforms and giving credit to the sarpanches concerned.

âWe will give you credit so that after seeing you, after seeing the schools that you have improved, many other village heads also start improving schools in their villages," Dipke said.

The CJP has also called for a citizen-led social audit of government schools.

Parents whose children study in government schools have been asked to visit the institutions and check basic facilities, including electricity, clean drinking water, functional washrooms and mid-day meals.

âYou go to your children's schools and see if basic facilities are available. See if there is electricity, waterâ¦ Do your children get washroom facilities? Do they get mid-day meals?â Dipke said.

He urged parents to record videos if basic facilities were unavailable. The CJP said it would soon issue a printable audit form through which citizens could record the facilities available at their children's schools and those that were missing.

The form will be shared through links on campaign videos on the CJP's official social media platforms and completed forms and video evidence can be emailed to the organisation.

The campaign aims to ensure that children of farmers and wage labourers studying in village schools have access to facilities comparable to those available to children in cities.

âIf not, you make videos of it. Because your children's schooling should be good. That is your fundamental right," Dipke said.

âLet us all make a promise to the children who live in villages that we will improve their schools. Together, we can do this,â he said, concluding his video with the message, âReal India lives in villagesâ.

CJP backs Jharkhand protests

In a separate video, Dipke also extended his support to Jharkhand student leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who was hospitalised after his health deteriorated during a hunger strike over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations.

Calling the alleged police action against protesters âcruel and inhumanâ, Dipke drew a parallel with student protests at Delhi's Jantar Mantar. âBe it Jantar Mantar or Jharkhand, such police brutality against students is cruel and inhuman,â he said.

âCJP stands firmly with Devendra bhai and his struggle. He is a true hero. We salute his courage and strength!â he added.

Mahto has been at the centre of the ongoing JPSC-JSSC agitation in Ranchi over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations. He had been on an indefinite hunger strike and joined the students' Vidhan Sabha gherao march on Monday, arriving at the protest in an ambulance as his health deteriorated.

World.title: Govt condemns vandalism of Indian embassy in Slovenia
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Condemning the defacement of Indian embassy premises in Slovenia by Khalistan separatists, the govt urged law enforcement authorities elsewhere too to take note of the hateful propaganda and disinformation being spread by such groups.

Ministry of external affairs said in an official statement that under the Vienna Convention, diplomatic premises are inviolable and must be protected.

"We have taken up the matter strongly with Slovenian authorities, both in New Delhi and in Ljubljana so that the perpetrators behind such reprehensible acts are held accountable to the full extent of the law," it said.

"We also call upon law enforcement authorities elsewhere to take note of the hateful propaganda and disinformation being spread by such groups," it added.

In recent years, Indian diplomatic missions have been targeted, vandalised, or defaced with pro-Khalistan slogans and flags in many other countries, including Australia, Canada, UK and the US.

World.content:

GUWAHATI: China has hit back sharply at India for assigning standard names to 27 geographical locations in Arunachal Pradesh, with the state-run Global Times claiming these areas are in China's 'Zangnan' region - Beijing's term for Arunachal Pradesh and adjoining areas that it claims as part of Tibet Autonomous part.The daily reiterated that Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said at a routine press briefing on April 14 that the Zangnan region is China's territory and "China does not recognise the so-called 'Arunachal Pradesh' illegally set up by India. It is fully within China's sovereign rights for the Chinese govt to issue standard names for some of the places in Zangnan."The reaction came three days after India's Survey of India updated its official map to identify 21 land areas, four passes, a high-altitude glacial lake and a 1962 war hero monument in Arunachal Pradesh, which govt said was an exercise to ensure the "correct identification" of places and enhance public awareness of their geographical and historical significance.Global Times reported on Sunday night that the mapping by India came shortly after the 36th meeting of the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination on China-India Border Affairs (WMCC), held on Aug 6 in New Delhi, where officials from both sides discussed issues including boundary delimitation, border management and control, mechanism building and cross-border cooperation."India's latest move is essentially an attempt to reinforce its claims over disputed territory and counter China's sovereignty position," Guo Xuetang, a professor at Shanghai International Studies University, said.The latest "war of names" adds another layer to an already complex border dispute, even as both sides seek to keep military and diplomatic channels open.

World.title: Kerala seeks extension of AICTE deadline for engineering admissions
World.content:
The Higher Education department in Kerala is learnt to have requested the Union Ministry of Education to extend the deadline for the engineering admissions process in the State, against the backdrop of concerns raised by a section of aspirants about seats remaining vacant in government engineering colleges and objections to the ongoing decentralised spot admissions process to fill them.

August 14 is the deadline set by the All-India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) to end the engineering admissions process across the country. Some other States have also requested the Centre to extend the admission deadline, citing issues such as examination irregularities, floods and reported deficiencies in the Central Board of Secondary Education’s evaluation process.

Sources in the office of Roji M. John, Higher Education Minister, told The Hindu on Tuesday (August 11, 2026) that if the deadline is extended, more rounds of allotment could be held to ensure that no seats remain vacant in government engineering colleges.

This year, the Commissioner for Entrance Examinations conducted three rounds of allotment for B.Tech admissions. However, a section of students, who do not wish to be quoted, say there were no significant changes in the first two allotments. One of the major reasons for this was that the KEAM allotment process was conducted simultaneously with national-level admission processes such as those of the Joint Seat Allocation Authority and the Central Seat Allocation Board.

As a result, many students reportedly did not see any meaningful change in their preferred options in the initial allotments. Although there were some changes in the third allotment, only limited opportunities were available to the students. A parent from Kozhikode points out that conducting a fourth round of allotment would have been reasonable. It could have helped those who would have become eligible for seats that fell vacant due to withdrawals and changes following national-level counselling processes. However, it was not done, he says.

In the past 10 years, a centralised spot admissions (CAP) process used to be held at the Government Engineering College, Thrissur, to fill vacant seats. This ensured that almost all seats in government engineering colleges were filled. This year, however, the government engineering colleges in the State were allowed to conduct separate sessions. The spot admissions were held at the College of Engineering, Thiruvananthapuram, on August 11. The process is scheduled to be held at seven other colleges on August 13 and August 14.

The parents say that students may get to understand details about seat vacancies only after attending the process at a particular college. Even if seats remain vacant in other colleges, they may not be able to join there. Many students who have already secured admission in self-financing colleges by paying higher fees may not get an opportunity to shift to government engineering colleges. The AICTE’s deadline could further restrict the opportunity for students who fail to secure medical admissions as well, they say.

SFI opposes decentralised spot admissions

Meanwhile, functionaries of the Students’ Federation of India (SFI) claim that the decentralised process will only help self-financing engineering colleges. The schedule for the process was also announced in a hurry. Students from poor families will not be able to claim the vacant seats in government colleges.

They also claim that self-financing college managements were not providing no-objection certificates to their students to join the process.

World.title: Jharkhand students' protests LIVE: ABVP workers detained during march to Assembly over police action

On Monday (August 10, 2026), police used lathis and water cannons to control the crowd during a “Vidhan Sabha gherao” march by JPSC and JSSC aspirants in Ranchi. The protesters had gathered to press their demands over alleged irregularities in examinations and recruitment. The students have alleged that their demands have not been fully accepted by the State government.

World.title: Kanwar Yatra 2026: Traffic restrictions in Delhi, U.P., and Haryana
World.content:
Kanwar Yatra, or the annual pilgrimage of people from the Ganges River to their local temples, is underway and will conclude on Tuesday (August 11, 2026).

The festive pilgrimage began on July 30 and will conclude on August 11, 2026 on the day of Shivratri.

U.P. CM Yogi showers flowers on Kanwariyas, describes Kanwar Yatra as unparalleled example of devotion, unity

Owing to the heavy pedestrian and pilgrimage traffic, specific advisories have been issued by authorities to ease commute of citizens, especially in Uttar Pradesh, Delhi, and Haryana.

Here’s your guide to what’s open and what’s closed.

Region/State Affected areas and restrictions Duration of restrictions Recommended Alternate Routes Delhi • Kalindi Kunj junction, Okhla Barrage road, Noida–Kalindi Kunj road, and Okhla Bird Sanctuary • GT Road (Apsara Border to Yamuna Bridge) closed for general traffic August 11–12, 2026 • Avoid Kalindi Kunj, GT Road, and Wazirabad Road. • Use designated alternate corridors like NH-9 and NH-44. Gurugram (Haryana) • Heavy vehicle movement entering Delhi via Haridwar return paths • Travel corridors toward Rajasthan, Jhajjar, Rewari, Pataudi, Nuh, and Faridabad August 9 – 11, 2026 • Use Dwarka Expressway. • Use KMP Expressway via Panchgaon Chowk. Ghaziabad (Uttar Pradesh) • Delhi-Meerut Expressway (DME) • Heavy pilgrim traffic on NH-58 / Delhi-Meerut route August 9 – 12, 2026 •Use NH-09 as primary alternative route • Siddharth Vihar to Meerut Tiraha: Take NH-09, Vijayanagar Cut, Overbridge, and Chaudhary Mod.

Delhi

The Delhi Traffic Police, in a post on X on August 10, 2026, said that “traffic congestion is likely on Kalindi Kunj junction, Okhla Barrage road, Noida, Kalindi Kunj-Noida road and the connecting roads towards Okhla Bird Sanctuary.” It especially warned commuters not to use the routes leading through Kalindi Kunj junction, to plan commutes in advance and to allow sufficient additional travel time.

Delhi CM assures kanwariyas will not face any difficulties

TRAFFIC ADVISORY



Traffic movement in and around Kalindi Kunj Junction is likely to remain slow and congested till 12.08.2026 due to heavy movement of Kanwariyas during the ongoing Kanwar Yatra and ongoing road repair work on the Okhla Barrage–Kalindi Kunj stretch.



📍ADVISORY… pic.twitter.com/dzqYI092mO — Delhi Traffic Police (@dtptraffic) August 9, 2026

Gurugram, Haryana

Gurugram traffic police, on August 8, detailed alternate routes for heavy vehicles to take to enter the national capital of Delhi owing to the ‘Kanwar Yatra’ pilgrimage and the return of the ‘kanwariyas’ from Haridwar.

School van vandalised in Lucknow allegedly by Kanwariyas

It asked commuters to “use Dwarka and KMP expressway via Panchgaon Chowk” as travel corridors to Rajasthan, Jhajjar, Rewari, Pataudi, Nuh, and Faridabad may also be affected.

This advisory is in effect till August 11, 2026 and the traffic police also attached maps for easy referencing for citizens.

Heavy Vehicle Advisory (9–11 Aug)

Kanwariyas return from Haridwar for jalabhishek on Mahashivratri, 11 Aug.

· Use Dwarka & KMP Expressway via Panchgaon Chowk

· For Rajasthan, Jhajjar, Rewari, Pataudi, Nuh, Faridabad

📞 112 | 1095#TrafficAdvisory#KMPExpressway#RoadSafetypic.twitter.com/QNABiSDIuF — Gurugram Traffic Police (@TrafficGGM) August 8, 2026

Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh

Ghaziabad in Uttar Pradesh is also under a traffic advisory by the traffic police. An X post, with a video by Varun Kumar Singh, Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police (Traffic), said that “For the safe movement of Kanwar devotees, the Delhi-Meerut Expressway (DME) will be restricted for general traffic on August 10 and 11, 2026.” It added that: In view of the large number of Kanwar pilgrims on NH-58/Delhi-Meerut route, use Rapid Metro (RRTS) and public transport instead of private vehicles, and use NH-09 as much as possible.

Traffic curbs for Kanwar Yatra in U.P.’s Muzaffarnagar till August 12

Vehicles coming from Siddharth Vihar to Meerut Tiraha should use NH-09, Vijayanagar Cut, Overbridge, and Chaudhary Mod.”

It advised locals to use NH-09 instead for commuting.

What is Kanwar Yatra?

Kanwar Yatra is an annual pilgrimage where devotees of Lord Shiva collect holy water from the Ganges River from places like Haridawar, Gangotri, Gaumukh, or Sultanganj and take it to their local temples, often walking barefoot for long distances.

It occurs during July-August, depending on the Hindu calendar month of ‘Shravan.’

World.title: Unorganised sector workers stage 'jail bharo' protest in Jalna; 80 detained
World.content:
Workers from the unorganised sector, led by the Centre of Indian Trade Unions (CITU), have staged a ‘jail bharo’ agitation in Maharashtra's Jalna city, demanding permanent employee status, PF and pension benefits for unorganised workers.

A large number of CITU activists, agricultural labourers and workers' organisation members staged the protest at the Jalna Zilla Parishad office on Monday (August 10, 2026).

As many as 80 protesters were detained and later let off, a police official said.

CITU leader Anna Sawant said the protest was held as part of a nationwide call by the joint action committee of Central Trade Unions and the Samyukta Kisan Morcha to oppose what they claimed were anti-worker and anti-farmer policies of the central and State governments.

Farmers, agricultural labourers and various unorganised sector workers, including women, participated in the agitation. They raised slogans against rising inflation and unemployment, contractualisation of jobs, and the reduction of social security benefits.

The protesters demanded permanent employee status, along with ESI, PF and pension benefits, for anganwadi workers and helpers, ASHA workers, group facilitators, school mid-day meal workers, gram rozgar sevaks and employees working under the National Health Mission and other government schemes.

They also demanded restoration of the MGNREGA system, 200 days of employment per family and a daily wage of Rs 700. The protesters sought distribution of agricultural land to landless families and regularisation of gairan land (common land set apart by the administration for the free grazing of cattle) already in their possession.

"We demand the immediate repeal of the four labour codes, as they would adversely affect workers' legal rights, job security, wages and social security," Mr. Sawant said.

A memorandum addressed to the Prime Minister was submitted by the protesters to the Zilla Parishad Chief Executive Officer Dr Krishna Kant Kanwaria.

The police detained 80 protesters and later let them off, an official from Kadim Jalna police station said.

World.title: U.S. firm Blackbaud plans second Hyderabad office, eyes 1,000 headcount
World.content:
U.S. software solutions provider Blackbaud — whose focus is on the non-profit sector and had in November, 2025, formally opened its India office in Hyderabad — plans to expand its footprint in the city with a second office in the Financial District.

“We’re now about 700 people at HITEC City and set to launch our new site in the Financial District soon. Over the next 12-18 months, between the two sites, we expect to have a headcount of 1,000 people, if not more, driving a lot of our global work out of India,” said Rajiv Gajria, vice president and managing director of Blackbaud India.

While the immediate focus is on strengthening its India capabilities, the company would also like to evaluate the country as a potential market for its products. “There is a lot of opportunity here. But for now, the focus is on building capabilities in India,” he said in an interaction recently.

Blackbaud narrowed down on Hyderabad for its India centre. “India is not an outpost for execution or just an offshore services setup. We are a full stack capability centre. Teams [here] are engaged in product development and management, product roadmap planning, customer operations, professional services and customer support,” said Mr. Gajria.

Besides product and customer facing operations, the Hyderabad facility provides supporting functions around enterprise IT, marketing and finance. The headcount it is likely to be around 800 by year end.

While the majority of Blackbaud’s customers are in North America, it has an established business in Western Europe with a growing presence in Australia. The firm is hopeful of tapping India with many of its U.S. customers having a presence in the country. Blackbaud software helps the nonprofit sector entities digitize and scale to reach, establish and sustain relationships with the donors.

On Artificial Intelligence and its impact, he said Blackbaud has become an AI first company and seeing growing demand for AI products and solutions from the social impact sector. It is in this backdrop, the firm intends to expand AI capabilities across the product stack. On the hiring in Hyderabad, he said while lateral hiring remains the focus, the company recently recruited the first batch of fresh graduates.

World.title: Trump secretly flew out of Turkiye after NATO summit because of Iran threat: report
World.content:
U.S. President Donald Trump secretly flew out of last month's NATO summit in Ankara, Turkiye, on an alternate military aircraft while the White House made it appear that the Republican president was flying on Air Force One, according to a report published by The Washington Post on Monday (August 10, 2026).

The Post said an Iranian assassination threat against Mr. Trump prompted the operation. The ruse was carried out as journalists and some White House staff members were led to believe they were on the same plane as the President as he began his journey back to Washington from the annual gathering of NATO country leaders.

The Post cited material reviewed by the newspaper, a U.S. official familiar with the operation and another person with knowledge of the president’s travel. The Associated Press has not independently confirmed the report.

Mr. Trump had flown to the summit in a new Qatari-gifted and retrofitted red, white and navy blue jet. But ahead of departing Turkiye, he said he would fly partway home on an older-model baby blue Air Force One plane instead.

The President at the time said the new luxury jet was being flown out ahead of his departure from Ankara to give some U.S. troops based in eastern England a chance to check out the new Air Force One.

In Ankara, Mr. Trump boarded the old Air Force One jumbo jet in view of television cameras ahead of the plane flying to Royal Air Force Mildenhall in the United Kingdom.

However, according to the Post report, after boarding the legacy Air Force One jet, he was secretly shuttled minutes later to a smaller plane — an Air Force C-32A — via an airport catering truck typically used to load meals and other supplies. Trump flew to Mildenhall on that smaller jet.

Also read: West Asia war LIVE updates

The White House did not respond directly to questions about the Post report of the secret operation to whisk Mr. Trump out of the country on a third aircraft, or the reported elaborate ruse to make it appear he was on the baby blue Air Force One jet flying to Mildenhall.

“As the President has said recently, there are many enemies of America who have their sights on him, and we use every tool at our disposal to address those threats,” White House communications director Steven Cheung said in a statement.

The U.S. Secret Service declined to comment. The Air Force, which maintains the fleet of executive travel aircraft, referred questions to the White House.

While Mr. Trump was in Turkiye, the U.S. military conducted a series of large strikes in Iran in retaliation for its attacks on merchant shipping in the region.

The New York Times and CBS News reported last month that intelligence officials had raised concerns about a potential attack on the president or his jet, triggering additional precautions and the decision not to use the newly inaugurated aircraft gifted to Trump by Qatar for the first leg of Mr. Trump’s trip home from Ankara.

The swap had spurred questions about the security of the Qatar-provided aircraft, and Mr. Trump said last month after the trip that it would undergo additional upgrades.

Mr. Cheung on Monday maintained that the new, Qatari-gifted plane was “a state-of-the-art aircraft that has been fitted with high-level security protocols that ensure the safety of the President and his staff.”

The new Post report on clandestinely putting Mr. Trump on a third aircraft and quietly whisking him out of the country adds a fresh layer to just how seriously concerned U.S. security officials were about the threat against Mr. Trump during the ongoing war with Iran.

Paul Eckloff, a former special agent with the Secret Service, said such an unusual move could either reflect actionable intelligence or an abundance of caution given volatility in the region with the wars in Iran and Ukraine.

“I would not say unprecedented, but it is an unusual occurrence,” Mr. Eckloff told The Associated Press.

The Post reported that to exit that plane without being seen by those uninvolved in the operation, Mr. Trump and several aides stepped aboard an airport catering truck, which was elevated planeside using hydraulics and positioned at a door on the opposite side of Air Force One’s entrance.

The small group of reporters who thought they were travelling with Mr. Trump were advised to lower their window shades ahead of takeoff.

After arriving at Mildenhall, news photographers captured images of Mr. Trump getting off the presidential plane — suggesting he reboarded Air Force One out of sight of the pack of journalists who thought they were traveling with him.

Democratic Sen. Richard Blumenthal called for a congressional investigation.

“It is unprecedented and it is surreal,” he said Monday on CNN, calling the incident “downright scary.”

After the brief visit to the base at Mildenhall, Mr. Trump boarded the new Air Force One aircraft to fly the rest of the way to Washington.

During a gaggle with reporters aboard the aircraft, Mr. Trump was asked directly if there was any credible threats on Air Force One by Iran.

“Well, I have a threat all the time. I’m number one on their list before you,” Mr. Trump said. He added to the traveling reporters, “But if I go, you go.”

World.title: Tamil Nadu Assembly adopts resolution seeking abolition of NEET for undergraduate medical courses
World.content:
The Tamil Nadu Assembly on Tuesday (August 11, 2026) unanimously adopted a resolution urging the Union government to do away with the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (NEET) for admission to undergraduate medical courses, citing repeated irregularities in the conduct of the examination, proliferation of coaching centres, and loss of lives. The lone BJP MLA M. Bhojarajan opposed the resolution and staged a walkout before the voting.

Tamil Nadu Assembly had adopted resolutions seeking exemption from NEET in the past too. Earlier, in 2021, when the DMK was in power, the Assembly passed the Tamil Nadu Admission to Undergraduate Medical Degree Courses Bill (L.A. Bill No. 43 of 2021), seeking to exempt the State from NEET. However, the Bill was reserved for the consideration of the President, and presidential assent has been withheld.

Moving the resolution, Health, Medical Education and Family Welfare Minister K.G. Arunraj urged the Union government to make necessary amendments to the National Medical Commission Act, 2019 (Central Act No. 33 of 2019), the National Commission for Indian System of Medicine Act, 2020 (Central Act No. 14 of 2020), the National Commission for Homoeopathy Act, 2020 (Central Act No. 15 of 2020), and other relevant Central enactments.

“This will enable admission to medical courses in the State on the basis of marks obtained in the Class XII examination,” the resolution said.

The resolution said the Tamil Nadu government had consistently maintained that NEET was against social justice and equality and infringed upon the rights of the States in matters relating to medical education. It said the examination had seriously undermined the opportunities available to rural and socio-economically disadvantaged students, including those whose medium of instruction was Tamil.

NEET had also led to the proliferation of coaching centres charging exorbitant fees and diverted students’ attention from the school curriculum towards NEET-oriented coaching, it said.

“A single day’s test, rather than twelve years of school education, now determines the course of a student’s higher education,” the resolution said.

It further pointed to repeated question-paper leakages and other irregularities in the conduct of NEET, culminating in the cancellation of NEET-UG 2026 and the subsequent re-examination. These developments had caused “untold mental agony” to lakhs of students and had even resulted in the tragic loss of young lives, it said.

“The examination has forfeited the trust of the students of this country. NEET should, therefore, be abolished,” the resolution said.

Demand to move education to State List

Mr. Arunraj said the permanent solution to the NEET issue was to shift education from the Concurrent List to the State List.

“I take pride and am happy to introduce this Bill as a doctor who secured admission to medical college through the direct admission system and subsequently served as a doctor in a Primary Health Centre (PHC) for five-and-a-half years,” he said.

Mr. Bhojarajan said NEET would encourage students and create a future. In Palladam, 10 Tamil-medium students cleared NEET. “Why can’t the government run coaching centres? Tamil Nadu students are intelligent. They should be given quality education and coaching,” he said.

World.title: Man allegedly kills woman, turns critical himself as families oppose marriage in Rajamahendravaram
World.content:
A 21-year-old woman, Varada Prasanna, was allegedly killed by Kusuma Abhilash, 21, near the Fourth Bridge in Rajamahendravaram city on Monday (August 10, 2026) night. Abhilash then allegedly attempted to end his own life, in what the police described as an attempt by the two to die together.

The incident came to light after National Highway authorities alerted the city police to the presence of the two and a two-wheeler on the roadside at around 11.30 p.m.

According to a release issued by East Godavari Superintendent of Police D. Narasimha Kishore on Tuesday, Ms. Prasanna died of knife injuries. Abhilash was found unconscious and is critical in a private hospital.

The two had reportedly arrived at the spot on a two-wheeler at around 8.30 p.m. Based on preliminary information provided by Abhilash, the police said the two decided to end their lives after their parents rejected their marriage proposal, citing community.

The Three Town police have registered a case and the investigation is on. The body has been sent to the Government General Hospital for post-mortem.

Those in distress or having suicidal thoughts can call the East Godavari police helpline at 70757-49825, or Tele-MANAS at 14416.

World.title: President Zardari approves additional judges' appointments to high courts, ending weeks-long deadlock
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: President Asif Ali Zardari on Tuesday gave his assent to the appointment of 19 additional judges for five high courts, along with confirmation of another five as permanent judges, ending a weeks-long deadlock between the Presidency and the government over the judicial appointments.

“The president has approved the appointment of additional judges in the Lahore High Court (LHC), Sindh High Court (SHC), Peshawar High Court (PHC), Islamabad High Court (IHC), and Balochistan High Court (BHC),” the Presidency said in a statement.

It added that he had also given his assent to the confirmation of certain additional judges of SHC and LHC as permanent judges.

The president gave his assent to the summary forwarded by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, which was based on the recommendations of the Judicial Commission of Pakistan (JCP), official sources confirmed on Tuesday.

The appointments of 19 additional judges and confirmations of five judges were pending since July 20 and July 21, when the JCP — the body responsible for appointing judges to the superior judiciary — recommended them.

The oath-taking ceremony for the judges had been scheduled for July 27 but was indefinitely postponed after President Zardari neither accorded assent to the summary nor returned it for reconsideration, with the government maintaining there was no legal justification for keeping it pending.

The president’s legal team had raised certain objections to the JCP proceedings, noting that nearly all nominees proposed by the PPP were rejected. They had also conveyed that some candidates recommended for appointment had criminal records.

The delay prompted the federal government to even consider bypassing the president’s approval by invoking Article 48(1) of the Constitution, arguing that he was required to act on the summary within a fortnight of its submission, sources said.

However, government functionaries later maintained that with the matter now sub judice, notifications could not be issued at this stage. Sources had said the government’s legal team planned to pursue an “out-of-court” settlement with its counterparts at the Presidency.

The approvals follow a positive meeting between the legal teams of the Presidency and the federal government, with sources privy to the development describing the matter as “on its way to resolution”. Another meeting between the two legal teams was expected to be held in the coming days.

The delay had created practical complications for the high courts. Four additional judges of the PHC whose confirmation had been recommended by the JCP ceased to hold office after their tenure expired on August 4 in the absence of formal notifications.

Similarly, an additional judge of the SHC, whose term had been extended for six months, relinquished office after his tenure expired on July 29.

The judges

The JCP had recommended five additional judges to be made permanent, a six-month extension for an additional judge of the SHC, and the appointment of 19 additional judges to the Lahore, Islamabad, Sindh and Balochistan high courts.

For SHC, the JCP recommended the appointment of Advocate Muhammad Humayon Khan, District and Sessions Judge Suresh Kumar, and Advocate Dr Shah Nawaz Memon as additional judges.

It also recommended a six-month extension in the term of Justice Khalid Hussain Shahani as an additional judge of the SHC.

For IHC, the JCP recommended the appointment of three nominees as additional judges, namely Advocate Ayyaz Shaukat, District and Sessions Judge Shahrukh Arjumand, and Advocate Umair Majeed Malik.

For LHC, the commission recommended the appointment of 10 nominees as additional judges of the LHC by a majority.

They included advocates Amir Ajam Malik, Asad Ali Bajwa, Barrister Muhammad Usman Ghani Rashid Cheema, Ghulam Sarwar Nihang, Khalid Ibn-i-Aziz, Muhammad Ajmal Khan Zahid, Muhammad Amjad Pervaiz, Munawar Iqbal Duggal, Shiren Imran and Syed Farhad Ali.

For BHC, the JCP recommended the appointment of district and sessions judges Allah Dad Roshan and Abdul Qayyum Lehri, as well as Advocate Muhammad Rauf Atta.

Among those recommended as permanent judges were four additional judges of the PHC — Justices Farah Jamshed, Inaamullah Khan, Sabitullah Khan, and Aurangzeb — along with Additional Judge Justice Tariq Mahmood Bajwa of the LHC.

IHC requested to keep matter pending

The matter had also been sub judice before the IHC, where a plea challenging the delay in notifying the judicial appointments was filed last week.

On Tuesday, Justice Arbab Muhammad Tahir heard the petition, which was filed by advocate Luqman Zafar Chaudhary through his counsel Zahid Asif Chaudhry.

The IHC adjourned the proceedings after the counsel requested the court to keep the matter pending until the law ministry issues a formal notification.

On Monday, the IHC had issued notices to President Zardari, the federation and the attorney general and directed them to submit separate concise reports explaining the timeline and present status of the summary forwarded by PM Shehbaz concerning the judicial appointments.

The petitioner’s counsel had argued that Article 48(1) of the Constitution uses the expression “shall”, imposing a constitutional obligation on the president to act on the advice tendered by the prime minister.

The proviso to Article 48(1) permits the president to return the advice for reconsideration within 15 days, after which the president is required to act within 10 days on the advice tendered after reconsideration.

For its part, the Presidency’s legal team had contended that Article 175-A did not prescribe a specific timeframe for the president’s action and that the provision could not be overridden by Article 48(1) to bypass the Presidency.

They had also referred to Article 48(2), which empowered the president “to act in his discretion in respect of any matter in respect of which he is empowered by the Constitution to do so” and states that the validity of anything done by the president shall not be called into question on any ground whatsoever.

On the other hand, government sources had maintained that judicial appointments were governed by constitutional provisions and that any deadlock must be resolved strictly in accordance with the Constitution.

Other approvals

Apart from giving his nod to the judges’ appointments and confirmations, President Zardari also approved the equalisation of the salaries, allowances, and pensions of Supreme Court judges with those of judges of the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC).

Moreover, he approved amendments to the 1997 order relating to the leave, pensions, and privileges of high court judges, the Presidency said.

He also gave his assent to the appointment of Haroon Akhtar as advisor to the prime minister on industries and production.

The Ministry of Law and Justice also approved the appointments of all the judges and issued notifications to this effect.

World.title: NCCIA summons 4 individuals on Sharjeel Memon's complaint in connection with Mir Raza's case
World.content:
KARACHI: The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) has summoned four Karachi residents on a complaint filed by Sindh Senior Minister Sharjeel Inam Memon over “false and malicious content on social media against him and his son” in connection with the Mir Raza Ali murder case.

The NCCIA’s notices, dated August 10 and seen by Dawn, stated that the agency was “conducting an inquiry into the subject matter concerning allegations of defamation through electronic/digital means, which was initiated on the basis of a complaint submitted by Naqvi Law Associates on behalf of Sharjeel Inam Memon, son of Inamul Haque Memon”.

“The complaint pertains to the alleged dissemination of defamatory and fabricated content through digital platforms, which […] has caused damage to his reputation and has attracted provisions of applicable cybercrime laws,” the notices said.

All four individuals have been directed to appear in person at the NCCIA Karachi office on Aug 13 at 11:30am.

The notices said the respondents were required to bring their original CNICs, relevant evidence and documents in their defence, record their statements and submit their digital devices.

The NCCIA warned that failure to comply would compel the agency to initiate legal proceedings before the competent court of law.

The development comes a day after Memon, through his counsel, approached the NCCIA against unidentified persons for allegedly “causing harassment” and creating false and malicious content on social media against him and his son.

Memon rejected allegations that he owned the guest house in Gulistan-i-Jauhar where Mir Raza Ali was allegedly tortured and murdered, and that his son had left for London immediately after the incident and had since been moving around with a bodyguard.

He said the allegations had “no factual or evidentiary basis” and were intended to malign him and his son for “extraneous political motives”.

His counsel asked the NCCIA to register an FIR and proceed against those found responsible under the applicable provisions of the Prevention of Electronic Crime Act, 2016, and any other relevant law.

An IBA graduate and owner of the eatery Wafflix, Ali had gone missing on July 28, and his body was found a day later with a gunshot wound in bushes near Shahi Qila Ground in Karachi’s Gulistan-i-Jauhar.

While investigators initially focused their probe on the possibility of suicide, Ali’s family has been saying that he was kidnapped, tortured and murdered. Later, a second postmortem following a controversy over his first autopsy revealed that he was shot in the back, ruling out the possibility of suicide.

The counsel for Ali’s family, Jibran Nasir, had demanded that the team probing the case be changed and accused the authorities of trying to “bury the facts”.

On Sunday, a new team was assigned the case, and a murder charge was also added to the first information.

World.title: World Bank unhappy over fund diversion from Balochistan
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Expressing serious displeasure over reputational challenges, the World Bank has warned that redirecting funds from a multi-billion-rupee resilient housing programme for the flood-affected population to infrastructure projects would further aggravate poverty in Balochistan.

“Based on the socio-economic profile of the eligible household, the risk is not simply that households remain without housing assistance; rather, it is that existing vulnerabilities become mutually reinforcing and deepen over time,” the World Bank said in detailed communication to the federal and Balochistan governments.

In this case, 84 per cent of eligible beneficiaries are ultra-poor and vulnerable, with 28pc earning less than $30 and another 26pc earning between $31 and $70 per month, while 39pc are tenants, 37pc are daily-wage labourers and 8pc are small farmers. These groups typically have limited savings, weak access to formal credit, few productive assets and low capacity to absorb shocks, WB said.

After meetings with the federal minister for planning, the chief minister of Balochistan and others following the capping of housing support at 62,966 first-tranche beneficiaries as of June 22, 2026, and subsidy support to 97,000, World Bank’s country director Boloromaa Amgaabazar expressed concern over the decision as well as the handling of issues pertaining to fraud and corruption.

Cautions exclusion could deepen poverty, disaster risks, social tensions

She wrote to the federal secretaries for economic affairs and planning, as well as the secretary of Balochistan, that the capping and redirection of housing support was leaving 119,049 verified and eligible households without identified financing support. Its public disclosure before the finalisation of a jointly agreed communication strategy with the bank had also created risks, as households that had completed verification and signed the project undertakings might continue to expect housing assistance.

She wrote that 66,120 exclusion-related grievances had been registered in the project grievance management system on or before the agreed cut-off date. Therefore, each complainant should be contacted individually and formally notified of the decision.

“Written acknowledgment, or other verifiable evidence confirming delivery and receipt of the communication, should be obtained and shared with the bank for review. A credible and transparent grievance resolution process is essential to mitigating legal, operational, and reputational risks associated with eventual closure of the component,” Ms Amgaabazar wrote.

With the capping of housing support, eligible but excluded households may face a compounding cycle of vulnerability that not only reinforces poverty but increases it, raises disaster risk and undermines long-term recovery and resilience, diminishing the objectives with which the project was initiated.

With limited resources, families may be forced to divert income from essential needs such as food, healthcare and education towards continued temporary shelter repairs, while also resorting to debt or the sale of productive assets to cope.

At the same time, families unable to rebuild resilient homes may remain in damaged or unsafe structures, leaving them more exposed to recurring floods, storms, earthquakes and heatwaves.

On top of that, the exclusion of verified eligible beneficiaries may also generate grievances, perceptions of inequity and unfairness, and continued erosion of trust in government institutions and development programmes, risks that have been observed in other housing reconstruction operations.

Published in Dawn, August 11th, 2026

World.title: 'Not an ordinary year': Pakistani students receive their CIE AS & A Level results for June series
World.content:
Students of Cambridge International Education’s (CIE) AS and A Level across Pakistan on Tuesday began receiving their results for the June 2026 exam series.

The CIE, part of Cambridge University Press and Assessment, offers internationally recognised exams to schools in 160-plus countries. In Pakistan, O Levels (grades 9–10) cover a broad subject range, while A and AS Levels (grades 11–12) are more specialised and advanced, providing pathways to higher education in Pakistan and abroad.

Over 100,000 students from over 850 schools across Pakistan sat for the June 2026 exam series for Cambridge International AS & A Level, Cambridge O Level and IGCSE this year, noted a CIE press release issued on Tuesday.

The most popular subjects in the country were Physics, Mathematics, Business, Chemistry and Computer Science.

This year’s June series was marred by the leak of its AS/A Level Mathematics Paper 12 taken on April 29, which the CIE subsequently cancelled and scheduled a re-take for June 9.

Uzma Yousuf, country director for International Education at Cambridge, congratulated the learners who were receiving their exam results.

“This has not been an ordinary year. Some students prepared for their examinations against a backdrop of regional tensions, uncertainty and disruption, which makes today’s achievement even more meaningful,” the press release quoted her as saying.

“I hope every learner takes a moment to celebrate what they’ve accomplished,” Yousuf said, thanking teachers, parents and school communities across Pakistan who supported students.

“At Cambridge, we believe education is about more than examination results. It’s about helping young people build the knowledge, confidence and skills to thrive at university, in their careers, and in life,” she added.

Yousuf said CIE looked forward to continuing innovation in assessments, such as its digital exams pilot this year and modular assessment options at A Level, for better inclusivity and flexibility for students.

Rod Smith, group managing director for International Education at Cambridge, also congratulated the students. He noted: “More students are turning to our AS & A Levels because they combine deep subject knowledge with the skills universities and employers value most.”

Smith observed that this year’s “continued growth shows just how clearly that combination resonates in a world being reshaped by AI”, expressing confidence that AS & A Levels will become increasingly important in the years ahead for this reason.

CIE exams are typically held twice a year, in June and November, with results released in August and January, respectively. This year, June series papers were held from April 23 to June 9.

More to follow

World.title: Bahrain FM congratulates Dar on Makkah defence pact, expresses desire to visit Pakistan
World.content:
In a phone call with Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Bahrain’s Foreign Minister Dr Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani congratulated Pakistan on the signing of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, the Foreign Office (FO) said on Tuesday.

The joint defence agreement, signed on August 7 between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empowers its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.
